children.title: Two-Stage Stochastic Mixed-Integer Programs
children.top_down_role: Here-and-now decisions coupled to scenario-dependent recourse.

knowledge_statements.title: Two-Stage Stochastic Mixed-Integer Programs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-scenario, risk-neutral two-stage formulation with nonanticipative first-stage decisions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(S\) be a finite scenario set with probabilities \(p_s>0\) satisfying \(\sum_{s\in S}p_s=1\). A two-stage stochastic mixed-integer program has the form
\[\min_{x\in X}\left\{c^\top x+\sum_{s\in S}p_s Q_s(x)\right\},\qquad Q_s(x):=\min_{y_s\in Y_s}\{q_s^\top y_s:W_s y_s=h_s-T_sx\}.\]
The here-and-now vector \(x\) is common to every scenario, whereas \(y_s\) is selected after scenario \(s\) is observed. The feasible sets \(X\) and \(Y_s\) may contain continuous and integer-constrained components, and at least one component of \(x\) or of some \(y_s\) is integer-constrained. Each recourse value is feasible and finite on the admitted first-stage domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A common first-stage decision is chosen before uncertainty, followed by scenario-specific recourse decisions minimizing expected total cost; at least one decision component in the two-stage model is integer-constrained.
assumptions_latex: \(S\) is finite and \(p_s>0\) with \(\sum_{s\in S}p_s=1\).
\(X\) and each \(Y_s\) are feasible sets with designated continuous or integer-constrained components, and at least one designated component in the model is integer-constrained.
\(Q_s(x)\) is feasible and finite for every admitted \(x\) and \(s\in S\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed finite-scenario formulation represents \(\min_{x\in X}\{c^\top x+\mathbb E[Q_\xi(x)]\}\) with one nonanticipative first-stage vector \(x\) and scenario-dependent recourse vectors \(y_s\).

children.title: Multistage Stochastic Mixed-Integer Programs
children.top_down_role: Discrete decisions distributed across a sequential information structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Multistage Stochastic Mixed-Integer Programs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-horizon scenario-tree formulation with stagewise nonanticipativity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathcal N\) be the nodes of a finite rooted scenario tree with root \(r\), unconditional node probabilities \(p_n\), stage map \(t(n)\), and parent map \(a(n)\) for \(n\ne r\). For each node, let \(c_n\), \(A_n\), \(B_n\), and \(b_n\) be dimensionally compatible deterministic-equivalent data, and let \(X_n\subseteq\mathbb R^{d_n-k_n}\times\mathbb Z^{k_n}\), where \(0\le k_n\le d_n\) and \(k_n\ge1\) for at least one node. A multistage stochastic mixed-integer program has the scenario-tree form
\[\min_{(x_n)_{n\in\mathcal N}}\sum_{n\in\mathcal N}p_n c_n^\top x_n\quad\text{subject to}\quad x_n\in X_n\ \text{for all }n,\qquad A_nx_n+B_nx_{a(n)}=b_n\ \text{for }n\ne r.\]
The decision \(x_n\) uses only the history represented by node \(n\). In a scenario-indexed equivalent formulation, decisions associated with histories that are indistinguishable at their decision stage must therefore be equal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Mixed-integer decisions are made sequentially on a finite scenario tree, with each decision depending only on information revealed along its history and with at least one integer-constrained decision component.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal N\) is a finite rooted scenario tree with consistent unconditional node probabilities \(p_n\).
\(X_n\subseteq\mathbb R^{d_n-k_n}\times\mathbb Z^{k_n}\), where \(0\le k_n\le d_n\), and \(k_n\ge1\) for at least one \(n\in\mathcal N\).
All displayed objective and linking data are dimensionally compatible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The feasible policies are the scenario-tree assignments \((x_n)_{n\in\mathcal N}\) satisfying the node domains, parent-child linking constraints, integrality restrictions, and the nonanticipativity encoded by the tree information structure.

notation.meaning: Decision made using the history represented by node n.

children.title: Rolling-Horizon Reoptimization Regime
children.top_down_role: Repeated finite-horizon stochastic integer models embedded in operational reoptimization.

children.title: Rolling-Horizon SMIP
children.top_down_role: Finite-horizon stochastic integer models advanced through successive planning windows.

knowledge_statements.title: Rolling-Horizon SMIP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-window stochastic mixed-integer control with repeated solution and partial implementation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given state \(s_t\), information \(\mathcal F_t\), window length \(H\), and implementation length \(k\le H\), construct at epoch \(t\) a scenario-tree SMIP over \(t,\ldots,t+H-1\), conditional on \(\mathcal F_t\). Solve it to obtain a nonanticipative policy \(\hat\pi_t\); implement only controls \(u_t,\ldots,u_{t+k-1}\) prescribed on the realized path. Observe new information, update the state, set \(t\leftarrow t+k\), and repeat until the operational terminal time. The output is the concatenation of implemented controls, not any single window's complete plan.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly solve a finite-horizon SMIP using current information, implement only its near-term controls, update the state, and shift the window.
assumptions_latex: \(H\in\mathbb N\) and \(1\le k\le H\).
The window model is measurable with respect to current information \(\mathcal F_t\).
Each solved window supplies an implementable first control block.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The procedure produces an adapted implemented sequence \((u_t)\) by repeated conditional SMIP solution and truncation.

notation.meaning: Number of controls implemented before reoptimization.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits the leaf and is internally coherent, but the cited general stochastic-systems section does not provide inspectable support for repeated finite-window SMIP solution, partial implementation, and window shifting. A rolling-horizon or model-predictive stochastic mixed-integer optimization source is required.

children.title: Operational Reoptimization
children.top_down_role: Repeated solution of stochastic integer models after updated operational information.

knowledge_statements.title: Operational Reoptimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feedback interpretation of repeated stochastic mixed-integer replanning.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
At each decision epoch \(t\), operational reoptimization maps the observed state and information to the first admissible control block of a newly solved conditional model:
\[u_t\in\operatorname{First}\!\left(\arg\min_{\pi\in\Pi_t(s_t)}\mathbb E\!\left[C_{t:t+H-1}(\pi,\xi)\mid\mathcal F_t\right]\right).\]
After implementing \(u_t\), the realized transition determines \(s_{t+1}\), and the optimization is reconstructed. Thus previously planned future controls carry no commitment unless encoded as state, contractual, or linking constraints; only the implemented control must be feasible for the current operational state.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Operational reoptimization converts repeated conditional optimization into feedback control: implement the current action, observe the transition, and recompute future actions.
assumptions_latex: \(s_t\) and \(\mathcal F_t\) are observed before choosing \(u_t\).
\(\Pi_t(s_t)\) contains nonanticipative mixed-integer policies feasible from \(s_t\).
The conditional optimization attains an implementable first control.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(u_t\) is \(\mathcal F_t\)-measurable and feasible at the observed state, while unimplemented future controls may be replaced at epoch \(t+1\).

notation.meaning: Feasible policies from the current state.
Projection onto the first implemented control block.

children.title: Horizon-Boundary Effects
children.top_down_role: Decision distortions associated with truncated future consequences.

knowledge_statements.title: Horizon-Boundary Effects
knowledge_statements.scope_note: End-of-window distortion caused by omitted post-horizon consequences.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a rolling window ending at \(T\) whose model minimizes \(\mathbb E[\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}c_t(s_t,u_t)+V_T(s_T)]\). If the terminal approximation \(V_T\) omits a nonzero continuation value or terminal feasibility requirement, two states with identical in-window costs but different post-\(T\) consequences are valued equally by the truncated model. Consequently, it may defer costly obligations beyond \(T\), deplete inventories, or leave infeasible commitments. The boundary effect disappears only when \(V_T\) and terminal constraints reproduce the relevant continuation problem exactly; otherwise it is a truncation-induced failure mechanism.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A truncated rolling window can favor actions whose costs or infeasibility occur just beyond its boundary unless terminal values and constraints capture continuation effects.
assumptions_latex: The true problem has consequences after the window endpoint \(T\).
The truncated model represents continuation through \(V_T\) and terminal constraints.
At least two reachable terminal states have distinct true continuation values.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(V_T\) or terminal feasibility is inexact, a truncated-window optimizer need not select the action preferred by the full-horizon problem.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure mechanism is plausible and fits the leaf, but no citation supports the asserted boundary distortion or the exact-continuation qualification. An authoritative rolling-horizon, terminal-value, or model-predictive-control source is required.

children.title: Integrality Placement
children.top_down_role: Problem classes distinguished by the stages containing discrete variables.

children.title: Integer First Stage with Continuous Recourse
children.top_down_role: Discrete planning decisions followed by continuous corrective action.

knowledge_statements.title: Integer First Stage with Continuous Recourse
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-stage linear stochastic program with first-stage integrality only.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(1\le k\le n\) and \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^{n-k}\times\mathbb Z^k\). An integer-first-stage stochastic program with continuous recourse is
\[\min_{x\in X}\left\{c^\top x+\sum_{s\in S}p_sQ_s(x)\right\},\qquad Q_s(x):=\min_{y_s\in\mathbb R_+^{m_s}}\{q_s^\top y_s:W_sy_s=h_s-T_sx\}.\]
All designated discrete choices occur in the here-and-now vector \(x\); every scenario-dependent recourse vector \(y_s\) is continuous. Thus, for fixed \(x\), each recourse problem is a linear program, although the overall model remains mixed-integer because \(X\) contains at least one integer-constrained component.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The initial planning vector contains at least one integer-constrained component, while every scenario-specific corrective problem is a continuous linear program.
assumptions_latex: \(S\) is finite with probabilities \(p_s>0\) satisfying \(\sum_{s\in S}p_s=1\).
\(1\le k\le n\) and \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^{n-k}\times\mathbb Z^k\).
Each continuous recourse problem is feasible and bounded on the admitted first-stage domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For fixed \(x\in X\), every \(Q_s(x)\) is an optimal linear-program value and no recourse component is integer-constrained.

notation.meaning: Mixed-integer first-stage feasible set with at least one integer-constrained component.

children.title: Continuous First Stage with Integer Recourse
children.top_down_role: Continuous initial decisions followed by discrete corrective action.

knowledge_statements.title: Continuous First Stage with Integer Recourse
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-stage stochastic program with continuous planning and mixed-integer corrective decisions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) contain no integrality restrictions. A continuous-first-stage program with integer recourse is
\[\min_{x\in X}\left\{c^\top x+\sum_{s\in S}p_sQ_s(x)\right\},\qquad Q_s(x):=\min_{y_s\in Y_s}\{q_s^\top y_s:W_sy_s=h_s-T_sx\},\]
where \(Y_s\subseteq\mathbb R^{m_s-\ell_s}\times\mathbb Z^{\ell_s}\) and \(\ell_s\ge1\). The here-and-now decision is continuous, but at least one scenario-dependent corrective decision is discrete, so the recourse value generally need not have the convex polyhedral structure of continuous linear recourse.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The initial decision is continuous, but each scenario may require discrete corrective choices, making the recourse value generally nonconvex.
assumptions_latex: \(S\) is finite with positive probabilities summing to one.
\(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) has no integer restriction.
\(Y_s\subseteq\mathbb R^{m_s-\ell_s}\times\mathbb Z^{\ell_s}\) with \(\ell_s\ge1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: All first-stage variables are continuous, while \(Q_s(x)\) is a mixed-integer recourse value for every scenario with \(\ell_s\ge1\).

notation.meaning: Number of integer recourse components in scenario s.

children.title: Mixed-Integer Decisions in Both Stages
children.top_down_role: Mixed discrete and continuous decisions on both sides of information revelation.

knowledge_statements.title: Mixed-Integer Decisions in Both Stages
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-stage formulation with designated integer components before and after uncertainty revelation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^{n-k}\times\mathbb Z^k\) with \(k\ge1\), and for each scenario let \(Y_s\subseteq\mathbb R^{m_s-\ell_s}\times\mathbb Z^{\ell_s}\) with \(\ell_s\ge1\). A mixed-integer program in both stages is
\[\min_{x\in X}\left\{c^\top x+\sum_{s\in S}p_s\min_{y_s\in Y_s}\{q_s^\top y_s:W_sy_s=h_s-T_sx\}\right\}.\]
The first-stage integer components are nonanticipative because \(x\) is shared across scenarios; the second-stage integer components may vary with the observed scenario through \(y_s\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Both the common pre-observation decision and the scenario-dependent recourse decisions contain integer components.
assumptions_latex: \(S\) is finite with positive probabilities summing to one.
\(k\ge1\) first-stage components are integer-constrained.
\(\ell_s\ge1\) recourse components are integer-constrained in each scenario.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed model places integrality on both the nonanticipative vector \(x\) and each adaptive recourse vector \(y_s\).

notation.meaning: Number of integer recourse components in scenario s.

children.title: Multistage State-Control Integrality
children.top_down_role: Sequential models distinguished by integrality in linking states, local controls, or both.

children.title: Multistage Discrete States
children.top_down_role: Integral state variables carrying decisions across stages.

knowledge_statements.title: Multistage Discrete States
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scenario-tree model whose endogenous state contains integer components.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
On a finite scenario tree with parent map \(a(n)\), let the endogenous state at node \(n\) be \(s_n=(s_n^c,s_n^d)\in\mathbb R^{r_n}\times\mathbb Z^{k_n}\), with \(k_n\ge1\) at every node classified as having a discrete state. Let \(u_{a(n)}\) denote the control selected at the parent and let \(\xi_n\) denote the uncertainty revealed on the arc into \(n\). A multistage discrete-state SMIP imposes
\[s_n=F_n(s_{a(n)},u_{a(n)},\xi_n)\]
for every nonroot node \(n\), where \(F_n\) maps feasible parent states, controls, and arc realizations into the declared state domain. Together with nonanticipative controls, these transitions propagate discrete endogenous information, such as commitment or installed-unit status, to descendant decisions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A multistage model has integer-valued state components generated by scenario-tree transitions and used to constrain later decisions.
assumptions_latex: The uncertainty process is represented by a finite scenario tree.
\(k_n\ge1\) at every node classified as having a discrete state.
Each transition map \(F_n\) maps its feasible arguments into \(\mathbb R^{r_n}\times\mathbb Z^{k_n}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each feasible policy induces node states \(s_n\in\mathbb R^{r_n}\times\mathbb Z^{k_n}\) satisfying the parent-child transition at every nonroot node.

notation.meaning: Integer component of the endogenous state at node n.
Control selected at the parent of node n.
Uncertainty realization revealed on the arc into node n.

children.title: Multistage Discrete Controls
children.top_down_role: Integral local decisions selected within individual stages.

knowledge_statements.title: Multistage Discrete Controls
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scenario-tree model with integer-valued controls selected after successive observations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
On a finite scenario tree, let \(s_n\) be the state observed at decision node \(n\). A multistage discrete-control SMIP assigns a control \(u_n=(u_n^c,u_n^d)\in U_n(s_n)\subseteq\mathbb R^{q_n}\times\mathbb Z^{k_n}\), where \(k_n\ge1\). The control is selected using the history represented by \(n\). For every child \(m\) of \(n\), let \(\xi_m\) be the uncertainty revealed on the arc from \(n\) to \(m\), and impose the successor transition
\[s_m=F_m(s_n,u_n,\xi_m).\]
In a scenario-indexed equivalent formulation, controls associated with histories that are indistinguishable when the control is selected must coincide. Thus integrality applies to adaptive actions, while nonanticipativity prevents those actions from using future uncertainty.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Controls containing integer components are selected sequentially from currently available information and affect successor states subject to nonanticipativity.
assumptions_latex: The uncertainty process is represented by a finite scenario tree.
\(U_n(s_n)\subseteq\mathbb R^{q_n}\times\mathbb Z^{k_n}\) with \(k_n\ge1\) at every node classified as having a discrete control.
Each control \(u_n\) is measurable with respect to the history represented by node \(n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A feasible policy selects integer-containing controls \(u_n\) using only information available at node \(n\) and satisfies the successor transition on every outgoing tree arc.

notation.meaning: Integer component of the control at node n.
State-dependent feasible control set at node n.
Uncertainty revealed on the arc into child node m.
Transition map to child node m.

children.title: Coupled State-Control Integrality
children.top_down_role: Sequential models with simultaneous integrality in linking states plus local controls.

knowledge_statements.title: Coupled State-Control Integrality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Joint integrality and transition condition linking discrete states to discrete controls.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
At each scenario-tree node \(n\), write \(s_n=(s_n^c,s_n^d)\) and \(u_n=(u_n^c,u_n^d)\), with \((s_n^d,u_n^d)\in\mathbb Z^{k_n}\times\mathbb Z^{\ell_n}\). Coupled state-control integrality holds when feasibility is imposed jointly by
\[(s_n,u_n)\in K_n,\qquad s_m^d=A_{mn}s_n^d+B_{mn}u_n^d+d_{mn}(\xi_m)\in\mathbb Z^{k_m}\]
for every child \(m\) of \(n\), rather than by independent state and control domains alone. The joint set \(K_n\) may encode logical restrictions, and the transition propagates each discrete action into descendant discrete states.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Discrete states and controls are jointly constrained, and integer transitions propagate their logical coupling to descendant nodes.
assumptions_latex: The model is defined on a finite scenario tree.
\(s_n^d\in\mathbb Z^{k_n}\) and \(u_n^d\in\mathbb Z^{\ell_n}\).
Transition data are compatible with integer successor states.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Feasibility requires both \((s_n,u_n)\in K_n\) and an integer-valued successor state satisfying the displayed coupled transition at every tree arc.

notation.meaning: Joint state-control feasible set at node n.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cited general stochastic-systems and discrete-optimization sections do not establish that the displayed joint-set and affine-transition condition is the intended mathematical meaning of this specialized terminal. A source specifically treating coupled discrete state-control restrictions is needed before choosing between this formulation and other legitimate coupling models.

children.title: Integer Recourse Classes
children.top_down_role: Classical recourse families distinguished by matrix structure and separability.

children.title: Fixed Integer Recourse
children.top_down_role: Integer recourse with a scenario-independent recourse matrix.

knowledge_statements.title: Fixed Integer Recourse
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Integer recourse whose technology matrix and integer lattice are scenario-independent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A two-stage stochastic program has fixed integer recourse when its second-stage value can be written
\[Q(x,\xi):=\min_{y\in Y}\{q(\xi)^\top y:Wy=h(\xi)-T(\xi)x\},\qquad Y:=\mathbb R_+^{m-k}\times\mathbb Z_+^k,\]
where \(k\ge1\) and the recourse matrix \(W\) and domain \(Y\) do not depend on the realization \(\xi\). The right-hand side, technology matrix, and recourse costs may be random. Thus every realization uses the same integer recourse columns and lattice structure, although its required recourse and costs may change.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Integer recourse is fixed when every uncertainty realization uses the same recourse matrix and mixed-integer domain, while costs or right-hand sides may vary.
assumptions_latex: \(k\ge1\), so the recourse vector has an integer component.
\(W\) and \(Y\) are deterministic and scenario-independent.
The recourse value is interpreted on first-stage decisions for which it is well-defined.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every realization \(\xi\), \(Q(x,\xi)\) uses the common matrix \(W\) and common mixed-integer set \(Y\).

children.title: Random Integer Recourse
children.top_down_role: Integer recourse whose feasible corrective structure varies with uncertainty.

assumptions_latex: The uncertainty (\xi\u001b) is defined on a probability space ((\Omega,\mathcal F,\mathbb P)\u001b).
For every admissible first-stage decision, the second-stage problem is measurable and has a well-defined extended-real optimal value.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The recourse is random integer recourse because the integer-feasible corrective system itself depends on \(\xi\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-stage linear random integer recourse, allowing scenario-dependent recourse matrices and integrality structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^{n-p}\times\mathbb Z^p\). A two-stage model has random integer recourse if its objective is \(\inf_{x\in X}\{c^{\mathsf T}x+\mathbb E[Q(x,\xi)]\}\), where
\[
Q(x,\xi)=\inf\{q(\xi)^{\mathsf T}y:W(\xi)y=h(\xi)-T(\xi)x,\ y\in Y(\xi)\},
\]
and \(Y(\xi)\subseteq\mathbb R^{m-r(\xi)}\times\mathbb Z^{r(\xi)}\) contains at least one integer-constrained component on a set of positive probability. The adjective random means that one or more of \(W(\xi)\), \(T(\xi)\), \(h(\xi)\), \(q(\xi)\), or \(Y(\xi)\) varies with \(\xi\), so the corrective integer optimization problem is scenario dependent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Random integer recourse is a second-stage integer optimization problem whose data or integer-feasible corrective structure changes with the realized uncertainty.
knowledge_statements.title: Random Integer Recourse

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cited general recourse section does not establish this integer-specific terminology. The statement also treats variation in costs or right-hand-side data as random integer recourse even though the node role requires variation of the feasible corrective structure; the conclusion is therefore inconsistent with the definition. The assumptions additionally contain control characters and malformed delimiters.

children.title: Simple Integer Recourse
children.top_down_role: Separable integer correction structures with specialized analytic and approximation theory.

assumptions_latex: The recourse variables are integer valued and componentwise nonnegative.
The expected recourse value exists as an extended-real quantity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The resulting value is a separable sum of one-dimensional upward and downward integer corrections.

notation.meaning: residual demand after the first-stage decision

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separable two-sided simple integer recourse with unit correction columns.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(z(\xi,x)=h(\xi)-T(\xi)x\in\mathbb R^m\), simple integer recourse is the value function
\[
Q(x,\xi)=\min\{(q^+)^{\mathsf T}y^+ +(q^-)^{\mathsf T}y^-:y^+-y^-=z(\xi,x),\ y^+,y^-\in\mathbb Z_+^m\},
\]
with \(q^+,q^-\in\mathbb R_+^m\). Equivalently, its recourse matrix is \(W=[I,-I]\) and all corrective variables are integer. Feasibility requires \(z(\xi,x)\in\mathbb Z^m\); when this lattice condition holds, the problem separates by coordinate and each coordinate is corrected upward or downward at its specified unit cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Simple integer recourse uses separable nonnegative integer shortage and surplus variables to match each component of an integral residual independently.
knowledge_statements.title: Simple Integer Recourse

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The equality formulation is feasible only for integral residuals and may not be the standard simple integer-recourse model, which commonly uses rounded one-sided corrections for nonintegral residuals. The cited section is not identified as supporting the integer variant, so the exact formulation requires an integer-recourse source.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite-shift bounds for a simple integer recourse function
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The bounds use the source-defined functions \(v\) and \(\widehat v\), whose definitions are not included in this extract.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\xi\) be a random variable with \(\widehat F(t)=\mathbb P\{\xi<t\}\). Then \[\widehat v(x)\leq v(x)\leq \widehat v(x)+\widehat F(x).\] For any integer \(n\geq1\), define \[v_n(x)=\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}\widehat F(x-k)+\widehat v(x-n).\] Then \[v_n(x)\leq v(x)\leq v_n(x)+\widehat F(x-n).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the source-defined integer-recourse functions v and v-hat, v-hat(x) is a lower bound on v(x), with gap at most F-hat(x). More generally, the stated finite-shift expression v_n(x) is a lower bound whose gap is at most F-hat(x−n).
assumptions_latex: \xi\text{ is a random variable and }\widehat F(t)=\mathbb P\{\xi<t\}
n\in\mathbb Z,\quad n\geq1
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \widehat v(x)\leq v(x)\leq\widehat v(x)+\widehat F(x),\qquad v_n(x)\leq v(x)\leq v_n(x)+\widehat F(x-n)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Integer-shift affine inequality for simple recourse
knowledge_statements.scope_note: An inequality for integer translates of the simple integer recourse value function; it is not described as convex interpolation because the extracted assumptions do not ensure that λ lies in [0,1].
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let $x^0\in\mathbb R$ and $i,j\in\mathbb Z$ satisfy $j\le i$ and $i\ne0$. Define $x^1=x^0+i$, $x^\lambda=x^0+j$, and $\lambda=(i-j)/i$. Then
\[
\Psi(x^\lambda)\le \lambda\Psi(x^0)+(1-\lambda)\Psi(x^1).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Let x0 be real and let i and j be integers with j≤i and i nonzero. Define x1=x0+i, xλ=x0+j, and λ=(i−j)/i. Then Ψ(xλ)≤λΨ(x0)+(1−λ)Ψ(x1).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Simple integer recourse and its separable representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definition of a two-stage simple-integer-recourse model and its decomposition into expected integer shortage and surplus terms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\xi\in\mathbb R^m\) be random, let \(T,q^+,q^-\) be fixed, and assume \(q_i^+,q_i^-\ge 0\). A two-stage stochastic program has simple integer recourse when its second-stage problem uses \(y^+,y^-\in\mathbb Z_+^m\) to satisfy
\[y^+\ge \xi-Tx,\qquad y^-\ge Tx-\xi,\]
and minimizes \((q^+)^Ty^++(q^-)^Ty^-\). Writing \(\chi=Tx\), the expected recourse function is separable:
\[\mathcal Q(x)=\sum_{i=1}^m\psi_i(\chi_i),\qquad \psi_i(\chi_i)=q_i^+u_i(\chi_i)+q_i^-v_i(\chi_i),\]
where
\[u_i(t)=\mathbb E\!\left[\lceil\xi_i-t\rceil^+\right],\qquad v_i(t)=\mathbb E\!\left[\lceil t-\xi_i\rceil^+\right],\qquad \lceil s\rceil^+=\max\{\lceil s\rceil,0\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Simple integer recourse compensates componentwise shortages and surpluses using nonnegative integer second-stage variables. With fixed technology and recourse costs, its expected recourse function separates by tender coordinate into weighted expected integer-shortage and integer-surplus functions.
assumptions_latex: \(\xi\) is an \(\mathbb R^m\)-valued random vector.
\(T,q^+,q^-\) are fixed and \(q_i^+,q_i^-\ge0\).
\(y^+,y^-\in\mathbb Z_+^m\) almost surely, with componentwise inequalities.
First-stage decisions satisfy \(Ax=b\) and \(x\in X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal Q(x)=\sum_{i=1}^m\bigl(q_i^+u_i((Tx)_i)+q_i^-v_i((Tx)_i)\bigr)\), where \(u_i(t)=\mathbb E[\lceil\xi_i-t\rceil^+]\) and \(v_i(t)=\mathbb E[\lceil t-\xi_i\rceil^+]\).

children.title: Structured Integer Recourse Classes
children.top_down_role: Structured recourse classes supporting specialized convexification and approximation.

children.title: Network Integer Recourse
children.top_down_role: Integer recourse organized by network-flow structure.

assumptions_latex: The directed network and its node-arc incidence matrix are fixed for the recourse problem.
Arc flows satisfy stated integral restrictions and bounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The second-stage correction is an integer network-flow optimization problem.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Integer recourse whose equality constraints are flow-balance equations on a directed network.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(G=(V,A)\) be a directed graph with node-arc incidence matrix \(B\). A recourse function has network integer recourse when it can be written
\[
Q(x,\xi)=\min\{q(\xi)^{\mathsf T}y:By=b(x,\xi),\ \ell(\xi)\le y\le u(\xi),\ y_a\in\mathbb Z\text{ for }a\in A_I\},
\]
where \(A_I\subseteq A\) is nonempty and \(b(x,\xi)=h(\xi)-T(\xi)x\). Thus every recourse equality is a node-flow balance equation, while bounds encode arc capacities. The value is \(+\infty\) when no bounded integral flow satisfies the realized balances.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Network integer recourse represents corrective decisions as bounded integer arc flows satisfying scenario-dependent node-balance equations.
knowledge_statements.title: Network Integer Recourse

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The content kind and network-flow definition fit the leaf, but no inspectable source supports the dedicated notion of network integer recourse or its precise formulation.

children.title: Totally Unimodular Integer Recourse
children.top_down_role: Recourse models governed by totally unimodular constraint matrices.

assumptions_latex: The recourse matrix is totally unimodular.
The realized right-hand side and all finite variable bounds are integral.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every nonempty recourse polyhedron has integral extreme points, so its linear relaxation attains an integer optimum whenever it attains an optimum.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Integrality consequence of total unimodularity for scenario-wise recourse polyhedra.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(W\in\{-1,0,1\}^{m\times n}\) be totally unimodular and define
\[
P(x,\xi)=\{y\in\mathbb R^n:Wy=r(x,\xi),\ \ell(\xi)\le y\le u(\xi)\}.
\]
If \(r(x,\xi)\), \(\ell(\xi)\), and \(u(\xi)\) are integral whenever finite, then every extreme point of \(P(x,\xi)\) is integral. Consequently, for any cost vector \(q(\xi)\), if the linear program \(\min\{q(\xi)^{\mathsf T}y:y\in P(x,\xi)\}\) has an optimal solution, it has an integral optimal solution and equals the corresponding all-integer recourse value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A totally unimodular recourse matrix with integral balances and bounds makes the scenario-wise linear relaxation exact for all-integer recourse.
knowledge_statements.title: Totally Unimodular Integer Recourse

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property correctly matches the leaf and states the standard total-unimodularity consequence under integral data, but the nontrivial integrality claim has no cited source.

children.title: Network Convexification Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Structural limits of network-based convexification for integer recourse.

assumptions_latex: The base recourse constraints use a node-arc incidence matrix.
The modified model permits either fractional balances or additional non-network constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Network structure alone does not guarantee that the linear relaxation equals the integer recourse problem.

notation.meaning: incidence matrix of a one-arc network

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp limits of incidence-matrix integrality under nonintegral data or structure-destroying side constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Total unimodularity yields integral network-flow vertices only with integral right-hand sides and bounds. For the one-arc balance system \(B=[1]\), the relaxation \(\{y\in\mathbb R_+:By=1/2\}\) has the unique fractional point \(y=1/2\), whereas \(\{y\in\mathbb Z_+:By=1/2\}\) is empty. Even with integral balances, adjoining arbitrary linking or side constraints can produce a matrix that is not totally unimodular and fractional extreme points may appear. Hence replacing network integer recourse by its linear relaxation is exact only while the relevant total-unimodularity and integral-data hypotheses are preserved.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Network-flow convexification can fail when balances or bounds are fractional, or when added side constraints destroy total unimodularity.
knowledge_statements.title: Network Convexification Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role is appropriate and the fractional-balance example is coherent, but neither the boundary claim nor the effect of added side constraints has an inspectable citation.

children.title: Uncertainty Representation Classes
children.top_down_role: SMIP regimes distinguished by finite, sampled, or continuously distributed uncertainty.

children.title: Finite-Scenario SMIP
children.top_down_role: Models represented by an explicit finite scenario set or tree.

assumptions_latex: The uncertainty has finite support with positive scenario probabilities summing to one.
Each scenario-wise recourse value is well defined in the extended reals.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The stochastic expectation is exactly a finite probability-weighted sum of scenario recourse values.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-stage finite-support stochastic mixed-integer model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(S=\{1,\ldots,N\}\) be the support of \(\xi\), with \(p_s>0\) and \(\sum_{s\in S}p_s=1\). A finite-scenario stochastic mixed-integer program has the representation
\[
\min_{x\in X}\left\{c^{\mathsf T}x+\sum_{s\in S}p_sQ_s(x)\right\},
\qquad
Q_s(x)=\min_{y_s\in Y_s}\{q_s^{\mathsf T}y_s:W_sy_s=h_s-T_sx\},
\]
where \(X\) or at least one \(Y_s\) imposes integrality. This finite sum is the exact expectation under the stated discrete law, rather than an empirical approximation to a different distribution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite-scenario SMIP exactly replaces expectation by a probability-weighted sum over the finite support of the specified uncertainty distribution.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Scenario SMIP

children.title: Sampled SMIP
children.top_down_role: Finite empirical models generated from an underlying probability law.

assumptions_latex: The observations are sampled from an underlying probability law.
The same first-stage feasible set is used in the population and empirical models.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The sampled SMIP minimizes the empirical average of scenario recourse values.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite empirical approximation of a population stochastic mixed-integer program.

source_refs.locator: 1.4 Deterministic optimization procedures and their stochastic counterparts p. 22

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given realizations \(\xi^1,\ldots,\xi^N\) from a probability law \(P\), the sampled stochastic mixed-integer program associated with
\[
\min_{x\in X}\{c^{\mathsf T}x+\mathbb E_P[Q(x,\xi)]\}
\]
is
\[
\min_{x\in X}F_N(x),
\qquad
F_N(x)=c^{\mathsf T}x+\frac1N\sum_{i=1}^N Q(x,\xi^i),
\]
where \(X\) or the feasible set defining \(Q\) contains integer restrictions. Conditional on the sample, this is a finite-scenario SMIP with empirical probabilities \(1/N\); it need not equal the population problem for finite \(N\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sampled SMIP replaces a population expectation by the average recourse cost over finitely many sampled realizations.
knowledge_statements.title: Sampled SMIP

source_witnesses.locator: 1.4 Deterministic optimization procedures and their stochastic counterparts p. 22

children.title: Continuous-Distribution Integer Recourse
children.top_down_role: Integer-recourse models retaining integration over a nonfinite probability law.

assumptions_latex: The uncertainty law is not finitely supported.
The integer-recourse value is measurable and its expectation is well defined as an extended-real integral.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The objective retains integration over the nonfinite probability law rather than an exact finite scenario sum.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-stage integer recourse under a nonfinite, possibly continuous, uncertainty distribution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(P\) be a probability measure whose support is not finite. A continuous-distribution integer-recourse model is
\[
\inf_{x\in X}\left\{c^{\mathsf T}x+\int Q(x,\xi)\,P(d\xi)\right\},
\qquad
Q(x,\xi)=\inf_{y\in Y}\{q(\xi)^{\mathsf T}y:W(\xi)y=h(\xi)-T(\xi)x\},
\]
where \(Y\subseteq\mathbb R^{m-r}\times\mathbb Z^r\) with \(r\ge1\). The defining distinction is that the integral is part of the model itself; any finite sample or quadrature rule produces an approximation unless it integrates the relevant recourse function exactly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Continuous-distribution integer recourse integrates an integer second-stage value over a nonfinite uncertainty law; finite scenarios generally provide only an approximation.
knowledge_statements.title: Continuous-Distribution Integer Recourse

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Nonfinite support does not imply a continuous distribution; it also includes countably infinite discrete laws. The definition must specify the intended continuous or non-atomic law, and the general cited recourse sections do not establish the integer-specific formulation.

children.title: SMIP Representation Family
children.top_down_role: Alternative organizations of scenario structure, nonanticipativity, recourse functions, and sequential state.

children.title: Scenario Extensive Forms
children.top_down_role: Monolithic deterministic-equivalent organizations of scenario copies and linking structure.

children.title: Two-Stage Block-Angular Form
children.top_down_role: A common first-stage block coupled to scenario recourse blocks.

assumptions_latex: The uncertainty has finitely many scenarios with probabilities summing to one.
Scenario recourse variables interact only with the common first-stage decision.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Replicating recourse variables by scenario yields the displayed block-angular deterministic equivalent.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic equivalent of a finite-scenario two-stage stochastic mixed-integer program.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For scenarios \(s\in S\), the two-stage extensive form is
\[
\min_{x,\{y_s\}_{s\in S}} c^{\mathsf T}x+\sum_{s\in S}p_sq_s^{\mathsf T}y_s
\]
subject to \(Ax=b\), \(T_sx+W_sy_s=h_s\) for every \(s\in S\), \(x\in X\), and \(y_s\in Y_s\), where \(X\) or some \(Y_s\) imposes integrality. In the constraint matrix, each scenario row block contains the shared columns of \(x\) and only its own columns of \(y_s\); distinct recourse blocks have no direct common variables. This is the two-stage block-angular form.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The deterministic equivalent couples one common first-stage block to independent scenario-specific recourse blocks through scenario constraints.
knowledge_statements.title: Two-Stage Block-Angular Form

children.title: Scenario-Tree Extensive Form
children.top_down_role: Multistage deterministic equivalents organized by information nodes.

assumptions_latex: The uncertainty is represented by a finite rooted scenario tree.
Decisions at a node may depend only on information revealed along the path to that node.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: One decision vector per information node gives a deterministic equivalent satisfying nonanticipativity by construction.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Node-based deterministic equivalent for a finite multistage stochastic mixed-integer program.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathcal T=(\mathcal N,\mathcal A)\) be a finite rooted scenario tree, with predecessor \(a(n)\) for each nonroot node and reach probability \(p_n\). A node-based extensive form assigns one vector \(x_n\in X_n\) to each information node and has the form
\[
\min \sum_{n\in\mathcal N}p_nc_n^{\mathsf T}x_n
\quad\text{subject to}\quad
A_nx_n+B_nx_{a(n)}=b_n\ \text{for all nonroot }n,
\]
together with root constraints and any prescribed integrality in \(X_n\). Because histories sharing the same information node use the same \(x_n\), nonanticipativity is enforced by the indexing itself.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A scenario-tree extensive form assigns decisions to information nodes and links each node to its predecessor, enforcing nonanticipativity by shared node decisions.
knowledge_statements.title: Scenario-Tree Extensive Form

children.title: SMIP Formulation Size-Strength Tradeoff
children.top_down_role: Alternative variable spaces trading formulation size against relaxation strength.

children.title: Compact SMIP Formulations
children.top_down_role: Stochastic mixed-integer formulations using reduced variable spaces.

assumptions_latex: The formulation uses the original decision variables of the selected SMIP representation.
Its feasible integer points project trivially to the intended feasible decisions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A compact formulation describes the SMIP without auxiliary-variable projection, though its linear relaxation may be weaker than an extended formulation.

notation.meaning: original variables of the deterministic equivalent

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Original-space formulation of a finite deterministic equivalent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F\subseteq\mathbb R^{d-r}\times\mathbb Z^r\) be the feasible set of a finite deterministic equivalent in its original variables \(z\). A compact SMIP formulation is a mixed-integer linear system
\[
P=\{z:Az\le b,\ z_j\in\mathbb Z\text{ for }j\in I\}
\]
with \(P\cap(\mathbb R^{d-r}\times\mathbb Z^r)=F\), expressed without auxiliary variables requiring projection. Compactness is relative to a chosen encoding and means that the formulation size, measured by its variables and inequalities, is controlled directly in the original space. This definition does not assert that the relaxation \(P\) equals \(\operatorname{conv}(F)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A compact SMIP formulation uses only original deterministic-equivalent variables and constraints; compactness does not imply a strong linear relaxation.
knowledge_statements.title: Compact SMIP Formulations

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source supports the chosen convention that compact necessarily means an original-space formulation without auxiliary variables. Because compactness is encoding-dependent and is not universally contrasted with extension in this way, the exact definition requires a formulation source.

children.title: Extended SMIP Formulations
children.top_down_role: Stochastic mixed-integer formulations using lifted variables or auxiliary structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Extended SMIP Formulations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lifted mixed-integer formulation whose projection is the original deterministic equivalent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F\subseteq\mathbb R^{d-r}\times\mathbb Z^r\) be the feasible set of an SMIP deterministic equivalent. An extended SMIP formulation is a mixed-integer linear set
\[
E=\{(z,u):Az+Bu\le b,\ z_j\in\mathbb Z\text{ for }j\in I,\ u_k\in\mathbb Z\text{ for }k\in J\text{ when required}\}
\]
satisfying
\[
\operatorname{proj}_z(E)=F.
\]
The auxiliary vector \(u\) may encode scenario structure, disjunctions, paths, or additional state. Validity is determined by exact projection of mixed-integer feasible points; relaxation strength is determined separately by the projected continuous relaxation \(\operatorname{proj}_z(\operatorname{relax} E)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An extended SMIP formulation introduces auxiliary variables and constraints whose projection exactly recovers the original mixed-integer feasible set.
assumptions_latex: The intended feasible set is expressed in original variables.
Auxiliary variables may be continuous or integer, as specified by the formulation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The extended system is valid exactly when projecting its mixed-integer feasible points recovers the original SMIP feasible set.

children.title: Size–Strength Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Comparisons of formulation scale against relaxation quality.

knowledge_statements.title: Size–Strength Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compares equivalent extensive formulations through their continuous relaxations and encoding sizes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F_C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be a compact mixed-integer formulation and \(F_E\subseteq\mathbb R^{n+r}\) an extended formulation with \(\operatorname{proj}_x(F_E)=F_C\). Let \(R_C\) and \(R_E\) denote the formulations obtained by relaxing all integrality restrictions. If \(\operatorname{proj}_x(R_E)\subseteq R_C\), then the extended formulation is at least as strong: for every linear minimization objective \(c^Tx\), \[\min\{c^Tx:(x,z)\in R_E\}\geq\min\{c^Tx:x\in R_C\}.\] Strict inclusion can produce a strictly stronger bound, while \(F_E\) may require additional variables and constraints. Formulation size alone therefore does not order relaxation strength.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An equivalent extended formulation gives at least as strong a minimization bound when its projected relaxation is contained in the compact relaxation, but it may be substantially larger.
assumptions_latex: \(F_C\) and \(F_E\) have the same projected mixed-integer feasible set.
The compared objective depends only on \(x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{proj}_x(R_E)\subseteq R_C\) implies the extended relaxation dominates the compact relaxation for linear minimization.

notation.meaning: Continuous relaxations of the compact and extended formulations.
Projection onto the original decision variables.

review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports the formulation-size versus relaxation-strength comparison.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property is mathematically standard and fits the leaf, but no source or inspectable locator supports the relaxation-dominance and size–strength claims.

children.title: Nonanticipativity Representations
children.top_down_role: Equivalent organizations of decisions that share the same information.

children.title: Explicit Nonanticipativity Constraints
children.top_down_role: Scenario-replicated decisions linked by direct consistency constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Explicit Nonanticipativity Constraints
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scenario copies are equated whenever their information histories agree.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Omega\) be a finite scenario set, and for each stage \(t\) let \(\omega\sim_t\omega'\) mean that scenarios \(\omega\) and \(\omega'\) have identical information through stage \(t\). A scenario-replicated policy \(\{x_t^\omega\}\) is nonanticipative exactly when \[x_t^\omega=x_t^{\omega'}\qquad\text{for every }t\text{ and every }\omega\sim_t\omega'.\] It suffices to impose equalities along the edges of any connected graph spanning each equivalence class of \(\sim_t\). These constraints remain valid when components of \(x_t^\omega\) are continuous, integer, or binary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Scenario-specific decisions are nonanticipative precisely when copies having the same observed history are equal; connected equality links within each history class suffice.
assumptions_latex: \(\Omega\) and the stage set are finite.
\(\sim_t\) partitions scenarios by information available when \(x_t\) is selected.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed equalities characterize nonanticipativity of the scenario-replicated decisions.

notation.meaning: The two scenarios have the same history through stage t.
Stage-t decision copy assigned to scenario omega.

children.title: Node-Based Nonanticipative Variables
children.top_down_role: Decisions shared directly at common scenario-tree nodes.

knowledge_statements.title: Node-Based Nonanticipative Variables
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A single decision variable is assigned to each scenario-tree information node.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal T\) be a finite rooted scenario tree, and let \(n_t(\omega)\) be the unique stage-\(t\) node traversed by scenario \(\omega\). Assign one decision vector \(x_n\) to each decision node \(n\). The induced scenario decision is \[x_t^\omega=x_{n_t(\omega)}.\] Consequently, scenarios sharing a node automatically receive the same decision. Conversely, every nonanticipative scenario-replicated family determines a unique node-based family by setting \(x_n\) equal to the common value of the copies passing through \(n\). Thus node variables and explicit nonanticipativity equalities describe the same policy set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Using one variable per scenario-tree node enforces nonanticipativity automatically and is equivalent to consistent scenario-replicated decisions.
assumptions_latex: Each scenario follows a unique root-to-leaf path in a finite scenario tree.
Tree nodes represent complete information histories at their stages.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Node-based and explicitly linked scenario-copy representations are in bijection.

notation.meaning: Stage-t node on scenario omega's path.

children.title: Nonanticipativity-Dual Representation
children.top_down_role: Scenario-separable representations obtained through dual treatment of agreement.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonanticipativity-Dual Representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lagrangian relaxation separates scenarios but may have a duality gap for integer decisions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(v=\inf\{\sum_{\omega}p_\omega f_\omega(x^\omega):x^\omega=z,\ x^\omega\in X_\omega\}\), where \(p_\omega>0\). Dualizing the agreement equations and minimizing over the unrestricted consensus vector \(z\) gives \[d=\sup_{\{\lambda^\omega:\sum_\omega p_\omega\lambda^\omega=0\}}\sum_\omega p_\omega\inf_{x\in X_\omega}\bigl(f_\omega(x)+(\lambda^\omega)^Tx\bigr).\] The inner problems are scenario-separable and weak duality gives \(d\leq v\). Equality follows under an applicable convex strong-duality condition; mixed-integer feasible sets generally do not guarantee equality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dualizing scenario agreement yields separable scenario subproblems and a lower bound for minimization; exactness needs convex strong duality and can fail with integrality.
assumptions_latex: \(\Omega\) is finite and \(p_\omega>0\) with \(\sum_\omega p_\omega=1\).
The scenario infima and primal value are well defined in the extended-real sense.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d\leq v\), with equality only when suitable strong-duality hypotheses hold.

notation.meaning: Multiplier for scenario omega's agreement equation.

review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports the nonanticipativity Lagrangian dual and its integer duality-gap boundary.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The weighted multiplier constraint, separability, weak-duality bound, and integrality boundary are plausible and correctly scoped, but no cited source supports this exact dual representation.

children.title: Integer Recourse Function Representations
children.top_down_role: Representations exposing first-stage dependence, epigraphs, or recourse disjunctions.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Survival-series representation of expected integer shortage
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distribution-function representation of the scalar expected integer-shortage function used in simple integer recourse.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\xi\) be a real-valued random variable with cumulative distribution function \(F(t)=\mathbb P\{\xi\le t\}\), and define \(u(x)=\mathbb E[\lceil\xi-x\rceil^+]\). Then
\[u(x)=\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\bigl(1-F(x+k)\bigr).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The expected positive integer-rounded shortage at x equals the sum of the survival probabilities at x, x+1, x+2, and so on.
assumptions_latex: \(\xi\) is a real-valued random variable with cumulative distribution function \(F(t)=\mathbb P\{\xi\le t\}\).
\(x\in\mathbb R\).
\(u(x)=\mathbb E[\lceil\xi-x\rceil^+]\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(u(x)=\displaystyle\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\left(1-F(x+k)\right).\)

children.title: Parametric Value-Function Representation
children.top_down_role: Recourse organized by its dependence on master decisions or tender quantities.

knowledge_statements.title: Parametric Value-Function Representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines integer recourse as an extended-real function of the master decision.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each scenario \(\omega\), let \(Y_\omega\subseteq\mathbb R^{r_\omega}\times\mathbb Z^{k_\omega}\) encode the recourse-variable domains. The parametric recourse value is \[Q_\omega(x)=\inf\{q_\omega^Ty:W_\omega y\geq h_\omega-T_\omega x,\ y\in Y_\omega\},\] with \(Q_\omega(x)=+\infty\) when the recourse system is infeasible and \(Q_\omega(x)=-\infty\) when it is unbounded below. A finite-scenario two-stage SMIP is therefore represented as \[\inf_{x\in X}\left(c^Tx+\sum_{\omega\in\Omega}p_\omega Q_\omega(x)\right).\] The parameter may equivalently be the tender vector \(T_\omega x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each scenario’s integer recourse problem defines an extended-real value function of the master decision, and the SMIP minimizes first-stage cost plus its expected value.
assumptions_latex: \(\Omega\) is finite and \(p_\omega\geq0\) with \(\sum_\omega p_\omega=1\).
The first-stage domain \(X\) and recourse domains \(Y_\omega\) include their required integrality restrictions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The two-stage SMIP objective equals \(c^Tx+\sum_{\omega}p_\omega Q_\omega(x)\).

notation.meaning: Mixed-integer domain of scenario-omega recourse decisions.

review_flags: Locator concerns value functions generally; direct SMIP recourse support should be checked.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The formula is a standard two-stage integer-recourse value-function representation, but the cited approximate-dynamic-programming section does not specifically support the SMIP recourse model or its extended-real conventions.

children.title: Epigraphic Recourse Representation
children.top_down_role: Master-space representations intended for outer approximation.

knowledge_statements.title: Epigraphic Recourse Representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Introduces master variables representing scenario recourse values.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q_\omega:X\to\overline{\mathbb R}\) be the scenario recourse functions. Their exact epigraphic master representation is \[\inf_{x\in X,\,\theta\in\mathbb R^{|\Omega|}}\left\{c^Tx+\sum_{\omega}p_\omega\theta_\omega:\theta_\omega\geq Q_\omega(x)\ \text{for all }\omega\right\}.\] If each \(Q_\omega\) is finite below at feasible \(x\), this has the same optimal value and optimal first-stage decisions as the value-function formulation. Replacing an epigraph by inequalities \(\theta_\omega\geq\ell_{\omega j}(x)\), where every \(\ell_{\omega j}\leq Q_\omega\), gives a valid outer-approximation relaxation for minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Recourse values can be represented by epigraph variables. Valid lower estimators give a master relaxation, while the complete epigraph gives an exact formulation.
assumptions_latex: \(p_\omega\geq0\) for every scenario.
The represented problem is a minimization problem and pathological \(-\infty\) recourse values are excluded.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exact epigraph constraints preserve the SMIP value; valid recourse underestimators produce lower-bounding master relaxations.

notation.meaning: Master variable representing scenario-omega recourse cost.
Valid lower estimator of the scenario recourse function.

children.title: Disjunctive Recourse Representation
children.top_down_role: Recourse regimes exposed as unions for convexification and separation.

knowledge_statements.title: Disjunctive Recourse Representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Expresses bounded integer recourse as a finite union of continuous regimes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose the integer component of scenario recourse can take values in a finite set \(K_\omega\). For each \(k\in K_\omega\), let \(P_{\omega k}(x)\) be the continuous recourse feasible set after fixing that component to \(k\), and define \(g_{\omega k}(x)=\inf\{q_\omega^Ty:y\in P_{\omega k}(x)\}\). Then \[Q_\omega(x)=\min_{k\in K_\omega}g_{\omega k}(x),\qquad \operatorname{epi}Q_\omega=\bigcup_{k\in K_\omega}\{(x,\theta):\theta\geq g_{\omega k}(x)\}.\] Convexifying this finite union yields a relaxation suitable for valid-inequality separation; it need not preserve the original integer epigraph without integrality or disjunctive enforcement.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fixing bounded integer recourse choices exposes finitely many regimes. Their union is the exact recourse epigraph, while its convex hull is generally only a relaxation.
assumptions_latex: The relevant integer recourse assignments form a finite set \(K_\omega\).
Each regime value uses the same recourse objective and the appropriately fixed feasible system.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The integer-recourse value is the minimum of regime values, and its epigraph is their finite union.

notation.meaning: Finite set of integer recourse regimes.
Continuous recourse set under fixed regime k.
Value function of fixed regime k.

review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports this finite disjunctive representation of integer recourse.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite-regime minimum and union-of-epigraphs identities are correctly scoped, but the disjunctive integer-recourse and convexification claims have no cited source.

children.title: Multistage State Representations
children.top_down_role: Sequential formulations organized around state, control, and interstage linking structure.

children.title: Scenario-Tree State Form
children.top_down_role: State transitions indexed by nodes and parent-child information relations.

knowledge_statements.title: Scenario-Tree State Form
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Indexes states, controls, costs, and transitions by scenario-tree nodes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal T=(N,A)\) be a finite rooted scenario tree with root \(r\), parent map \(a:N\setminus\{r\}\to N\), and node-reach probabilities \(p_n\), where \(p_r=1\). For compatible matrices \(A_n,B_n\), vectors \(b_n\), and mixed-integer node sets \(X_n\), a multistage SMIP state form is \[\min\; c_r(s_r,x_r)+\sum_{n\in N\setminus\{r\}}p_n c_n(s_{a(n)},x_n,s_n)\] subject to a prescribed or separately constrained root state \(s_r\), \((s_r,x_r)\in X_r\), and, for every \(n\in N\setminus\{r\}\), \[s_n=A_ns_{a(n)}+B_nx_n+b_n,\qquad (s_n,x_n)\in X_n.\] Integrality restrictions may occur in \(s_n\), \(x_n\), or both. Because each information node has one control \(x_n\), the formulation is nonanticipative by construction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A scenario-tree state formulation assigns one state and control to each information node, treats the root separately, and links every child state to its parent. Node-indexed controls enforce nonanticipativity structurally.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal T\) is a finite rooted tree whose nodes encode information histories.
Each nonroot node has a unique parent, and the root state is prescribed or separately constrained.
All matrices, vectors, costs, and mixed-integer node sets have compatible dimensions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Parent-child transition constraints and node-indexed controls define a nonanticipative multistage SMIP state form.

notation.meaning: Parent of the nonroot node n.
State and control at node n.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Scenario-tree deterministic equivalent of a multistage stochastic linear program
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Node-indexed extensive-form representation and its equivalence to path-indexed decisions subject to nonanticipativity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal I\) be the nodes of a finite scenario tree for the exogenous information process, and let each nonroot node \(j\) have parent \(i\). With linear contributions, node-indexed decisions satisfy \[\widetilde R_{t,\tau+1}(j)=\widetilde B_{t\tau}(i)\widetilde x_{t\tau}(i)+\delta\widetilde R_{t,\tau+1}(j),\qquad \widetilde A_{t\tau}(i)\widetilde x_{t\tau}(i)=\widetilde R_{t\tau}(i),\qquad \widetilde x_{t\tau}(i)\ge0.\] Simultaneous optimization over all stages and nodes therefore forms one deterministic linear program coupled through the parent-child resource equations. Equivalently, decisions may be indexed by complete paths \(\omega\), provided that \[\widetilde x_{t\tau}(\omega)=\widetilde x_{t\tau}(\omega')\quad\text{whenever \(\omega\) and \(\omega'\) share the history observed through stage \(\tau\)},\] which enforces nonanticipativity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Indexing decisions and resource states by scenario-tree information nodes turns a finite multistage stochastic linear model into one deterministic linear program linked by parent-child resource updates and nodewise feasibility constraints. An equivalent full-path formulation is obtained by requiring decisions to agree across paths with the same observed history; these are the nonanticipativity constraints.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal I\) is a finite scenario tree for the exogenous information process, with each nonroot node having a unique parent.
Stage contributions, resource updates, and feasibility constraints are linear.
\(\widetilde x_{t\tau}(i)\ge0\) for every applicable stage and information node.
The scenario-tree branches have specified conditional probabilities.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The node-indexed model is a deterministic extensive-form linear program and is equivalent to the path-indexed formulation when nonanticipativity constraints are imposed.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Information-state formulation of a multistage stochastic program
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-horizon nested formulation, including the sufficiency condition for replacing history conditioning and the boundary requiring state augmentation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For stages \(\tau=t,\ldots,t+H\), decisions \(\widetilde x_{t\tau}\in\mathcal X_{t\tau}(\widetilde S_{t\tau})\) may be represented through nested maximizations and conditional expectations. If \(\widetilde I_{t\tau}\) contains the information from the observed history required by the remaining problem, conditioning on the full history at each scenario-tree node can be replaced by conditioning on \(\widetilde I_{t\tau}\). The resulting stagewise optimizer is embedded in the formulation as \[\widetilde X^{SP}_{t\tau}(\widetilde S_{t\tau})\in\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{\widetilde x_{t\tau}\in\mathcal X_{t\tau}(\widetilde S_{t\tau})}\left\{C(\widetilde S_{t\tau},\widetilde x_{t\tau})+\mathbb E[\text{downstream value}\mid\widetilde I_{t\tau}]\right\}.\] Resource states still depend on preceding decisions. The identity \(\widetilde I_{t\tau}=\widetilde W_{t\tau}\) is valid only when current exogenous information is sufficient; dynamics requiring recent history require an augmented information state.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A multistage stochastic program can be written as nested stagewise optimizations and conditional expectations. Conditioning on the full scenario-tree history may be replaced by conditioning on an information state only when that state retains all information needed by the remaining problem. The optimizers define the embedded policy, while resource states remain linked to earlier decisions. When current exogenous information is insufficient, relevant history must be added to the information state.
assumptions_latex: \(\tau\in\{t,\ldots,t+H\}\) and \(\widetilde x_{t\tau}\in\mathcal X_{t\tau}(\widetilde S_{t\tau})\).
\(\widetilde I_{t\tau}\) contains the history information required for the relevant future conditional distributions and decisions.
Interstage resource feasibility and dependence on prior decisions are retained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Full-history conditioning may be replaced by conditioning on \(\widetilde I_{t\tau}\) under the stated information-sufficiency condition; otherwise \(\widetilde I_{t\tau}\) must be augmented with relevant history.

children.title: Policy-Graph SMIP Form
children.top_down_role: Sequential formulations using reusable information states rather than a pure tree.

knowledge_statements.title: Policy-Graph SMIP Form
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recombines histories whose augmented states are sufficient for identical continuation models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be a finite directed acyclic policy graph with root \(r\). Each arc \(e=(u,v)\) has probability \(p_e\) and disturbance data \(\xi_e\). A node policy selects \(x_v\) from a mixed-integer set \(X_v(s_v)\), while arc transitions satisfy \[s_v=F_e(s_u,x_u,\xi_e).\] Multiple histories may enter the same node only when \(s_v\) is sufficient: conditional future disturbances, feasible controls, transition laws, and future costs must depend on the past solely through \((v,s_v)\). Under this condition, merging those histories preserves feasible policies and their expected costs; otherwise the graph form is merely an aggregation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A policy graph may merge histories only when its node and state retain everything relevant to future uncertainty, feasibility, transitions, and costs.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is finite and acyclic, with specified arc probabilities or conditional probabilities.
The augmented node state satisfies the stated sufficiency condition.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Sufficient-state recombination yields an exact sequential SMIP representation; insufficient recombination can change the problem.

notation.meaning: Information state at graph node v.
State transition associated with arc e.

review_flags: The supplied dynamic-programming locator may not explicitly treat policy graphs or mixed-integer recombination.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cited dynamic-programming section does not specifically support policy-graph SMIP recombination. Moreover, a single state variable at a node with multiple incoming histories requires a more precise path-dependent or state-indexed construction before exact policy preservation is reliable.

children.title: Lifted State Representation Family
children.top_down_role: Reformulations that expose discrete linking states for decomposition.

children.title: State Augmentation
children.top_down_role: Additional state components exposing interstage discrete structure.

knowledge_statements.title: State Augmentation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes when added history summaries produce a sufficient Markov state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H_t\) be the history available at stage \(t\), let \(s_t\) be the original state, and choose a measurable summary \(m_t=M_t(H_t)\). The augmented state \(z_t=(s_t,m_t)\) is sufficient when, for every admissible action \(x_t\), the conditional law of the next disturbance and all current feasibility and cost data satisfy \[\mathcal L(\xi_{t+1}\mid H_t,x_t)=\mathcal L(\xi_{t+1}\mid z_t,x_t),\] and depend on \(H_t\) only through \((z_t,x_t)\). Under this condition, policies measurable with respect to \(z_t\) attain the same feasible value as history-dependent policies.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Appending a history summary creates a sufficient state when future uncertainty, costs, and feasibility depend on the past only through that augmented state.
assumptions_latex: Histories, states, actions, and disturbances are defined on measurable spaces.
The summary \(M_t\) is measurable and available when the stage-t action is chosen.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed conditional-independence and data-sufficiency predicate permits restriction to augmented-state policies without loss.
review_flags: Direct support for the stated sufficient-state condition should be checked.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cited policy-approximation section does not directly support the stated sufficient-state theorem. The hypotheses also do not explicitly ensure that the next augmented state can be generated from the current augmented state, action, and new information, so the no-loss conclusion requires source-guided correction.

children.title: Lifted State Representations
children.top_down_role: Higher-dimensional state spaces supporting structured decomposition.

knowledge_statements.title: Lifted State Representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Adds auxiliary state coordinates and linking constraints to expose structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let an original multistage feasible set be \(F\subseteq\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb Z^q\). A lifted state representation introduces auxiliary continuous or integer variables \(z\in Z\) and constraints defining \[\widehat F=\{(x,z):G(x,z)\leq0,\ H(x,z)=0,\ x\in\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb Z^q,\ z\in Z\}.\] It is an exact lift when \(\operatorname{proj}_x(\widehat F)=F\). In a sequential model, components of \(z_t\) may store cumulative quantities, delayed decisions, logical modes, or other history summaries, but their transition and initialization constraints must ensure that every lifted trajectory projects to an original feasible trajectory and every original trajectory has a lift.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A lifted state formulation adds auxiliary state variables and linking equations. It is exact precisely when projecting its feasible trajectories recovers all and only original trajectories.
assumptions_latex: All integrality restrictions on original and auxiliary variables are retained in \(\widehat F\).
Initialization and transition constraints defining auxiliary states are included in \(G\) and \(H\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exactness requires \(\operatorname{proj}_x(\widehat F)=F\).
review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports exact lifted mixed-integer state representations.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Projection equality is the appropriate exactness criterion and the representation fits the leaf, but no source supports the lifted mixed-integer state formulation or its trajectory-level interpretation.

children.title: Projection Equivalence
children.top_down_role: Correspondence between enriched state spaces plus their original formulations.

knowledge_statements.title: Projection Equivalence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: States exact equivalence between original and lifted feasible policies after projection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be an original mixed-integer policy set and \(\widehat F\) a lifted set in variables \((x,z)\). Suppose \(\operatorname{proj}_x(\widehat F)=F\) and the lifted objective is \(\widehat f(x,z)=f(x)\). Then \[\inf_{(x,z)\in\widehat F}\widehat f(x,z)=\inf_{x\in F}f(x).\] Moreover, the projection of every lifted optimizer is an original optimizer, and every original optimizer having a feasible lift yields a lifted optimizer. This equivalence concerns the mixed-integer sets; equality can fail after continuous relaxation because generally \(\operatorname{proj}_x(\widehat F^{\mathrm{rel}})\neq F^{\mathrm{rel}}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Equal projected mixed-integer feasible sets and a projection-invariant objective give equal optimal values and corresponding optimizers, even though their continuous relaxations may differ.
assumptions_latex: \(\operatorname{proj}_x(\widehat F)=F\).
The lifted objective depends on \(x\) exactly as the original objective does.
The relevant infima are well defined.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The original and lifted mixed-integer optimization problems have equal values and optimizer correspondence under projection.

notation.meaning: Continuous relaxation of the lifted feasible set.
Continuous relaxation of the original feasible set.

review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports projection equivalence and its relaxation boundary.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The projection-based value and optimizer correspondence is mathematically standard and properly distinguishes continuous relaxations, but no source or locator supports the complete claim.

children.title: Nonconvex Integer Recourse
children.top_down_role: Nonconvex value-function behavior induced by discrete recourse.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonconvex Integer Recourse
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A one-dimensional pure-integer recourse value function exhibiting jumps and failure of convexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let the tender be \(t\in\mathbb R\) and define the pure-integer recourse value
\[
Q(t):=\min\{y:y\in\mathbb Z,\ y\ge t\}=\lceil t\rceil.
\]
This is the value function of a feasible parametric integer program. It is not convex: with \(t_1=0\), \(t_2=1/2\), and \(\lambda=1/2\), one has \(Q(\lambda t_1+(1-\lambda)t_2)=Q(1/4)=1\), whereas \(\lambda Q(t_1)+(1-\lambda)Q(t_2)=1/2\). Thus integrality alone can produce a nonconvex, discontinuous recourse value function even when the objective and recourse constraint are linear.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The integer program minimizing an integer y subject to y at least t has value ceiling(t), which is discontinuous and violates convexity.
assumptions_latex: \(t\in\mathbb R\)
\(y\in\mathbb Z\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q(t)=\lceil t\rceil\) is nonconvex and discontinuous.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: General geometry of expected integer recourse
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic regularity and nonconvexity behavior of an integer-program recourse value function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an integer-program recourse model, the expected recourse function \(\mathcal Q(x)\) is, in general, lower semicontinuous, nonconvex, and discontinuous.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The expected recourse function of an integer program is generally lower semicontinuous, nonconvex, and discontinuous.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal Q(x)\) is the expected recourse function of an integer program.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal Q\) is in general lower semicontinuous, nonconvex, and discontinuous.
