children.title: Recourse Jump Geometry
children.top_down_role: Recourse regimes separated by changes in discrete solutions.

children.title: Recourse Discontinuity Sets
children.top_down_role: Locations where integer recourse values lose continuity.

knowledge_statements.title: Recourse Discontinuity Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Discontinuities of an extended-real recourse value on its finite-valued tender domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(Q:\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) be a recourse value function and let \(F:=\{t:Q(t)<+\infty\}\). Its relative discontinuity set is
\[
D_Q:=\left\{t\in F:Q|_F\text{ is not continuous at }t\right\}.
\]
Equivalently, \(t\in D_Q\) when there exist \(\varepsilon>0\) and a sequence \((t_k)\subset F\) with \(t_k\to t\) such that \(|Q(t_k)-Q(t)|\ge\varepsilon\) for every \(k\). This relative definition separates finite-value jumps from boundaries at which recourse becomes infeasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The discontinuity set contains feasible tenders admitting nearby feasible tenders whose recourse values stay a fixed positive distance from the value at the limit.
assumptions_latex: \(Q:\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\)
\(F=\operatorname{dom}Q\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D_Q=\{t\in F:Q|_F\text{ is discontinuous at }t\}\).

notation.meaning: relative discontinuity set of the recourse value

children.title: Recourse Jump Magnitudes
children.top_down_role: Sizes of value changes across discrete-solution boundaries.

knowledge_statements.title: Recourse Jump Magnitudes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Oscillation-based jump size, applicable without selecting a direction of approach.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a locally bounded recourse value \(Q:F\to\mathbb R\) on \(F\subseteq\mathbb R^m\), define its jump magnitude at \(t\in F\) by
\[
J_Q(t):=\lim_{r\downarrow0}\left(\sup_{u\in F\cap B_r(t)}Q(u)-\inf_{u\in F\cap B_r(t)}Q(u)\right).
\]
The limit exists in \([0,+\infty]\) because the displayed oscillations are nonincreasing as \(r\downarrow0\). Moreover, \(Q\) is continuous at \(t\), relative to \(F\), exactly when \(J_Q(t)=0\); consequently \(J_Q(t)>0\) measures a nonvanishing local recourse jump.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Jump magnitude is the limiting local range of recourse values. It is zero exactly at relative continuity points and positive at persistent jumps.
assumptions_latex: \(F\subseteq\mathbb R^m\)
\(Q:F\to\mathbb R\) is locally bounded
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q\text{ is continuous at }t\text{ relative to }F\iff J_Q(t)=0\).

notation.meaning: open radius-r ball centered at the tender t

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The oscillation formula and its continuity characterization are mathematically standard, but the record supplies no evidence for adopting this particular nondirectional quantity as a recourse jump magnitude.

children.title: Discrete-Regime Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Geometric interfaces separating distinct integer recourse solutions.

knowledge_statements.title: Discrete-Regime Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundaries where locally optimal integer recourse patterns cease to remain constant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider \(Q(t):=\inf\{q^{\mathsf T}y:(y,z)\in Y(t),\ z\in\mathbb Z^p\}\), and let
\[
R(t):=\left\{z\in\mathbb Z^p:\exists y\text{ such that }(y,z)\in Y(t)\text{ and }q^{\mathsf T}y=Q(t)\right\}.
\]
On the set \(F\) where the infimum is finite and attained, the discrete-regime boundary is
\[
\mathcal B_R:=\{t\in F:\text{no relative neighborhood of }t\text{ has constant }R(\cdot)\}.
\]
Thus every neighborhood of a boundary tender contains tenders having different sets of optimal integer patterns.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A discrete-regime boundary is a feasible tender around which the set of optimal integer recourse patterns cannot remain locally constant.
assumptions_latex: \(Q(t)\) is finite and attained for every \(t\in F\)
\(z\in\mathbb Z^p\) indexes the discrete recourse pattern
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(t\in\mathcal B_R\iff R(\cdot)\text{ is not locally constant at }t\text{ relative to }F\).

notation.meaning: set of optimal integer patterns at tender t

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proposed optimal-pattern boundary is plausible but specialized and unsupported. The spaces and dimensions of y, q, and Y(t) are also not fully introduced, so the precise intended formulation cannot be established without a source.

children.title: Piecewise Polyhedral Recourse Structure
children.top_down_role: Local polyhedral organizations induced by parametric mixed-integer subproblems.

knowledge_statements.title: Piecewise Polyhedral Recourse Structure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite local representation by polyhedral value pieces under bounded integer-pattern activity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(U\subseteq\mathbb R^m\) be polyhedral. Suppose only finitely many integer patterns \(z^1,\ldots,z^N\) can be optimal on \(U\), and fixing \(z^i\) leaves a feasible, bounded parametric linear program with polyhedral value function \(\phi_i\) on a polyhedron \(P_i\). Then
\[
Q(t)=\min_{i:\,t\in P_i}\phi_i(t),\qquad t\in U,
\]
with the minimum of the empty family interpreted as \(+\infty\). Hence \(U\) admits a finite polyhedral refinement on whose cells each \(\phi_i\) is affine, while \(Q\) is the pointwise lower envelope of the active affine pieces and need not be convex.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With finitely many relevant integer patterns, recourse is locally the minimum of finitely many polyhedral linear-program value functions and is affine on a refined partition.
assumptions_latex: \(U\subseteq\mathbb R^m\) is polyhedral
Only finitely many integer patterns can be optimal on \(U\)
Each fixed-pattern subproblem is a feasible bounded parametric linear program on its domain
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q(t)=\min_{i:t\in P_i}\phi_i(t)\) on \(U\), with a finite piecewise-affine refinement.

notation.meaning: tenders feasible for integer pattern i

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite lower-envelope representation fits the leaf, but the cited broad recourse and discrete-optimization sections do not inspectably support the asserted finite polyhedral refinement. Source confirmation is needed for the parametric and finite-pattern hypotheses.

children.title: Closed Recourse Representation Family
children.top_down_role: Closed representations used at discontinuous recourse boundaries.

children.title: Lower-Semicontinuous Recourse
children.top_down_role: Integer recourse value functions with lower-semicontinuous boundary behavior.

knowledge_statements.title: Lower-Semicontinuous Recourse
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential lower semicontinuity for an extended-real recourse value function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A recourse value function \(Q:\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) is lower semicontinuous at \(t\in\mathbb R^m\) when
\[
Q(t)\le\liminf_{k\to\infty}Q(t_k)
\]
for every sequence \((t_k)\subseteq\mathbb R^m\) satisfying \(t_k\to t\). It is lower semicontinuous when this condition holds at every tender. Equivalently, every sublevel set \(\{t:Q(t)\le\alpha\}\) is closed for \(\alpha\in\mathbb R\), or, equivalently, its epigraph \(\{(t,r):r\ge Q(t)\}\) is closed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Recourse is lower semicontinuous when its value at every limiting tender does not exceed the limit inferior of nearby recourse values.
assumptions_latex: \(Q:\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q\text{ is lower semicontinuous}\iff\operatorname{epi}Q\text{ is closed}\).

notation.meaning: epigraph of the recourse value function

children.title: Closed Recourse Representations
children.top_down_role: Closed formulations of recourse behavior at discontinuity boundaries.

knowledge_statements.title: Closed Recourse Representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Epigraph representation of a proper closed recourse value function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(Q:\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) be proper, and set \(E:=\operatorname{epi}Q\). If \(Q\) is lower semicontinuous, then \(E\subseteq\mathbb R^{m+1}\) is closed, is upward closed in its last coordinate, and
\[
Q(t)=\inf\{r\in\mathbb R:(t,r)\in E\},
\]
where the infimum of the empty set is \(+\infty\). Conversely, any nonempty closed set \(E\) satisfying \((t,r)\in E\Rightarrow(t,s)\in E\) for every \(s\ge r\), and containing no complete vertical line, defines a proper lower-semicontinuous function by this formula.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Proper lower-semicontinuous recourse functions correspond to closed upward-closed epigraphs, and the function is recovered as each vertical section's lowest height.
assumptions_latex: \(Q:\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) is proper
\(E=\operatorname{epi}Q\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q(t)=\inf\{r:(t,r)\in E\}\), and closed upward epigraphs represent proper lower-semicontinuous functions.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The epigraph representation is mathematically plausible and correctly classified, but no source is supplied for the converse characterization and its properness conditions.

children.title: Boundary Closure Effects
children.top_down_role: Changes induced by closure at discrete recourse boundaries.

knowledge_statements.title: Boundary Closure Effects
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Effect of epigraph closure on recourse values at regime and feasibility boundaries.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(Q:\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) be proper and bounded below on a neighborhood of every point in its domain. Define
\[
Q^{\mathrm{cl}}(t):=\liminf_{u\to t}Q(u).
\]
Then
\[
\operatorname{epi}Q^{\mathrm{cl}}=\operatorname{cl}(\operatorname{epi}Q),
\]
and \(Q^{\mathrm{cl}}\le Q\). Thus closing a recourse epigraph leaves every lower-semicontinuity point unchanged but replaces any nonclosed boundary value by the smallest value supported by nearby epigraph points. In particular, \(Q^{\mathrm{cl}}=Q\) everywhere exactly when \(Q\) is lower semicontinuous.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Closing the recourse epigraph produces the lower-semicontinuous envelope, changing only boundary values unsupported by nearby feasible epigraph points.
assumptions_latex: \(Q:\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) is proper
\(Q\) is locally bounded below on its domain
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{epi}Q^{\mathrm{cl}}=\operatorname{cl}(\operatorname{epi}Q)\) and \(Q^{\mathrm{cl}}=Q\iff Q\) is lower semicontinuous.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The stated local lower-bound assumption only applies near points of dom Q and does not prevent Q from tending to minus infinity near a point outside its domain. Consequently the liminf envelope may take minus infinity and the asserted epigraph-closure identity is not secured in the declared codomain. A source is needed to determine the correct hypotheses.

children.title: Tender-Space Geometry
children.top_down_role: Analysis in the image through which first-stage decisions affect recourse.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: Section 7.3(a), Looking in the Space of Tenders

children.title: Tender-Space Partitions
children.top_down_role: Regions sharing recourse combinatorics or value-function behavior.

knowledge_statements.title: Tender-Space Partitions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Partition of tender space into regions having invariant recourse combinatorics and value formulas.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F\subseteq\mathbb R^m\) be the feasible tender domain and let \(R(t)\) denote recourse-regime data, such as the active integer patterns and active linear constraints at \(t\). A tender-space partition subordinate to \(R\) is a locally finite family \(\mathcal P=\{C_j\}_{j\in J}\) of pairwise disjoint sets satisfying
\[
F=\bigcup_{j\in J}C_j,
\]
such that \(R(t)\) is constant on the relative interior of each \(C_j\). For a polyhedral recourse partition, every \(C_j\) is polyhedral and the restriction of \(Q\) to each cell is given by a fixed polyhedral value formula.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A tender-space partition divides feasible tenders into disjoint, locally finite cells sharing the same recourse regime and, in the polyhedral case, one value formula.
assumptions_latex: \(F\subseteq\mathbb R^m\) is the feasible tender domain
\(R(t)\) records specified recourse-regime data
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F=\bigcup_{j\in J}C_j\) with \(R(\cdot)\) constant on each \(\operatorname{ri}C_j\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: This is a plausible tender-space construction, but the locally finite disjoint-cell convention and the requirement imposed only on relative interiors are specialized choices with no cited support.

children.title: Integer-Lattice Interactions
children.top_down_role: Interactions between tender values, lattice structure, and discontinuities.

knowledge_statements.title: Integer-Lattice Interactions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recourse represented by continuous residual problems indexed by integer lattice shifts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(W_I\in\mathbb R^{m\times p}\), \(W_C\in\mathbb R^{m\times q}\), \(c_I\in\mathbb R^p\), and \(c_C\in\mathbb R^q\). With \(z\in\mathbb Z^p\) and \(y\in\mathbb R_+^q\), define
\[
Q(t):=\inf\{c_I^{\mathsf T}z+c_C^{\mathsf T}y:W_Iz+W_Cy=t,\ z\in\mathbb Z^p,\ y\in\mathbb R_+^q\}.
\]
If
\[
\phi(s):=\inf\{c_C^{\mathsf T}y:W_Cy=s,\ y\in\mathbb R_+^q\},
\]
with the value \(+\infty\) assigned to an empty feasible set, then
\[
Q(t)=\inf_{z\in\mathbb Z^p}\bigl(c_I^{\mathsf T}z+\phi(t-W_Iz)\bigr).
\]
Hence the continuous residual recourse geometry is translated by the additive set \(W_I\mathbb Z^p\); changes in the minimizing translate can generate lattice-dependent regime boundaries and jumps.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Mixed-integer recourse is the lower envelope of continuous residual recourse values translated by integer-generated tender shifts, linking changes of minimizing lattice translate to regime boundaries and possible jumps.
assumptions_latex: \(W_I\in\mathbb R^{m\times p}\) and \(W_C\in\mathbb R^{m\times q}\)
\(c_I\in\mathbb R^p\) and \(c_C\in\mathbb R^q\)
\(z\in\mathbb Z^p\) and \(y\in\mathbb R_+^q\)
Empty feasible sets have value \(+\infty\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q(t)=\inf_{z\in\mathbb Z^p}\{c_I^{\mathsf T}z+\phi(t-W_Iz)\}\).

notation.meaning: integer-generated additive set in tender space

children.title: First-Stage-Dependent Recourse Disjunctions
children.top_down_role: Changes in recourse disjunctions induced by master decisions.

knowledge_statements.title: First-Stage-Dependent Recourse Disjunctions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pullback of tender-space recourse regimes through the first-stage tender map.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), \(h\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(T\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), and define the tender map \(t(x):=h-Tx\) for \(x\in X\). Let \(K\) be an index set and suppose recourse has the disjunctive representation
\[
Q(t)=\inf_{k:\,t\in P_k}\phi_k(t),
\]
where \(P_k\subseteq\mathbb R^m\), with an empty infimum interpreted as \(+\infty\). Define
\[
X_k:=\{x\in X:h-Tx\in P_k\}.
\]
Then
\[
Q(h-Tx)=\inf_{k:\,x\in X_k}\phi_k(h-Tx).
\]
Consequently, movement of \(x\) across affine preimages of regime boundaries may change the feasible or optimal recourse disjunctions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Composing recourse regimes with the tender map pulls each regime back to first-stage space; crossing a pulled-back boundary may change the feasible or optimal recourse disjunction.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), \(h\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(T\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\)
\(t(x)=h-Tx\) for \(x\in X\)
\(Q(t)=\inf_{k:t\in P_k}\phi_k(t)\)
The infimum of an empty family is \(+\infty\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q(h-Tx)=\inf_{k:x\in X_k}\phi_k(h-Tx)\), where \(X_k=X\cap\{x:h-Tx\in P_k\}\).

notation.meaning: tender-space domain of recourse regime k

children.title: Recourse Feasibility Regimes
children.top_down_role: Regimes distinguished by availability of feasible discrete corrective actions.

children.title: Complete Integer Recourse
children.top_down_role: Integer correction available throughout the relevant tender space.

knowledge_statements.title: Complete Integer Recourse
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasibility of integer-constrained corrective actions for every tender in the prescribed space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(W\in\mathbb R^{m\times q}\), let \(Y:=\mathbb Z_+^p\times\mathbb R_+^{q-p}\), and let \(\mathcal T\subseteq\mathbb R^m\) be the prescribed tender space. The system has complete integer recourse on \(\mathcal T\) when
\[
\forall t\in\mathcal T\;\exists y\in Y\quad Wy=t.
\]
Equivalently, \(\mathcal T\subseteq W(Y):=\{Wy:y\in Y\}\), so the integer-restricted second stage is feasible for every prescribed tender. When \(\mathcal T=\mathbb R^m\), this is global complete integer recourse; restricting tenders to those generated by admissible first-stage decisions instead yields a relative completeness condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Complete integer recourse means that every prescribed tender can be matched by a feasible nonnegative recourse vector having the required integer components.
assumptions_latex: \(W\in\mathbb R^{m\times q}\)
\(Y=\mathbb Z_+^p\times\mathbb R_+^{q-p}\)
\(\mathcal T\subseteq\mathbb R^m\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal T\subseteq W(Y)\).

children.title: Relatively Complete Integer Recourse
children.top_down_role: Integer correction available for tenders generated by admissible first-stage decisions.

knowledge_statements.title: Relatively Complete Integer Recourse
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-stage mixed-integer recourse relative to the admissible first-stage set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((\Xi,\mathcal F,P)\) be a probability space, let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^{n_1}\times\mathbb Z^{n_2}\) be the nonempty admissible first-stage set, and let measurable maps \(W:\Xi\to\mathbb R^{r\times m}\), \(T:\Xi\to\mathbb R^{r\times(n_1+n_2)}\), and \(h:\Xi\to\mathbb R^r\) define \[Y(x,\xi)=\{y\in\mathbb R^{m_1}\times\mathbb Z^{m_2}:W(\xi)y=h(\xi)-T(\xi)x,\ y\ge 0\},\qquad m=m_1+m_2.\] The model has relatively complete integer recourse if \[P\bigl(\{\xi\in\Xi:Y(x,\xi)\ne\varnothing\}\bigr)=1\qquad\text{for every }x\in X.\] Thus every tender generated by an admissible first-stage decision admits an integer-feasible correction almost surely, although arbitrary tenders outside those generated by \(X\) need not be correctable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every admissible first-stage decision has a feasible mixed-integer recourse action with probability one; feasibility need not hold for arbitrary right-hand sides.
assumptions_latex: \((\Xi,\mathcal F,P)\) is a probability space.
\(X\ne\varnothing\).
The recourse-data maps are measurable and dimensionally compatible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P(\{\xi\in\Xi:Y(x,\xi)\ne\varnothing\})=1\) for every \(x\in X\).

notation.meaning: probability law on the uncertainty space

review_flags: integer-recourse specialization should be checked against source terminology

children.title: Incomplete Integer Recourse
children.top_down_role: Models requiring explicit detection and exclusion of recourse-infeasible decisions.

knowledge_statements.title: Incomplete Integer Recourse
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of relative completeness for mixed-integer second-stage decisions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((\Xi,\mathcal F,P)\) be a probability space, let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^{n_1}\times\mathbb Z^{n_2}\) be a nonempty admissible first-stage set, and let \(Y(x,\xi)\subseteq\mathbb R^{m_1}\times\mathbb Z^{m_2}\) denote the mixed-integer recourse-feasible set at \((x,\xi)\). Integer recourse is incomplete relative to \(X\) when \[\text{there exists }x\in X\text{ such that }P\bigl(\{\xi\in\Xi:Y(x,\xi)=\varnothing\}\bigr)>0.\] Equivalently, at least one admissible first-stage decision produces an integer-infeasible recourse system with positive probability. If an extended recourse value is assigned \(+\infty\) on infeasible realizations, such realizations must be detected, penalized, or excluded in a well-posed formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Integer recourse is incomplete when some admissible first-stage decision lacks an integer-feasible correction on an event of positive probability.
assumptions_latex: \((\Xi,\mathcal F,P)\) is a probability space.
\(X\ne\varnothing\).
For every \(x\in X\), the event \(\{\xi:Y(x,\xi)=\varnothing\}\) is measurable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists x\in X\) such that \(P(\{\xi\in\Xi:Y(x,\xi)=\varnothing\})>0\).

notation.meaning: probability law on the uncertainty space

review_flags: integer-recourse specialization should be checked against source terminology

children.title: Distributional Regularization Stability
children.top_down_role: Regularity and perturbation behavior of expected integer recourse.

children.title: Regularization by Expectation
children.top_down_role: Smoothing phenomena arising from aggregation over uncertain data.

knowledge_statements.title: Regularization by Expectation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Continuity obtained by averaging scenario-wise integer-recourse values.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be a metric space and \(Q:X\times\Xi\to\mathbb{R}\) be measurable in its second argument. Fix \(x\in X\). If every sequence \(x_k\to x\) satisfies \(Q(x_k,\xi)\to Q(x,\xi)\) for \(P\)-almost every \(\xi\), and there is an integrable random variable \(G\) with \(|Q(x_k,\xi)|\le G(\xi)\) for all \(k\), then \[\mathcal Q(x_k):=\mathbb E_P[Q(x_k,\xi)]\longrightarrow\mathcal Q(x).\] Hence expectation can yield a continuous expected-recourse function even when exceptional scenario-wise discontinuities occur on null sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Almost-sure scenario continuity plus an integrable envelope makes expected integer-recourse cost continuous by dominated convergence.
assumptions_latex: \(Q(x_k,\xi)\to Q(x,\xi)\) for \(P\)-almost every \(\xi\).
\(|Q(x_k,\xi)|\le G(\xi)\) with \(G\in L^1(P)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E_P[Q(x_k,\xi)]\to\mathbb E_P[Q(x,\xi)]\).
review_flags: stated version follows dominated convergence rather than a sharper distributional smoothing theorem

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The dominated-convergence statement is mathematically plausible and the property kind fits, but no inspectable source supports its placement as an integer-recourse regularization result.

children.title: Probability-Law Perturbation Stability
children.top_down_role: Stability families for integer recourse under distributional change.

knowledge_statements.title: Probability-Law Perturbation Stability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Wasserstein stability of expected recourse and optimal values.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be compact, and suppose \(Q(x,\cdot)\) is \(L\)-Lipschitz under metric \(d\), uniformly over \(x\in X\). For probability laws \(P\) and \(P'\) having finite first moments, define \(F_P(x)=c^\top x+\int Q(x,\xi)\,P(d\xi)\). Then \[\sup_{x\in X}|F_P(x)-F_{P'}(x)|\le L W_1(P,P'),\qquad |v(P)-v(P')|\le L W_1(P,P'),\] where \(v(P)=\min_{x\in X}F_P(x)\). If \(P_k\to P\) in \(W_1\), every cluster point of minimizers of \(F_{P_k}\) minimizes \(F_P\), provided \(F_P\) is lower semicontinuous.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform Lipschitz dependence on uncertainty bounds objective and optimal-value changes by the Wasserstein distance and yields outer stability of minimizers.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is compact and \(F_P\) is lower semicontinuous.
\(|Q(x,\xi)-Q(x,\xi')|\le Ld(\xi,\xi')\) uniformly in \(x\).
\(P\) and \(P'\) have finite first moments.

notation.meaning: first Wasserstein distance induced by the uncertainty metric

review_flags: integer-recourse hypotheses may require a specialized modulus

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The Lipschitz Wasserstein bounds are standard, but the integer-recourse hypotheses and minimizer-stability formulation lack a source. The Euclidean domain required by \(c^\top x\) should also be made explicit once a supported version is identified.

children.title: Empirical-Measure Stability
children.top_down_role: Stability routes connecting integer recourse to sampled probability models.

knowledge_statements.title: Empirical-Measure Stability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consistency under uniform convergence of sample-average recourse objectives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be compact, let \(\xi_1,\xi_2,\ldots\) be independent with law \(P\), and set \(P_N=N^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^N\delta_{\xi_i}\). Define \(F_N(x)=c^\top x+N^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^NQ(x,\xi_i)\) and \(F(x)=c^\top x+\mathbb E_P[Q(x,\xi)]\). If \[\sup_{x\in X}|F_N(x)-F(x)|\longrightarrow0\quad\text{almost surely},\] then the optimal values satisfy \(v_N\to v\) almost surely. Moreover, every cluster point of exact minimizers \(x_N\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}F_N(x)\) belongs to \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}F(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A uniform almost-sure law of large numbers gives convergence of sample-average optimal values and cluster-point consistency of empirical minimizers.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is compact.
\(F_N\to F\) uniformly almost surely.
Exact minimizers exist for every \(N\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v_N\to v\) almost surely, and every cluster point of \(x_N\) minimizes \(F\).
review_flags: integer-recourse measurability conditions require source confirmation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Uniform convergence gives optimal-value convergence, but cluster-point consistency additionally needs an appropriate lower-semicontinuity or closed-argmin hypothesis for \(F\). An authoritative consistency result is needed before fixing the theorem.

children.title: SMIP Relaxation-Convexification-Cut Taxonomy
children.top_down_role: Lower-bounding representations and valid-inequality families for stochastic integer structure.

children.title: Integrality Relaxation Hierarchy
children.top_down_role: Baseline relaxations obtained by removing all or selected integrality restrictions.

children.title: Recourse LP Relaxation
children.top_down_role: Continuous relaxation of discrete recourse decisions.

knowledge_statements.title: Recourse LP Relaxation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scenario-wise relaxation of second-stage integrality only.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(x\in X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) and \(\xi\in\Xi\). Let \(q(\xi)\in\mathbb R^m\), \(W(\xi)\in\mathbb R^{r\times m}\), \(h(\xi)\in\mathbb R^r\), \(T(\xi)\in\mathbb R^{r\times n}\), and let \(I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,m\}\) index the integer recourse variables. Define \[Q(x,\xi)=\inf\{q(\xi)^\top y:W(\xi)y=h(\xi)-T(\xi)x,\ y\in\mathbb R_+^m,\ y_j\in\mathbb Z\text{ for }j\in I\}.\] Its recourse LP relaxation is \[Q_{\mathrm{LP}}(x,\xi)=\inf\{q(\xi)^\top y:W(\xi)y=h(\xi)-T(\xi)x,\ y\in\mathbb R_+^m\},\] obtained by dropping all second-stage integrality restrictions while retaining the first-stage domain. In the extended-real ordering, \(Q_{\mathrm{LP}}(x,\xi)\le Q(x,\xi)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Drop every second-stage integrality restriction while retaining the recourse constraints and original first-stage domain; for minimization, the relaxed value is a lower bound on the mixed-integer recourse value.
assumptions_latex: The recourse problem is a minimization problem.
The data have the displayed compatible dimensions.
Both values are interpreted in the extended-real sense.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q_{\mathrm{LP}}(x,\xi)\le Q(x,\xi)\).
review_flags: locator may cover recourse models without explicit mixed-integer relaxation

children.title: Extensive-Form LP Relaxation
children.top_down_role: Global continuous relaxation of the scenario-expanded model.

knowledge_statements.title: Extensive-Form LP Relaxation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Continuous relaxation of every integer variable in a finite-scenario extensive form.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For scenarios \(s=1,\ldots,S\) with probabilities \(p_s\), consider the extensive form \[\min\left\{c^\top x+\sum_{s=1}^Sp_s q_s^\top y_s:Ax\ge b,\ W_sy_s=h_s-T_sx,\ x\in X_I,\ y_s\in Y_{I,s}\right\}.\] Its extensive-form LP relaxation replaces all integrality restrictions in \(X_I\) and every \(Y_{I,s}\) by their continuous linear relaxations, while preserving the shared variable \(x\) and hence nonanticipativity. For minimization, its optimal value is no greater than the mixed-integer extensive-form optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Relax every first- and second-stage integer variable in the finite-scenario deterministic equivalent while retaining scenario coupling and nonanticipativity.
assumptions_latex: The scenario set is finite.
All remaining constraints and objectives are linear.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v_{\mathrm{EF\text{-}LP}}\le v_{\mathrm{EF\text{-}MIP}}\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the terminal container and its bound is standard, but no source with a specific locator is supplied for the finite-scenario extensive-form LP relaxation.

children.title: Selective Integrality Relaxation
children.top_down_role: Relaxations preserving selected discrete state or decision structures.

knowledge_statements.title: Selective Integrality Relaxation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Partial relaxation indexed by a chosen subset of discrete variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(z\in\mathbb R^n\) satisfy a linear system \(Az\ge b\), and let \(I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\) index variables required to be integer in the original stochastic extensive form. For a retained subset \(J\subseteq I\), the selective integrality relaxation has feasible set \[R_J=\{z:Az\ge b,\ z_j\in\mathbb Z\text{ for }j\in J\},\] with variables indexed by \(I\setminus J\) made continuous. If \(J_1\subseteq J_2\subseteq I\), then \(R_I\subseteq R_{J_2}\subseteq R_{J_1}\subseteq R_\varnothing\); consequently, minimization bounds increase monotonically as integrality is restored.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Retain integrality only for a selected variable subset. Larger retained subsets yield tighter feasible sets and monotonically stronger minimization bounds.
assumptions_latex: The same linear constraints and objective are used for every retained subset.
The problem is a minimization problem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(J_1\subseteq J_2\Rightarrow R_{J_2}\subseteq R_{J_1}\) and \(v_{J_1}\le v_{J_2}\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The selective-relaxation definition and nesting relation are precise, but the record has no inspectable citation supporting this hierarchy in the SMIP setting.

children.title: Benders-Type Cut Families
children.top_down_role: Master inequalities derived from continuous, discrete, or hybrid recourse information.

children.title: Classical Recourse Cuts
children.top_down_role: Continuous-relaxation feasibility and optimality cut families used in SMIP.

knowledge_statements.title: Classical Recourse Cuts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Benders feasibility and optimality cuts derived from continuous recourse duality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), consider \[Q_{\mathrm{LP}}(x)=\inf\{q^\top y:Wy=h-Tx,\ y\in\mathbb R_+^m\},\] where \(q\in\mathbb R^m\), \(W\in\mathbb R^{r\times m}\), \(h\in\mathbb R^r\), and \(T\in\mathbb R^{r\times n}\). Let \(D=\{\pi\in\mathbb R^r:W^\top\pi\le q\}\). Every \(\pi\in D\) gives the valid optimality cut \[\theta\ge\pi^\top(h-Tx).\] Every \(r\in\mathbb R^r\) satisfying \(W^\top r\le0\) gives the necessary feasibility inequality \[r^\top(h-Tx)\le0.\] When the recourse LP is feasible and has a finite optimum, strong duality gives \(Q_{\mathrm{LP}}(x)=\sup_{\pi\in D}\pi^\top(h-Tx)\). A violated feasibility inequality certifies infeasibility of the recourse equations with \(y\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dual-feasible points produce optimality cuts, while dual recession directions produce feasibility inequalities for the continuous recourse relaxation.
assumptions_latex: The recourse subproblem is a linear program with the displayed compatible dimensions.
Strong LP duality applies when the recourse problem is feasible with finite optimum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\theta\ge\pi^\top(h-Tx)\) is valid for every \(\pi\in D\), and \(r^\top(h-Tx)\le0\) is necessary for feasibility for every \(r\) with \(W^\top r\le0\).

notation.meaning: dual-feasible set of the recourse LP

review_flags: sign conventions should be checked against the cited formulation

children.title: Laporte–Louveaux Integer Optimality Cuts
children.top_down_role: Integer-master cuts based on evaluated recourse at discrete decisions.

knowledge_statements.title: Laporte–Louveaux Integer Optimality Cuts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Integer L-shaped optimality cut for a binary master incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\{0,1\}^n\), let \(Q(x)\ge L\) for every \(x\in X\), and suppose \(Q(\bar x)\) has been evaluated at \(\bar x\in X\). Define the Hamming expression \[d_{\bar x}(x)=\sum_{i:\bar x_i=1}(1-x_i)+\sum_{i:\bar x_i=0}x_i.\] Then the Laporte–Louveaux integer optimality cut \[\theta\ge Q(\bar x)-\bigl(Q(\bar x)-L\bigr)d_{\bar x}(x)\] is valid for all \(x\in X\) whenever \(\theta\ge Q(x)\) is required. It is exact at \(\bar x\), while at every other binary point its right-hand side does not exceed \(L\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An evaluated binary incumbent and a global recourse lower bound yield a valid cut exact at that incumbent and harmless elsewhere.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\{0,1\}^n\).
\(L\le Q(x)\) for every \(x\in X\).
\(Q(\bar x)\) is finite and exactly evaluated.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\theta\ge Q(\bar x)-(Q(\bar x)-L)d_{\bar x}(x)\) is valid and exact at \(\bar x\).

notation.meaning: global lower bound on recourse value

review_flags: cut variant and naming require source confirmation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed binary Hamming cut is mathematically valid under the stated global lower bound, and certificate is an appropriate kind, but the Laporte–Louveaux attribution and exact variant require a primary-source locator.

children.title: Integer Recourse Feasibility Cuts
children.top_down_role: Cuts excluding decisions without feasible integer recourse.

knowledge_statements.title: Integer Recourse Feasibility Cuts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Binary no-good certificate excluding an integer-recourse-infeasible incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\{0,1\}^n\), and suppose the integer recourse system is infeasible at \(\bar x\in X\). The no-good feasibility cut \[\sum_{i:\bar x_i=1}(1-x_i)+\sum_{i:\bar x_i=0}x_i\ge1\] is satisfied by every binary vector except \(\bar x\). Consequently, adding it to the master problem removes the certified recourse-infeasible decision without excluding any other binary first-stage decision. Repeating this construction yields an exact finite exclusion scheme when \(X\) is finite, although it need not provide a strong description of the recourse-feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A binary no-good inequality excludes exactly one incumbent whose integer recourse has been certified infeasible, preserving every other binary decision.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\{0,1\}^n\).
Integer recourse at \(\bar x\) has been certified infeasible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed inequality excludes \(\bar x\) and no other binary vector.
review_flags: locator may discuss LP feasibility cuts rather than binary integer-recourse no-good cuts

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The no-good inequality correctly excludes exactly the binary incumbent, but the cited section appears to concern classical LP feasibility cuts rather than integer-recourse no-good cuts. A supporting locator is required.

children.title: Integrality-Strengthened Benders Cuts
children.top_down_role: Benders cut families strengthened with mixed-integer subproblem information.

knowledge_statements.title: Integrality-Strengthened Benders Cuts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Master inequalities valid for the integer-recourse epigraph and stronger than LP-dual cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be the discrete master domain and \(E_I=\{(x,\theta):x\in X,\ \theta\ge Q(x)\}\) the mixed-integer recourse epigraph. An integrality-strengthened Benders cut is an inequality \(\theta\ge\alpha+\beta^\top x\) valid for \(E_I\) whose right-hand side dominates a classical LP-recourse cut \(\theta\ge a+b^\top x\) on \(X\): \[\alpha+\beta^\top x\ge a+b^\top x\quad\text{for every }x\in X,\] with strict inequality for at least one \(x\in X\). Such a cut may use integer-subproblem values, disjunctions, or valid inequalities unavailable from the continuous recourse dual alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: These cuts remain valid for the integer-recourse epigraph and dominate a classical LP-based Benders cut somewhere on the discrete master domain.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is the intended discrete master domain.
Both compared inequalities are valid on their stated epigraphs.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The strengthened cut dominates the classical cut on \(X\), strictly at some \(x\in X\).

notation.meaning: mixed-integer recourse epigraph over the master domain
coefficients of a classical LP-recourse cut

review_flags: definition captures dominance but not a unique construction

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The dominance condition is coherent, but it does not establish an authoritative or unique definition of the integrality-strengthened Benders-cut family. A source is needed to fix the intended taxonomy and mathematical scope.

children.title: Parametric Cutting-Plane Families
children.top_down_role: Scenario cuts whose coefficients depend parametrically on first-stage decisions.

children.title: Affine Parametric Cuts
children.top_down_role: Parametric cuts preserving a polyhedral master approximation.

assumptions_latex: For every parameter \(x\in X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\), the relevant recourse epigraph is a set \(E(x)\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{m+1}\).
The coefficient maps are affine and the inequality is valid for every feasible parameter-recourse pair.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(E(x)\subseteq\{(y,\theta):a_0+A x+b^{\mathsf T}y+\beta\theta\geq 0\}\) for every \(x\in X\).

notation.meaning: Scenario recourse epigraph at parameter x

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines globally valid affine inequalities for a parameterized recourse epigraph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
An affine parametric cut for \(E(\cdot)\) is specified by \((a_0,A,b,\beta)\) such that
\[
a_0+A x+b^{\mathsf T}y+\beta\theta\geq 0
\]
holds for every \(x\in X\) and every \((y,\theta)\in E(x)\). For any finite collection of such cuts, their simultaneous imposition gives a polyhedron in \((x,y,\theta)\). Hence adding finitely many affine parametric cuts to a polyhedral master preserves its polyhedral form while providing an outer approximation of the parameterized recourse epigraph.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An affine parametric cut is valid for every parameterized recourse epigraph and remains a linear master constraint when first-stage variables are retained explicitly.
knowledge_statements.title: Affine Parametric Cuts

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition broadly fits the leaf, but no cited source supports the global parameter domain or outer-approximation claim. The dimensions of a0, A, b, and beta also need explicit specification, and the plain statement omits the finite-cut polyhedral-preservation claim.

children.title: Parametric Gomory Cuts
children.top_down_role: Gomory-derived cut families adapted to decision-dependent recourse sets.

assumptions_latex: Fix \(x\in X\) and a tableau row \(z_B=b(x)-\sum_{j\in N}a_j(x)z_j\) with \(z_B,z_j\in\mathbb{Z}_+\).
On a parameter cell \(P\subseteq X\), the relevant floors of \(b(x)\) and \(a_j(x)\) are constant and \(0<f_0(x)<1\), where \(f_0(x)=b(x)-\lfloor b(x)\rfloor\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_{j\in N}f_j(x)z_j\geq f_0(x)\) is valid for every integer tableau solution and every \(x\in P\), where \(f_j(x)=a_j(x)-\lfloor a_j(x)\rfloor\).

notation.meaning: Integer basic and nonbasic tableau variables
Fractional parts of the parameterized tableau coefficients
Parameter cell with fixed coefficient floors

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pure-integer Gomory form on parameter cells having fixed coefficient floors.

source_refs.locator: 3.5 Cutting Plane Method for the Solution of the All Integer Variable Linear Programming Problem p. 76

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For each \(x\in P\), taking fractional parts of the integer tableau row gives
\[
\sum_{j\in N} f_j(x)z_j\geq f_0(x).
\]
Indeed, the row identity implies that \(\sum_{j\in N}a_j(x)z_j-b(x)\) is integral, while all \(z_j\) are nonnegative integers. Because the floors are fixed on \(P\), the functions \(f_j(\cdot)\) and \(f_0(\cdot)\) are affine there. The collection indexed by the parameter cells is the corresponding parametric Gomory-cut family.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Gomory fractional inequality is generated at each first-stage parameter, with a piecewise-affine coefficient description on cells where tableau-coefficient floors remain fixed.
knowledge_statements.title: Parametric Gomory Cuts

source_witnesses.locator: 3.5 Cutting Plane Method for the Solution of the All Integer Variable Linear Programming Problem p. 76

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cited section supports ordinary all-integer Gomory cutting planes but does not establish the parameter-cell extension. Fixed floors alone do not make the fractional-part functions affine unless the tableau coefficient functions are affine on the cell. The statement also contains proof text, which must be removed once an authoritative source establishes the parametric version.

children.title: Parametric Disjunctive Cuts
children.top_down_role: Disjunctive separation families retaining first-stage dependence.

assumptions_latex: For each \(x\in X\), the recourse set satisfies \(F(x)\subseteq\bigcup_{k=1}^K P_k(x)\), where every \(P_k(x)\) is polyhedral.
For each branch, \(P_k(x)=\{y:A_k y\geq b_k-B_kx\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every inequality valid for \(\operatorname{conv}(\bigcup_{k=1}^K P_k(x))\) is valid for \(F(x)\), and retaining \(x\) yields a parametric disjunctive cut.

notation.meaning: Polyhedral terms of the recourse disjunction

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite polyhedral recourse disjunctions with explicit first-stage dependence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Introduce variables \(\lambda_k\geq0\) and \(y^k\) satisfying
\[
\sum_{k=1}^K\lambda_k=1,\qquad y=\sum_{k=1}^K y^k,\qquad A_k y^k\geq\lambda_k(b_k-B_kx).
\]
The projection of this extended system onto \((x,y)\), with \(x\) fixed, is \(\operatorname{conv}(\bigcup_{k=1}^K P_k(x))\) under the usual recession compatibility conditions. Any linear inequality obtained from this projected hull and written with its \(x\)-coefficients retained is a parametric disjunctive cut valid for \(F(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convexifying a finite decision-dependent recourse disjunction produces valid inequalities whose coefficients retain explicit dependence on the first-stage decision.
knowledge_statements.title: Parametric Disjunctive Cuts

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The fixed-x disjunctive-hull idea fits the leaf, but the displayed extended formulation contains lambda_k B_k x products when x is retained as a variable and therefore does not directly provide a polyhedral parametric formulation. A source and precise lifting or reformulation conditions are required.

children.title: Scenario-Set Integer-Hull Convexification Family
children.top_down_role: Convexification routes based on scenario feasible sets and their integer hulls.

children.title: Scenario-Set Convexification
children.top_down_role: Convexification of scenario feasible sets before master coordination.

assumptions_latex: The scenario set \(S\) is finite and scenario \(s\) has feasible epigraph \(E_s\subseteq X\times Y_s\times\mathbb{R}\).
The master uses nonanticipative first-stage variables and weights \(p_s>0\) with \(\sum_{s\in S}p_s=1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Replacing each \(E_s\) by \(\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{conv}(E_s)\) gives a convex master relaxation whose value is no larger than the original minimization value.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scenario-wise closed convexification before enforcing common first-stage coordination.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The scenario-convexified formulation is
\[
\min\left\{c^{\mathsf T}x+\sum_{s\in S}p_s\theta_s:(x,y_s,\theta_s)\in\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{conv}(E_s)\ \text{for all }s\in S\right\}.
\]
Because \(E_s\subseteq\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{conv}(E_s)\), every feasible solution of the original stochastic mixed-integer formulation is feasible here with the same objective value. Thus the formulation is a convex relaxation. It is exact precisely when an optimal convexified solution can be represented by scenario-feasible points sharing the same first-stage decision.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each scenario epigraph is replaced by its closed convex hull before the scenarios are coordinated through their shared first-stage decision.
knowledge_statements.title: Scenario-Set Convexification

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Scenario-wise closed convexification is a plausible representation, but the exactness characterization and required closedness conditions are unsupported. The formulation must also state precisely how the common first-stage coordinate is represented in every scenario epigraph.

children.title: C3 Convexification Principle
children.top_down_role: Set-convexification theory supporting large-scale stochastic mixed-integer decomposition.

assumptions_latex: For each scenario \(s\in S\), let \(E_s\) be its mixed-integer feasible epigraph.
All scenario copies of the first-stage decision are linked by the nonanticipativity subspace \(N\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{conv}((\prod_{s\in S}E_s)\cap N)\subseteq(\prod_{s\in S}\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{conv}(E_s))\cap N\), with equality only under compatible scenario decompositions.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Interprets C3 as scenario-hull convexification followed by nonanticipative coordination.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The C3 convexification principle replaces each difficult set \(E_s\) by its closed convex hull and then coordinates the resulting scenario blocks through \(N\). Formally,
\[
\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{conv}\left((\prod_{s\in S}E_s)\cap N\right)
\subseteq
\left(\prod_{s\in S}\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{conv}(E_s)\right)\cap N.
\]
Consequently, scenario-wise convexification yields a valid convex relaxation. Equality requires every coordinated point on the right to admit convex decompositions into original scenario points whose first-stage components can be coupled term by term to satisfy nonanticipativity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convexify every scenario set, then impose nonanticipativity; this is valid, but exactness requires compatible convex decompositions across scenarios.
knowledge_statements.title: C3 Convexification Principle

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The set inclusion is plausible, but no evidence identifies this interpretation as the C3 Convexification Principle or supports the stated compatibility characterization. The intended named principle must be confirmed from a specific source.

children.title: D2 Decomposition Framework
children.top_down_role: Decomposition architecture associated with scenario-set convexification.

assumptions_latex: The finite-scenario problem has scenario epigraphs \(E_s\) and a common first-stage variable \(x\).
A scenario oracle can optimize linear functions over \(E_s\) or separate points from \(\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{conv}(E_s)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If no oracle returns a violated valid inequality and the master is solved exactly, the current point is feasible for the maintained scenario-hull relaxation.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Oracle-based master-scenario decomposition for the scenario-hull relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Initialize a master containing first-stage constraints and lower variables \(\theta_s\). At iteration \(k\), solve the master for \((x^k,\theta^k)\). For every \(s\in S\), call the scenario oracle at \(x^k\). If it returns an inequality
\[
\theta_s\geq\alpha_s+\beta_s^{\mathsf T}x
\]
valid for \(\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{conv}(E_s)\) and violated by \((x^k,	heta_s^k)\), add it to the master. Stop when no scenario returns a violated inequality; output the current master solution and bound. Finite termination additionally requires a finite exact inequality description or a finite-generation rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: D2 alternates between a coordinated first-stage master and scenario-hull oracles, adding violated scenario inequalities until none remain.
knowledge_statements.title: D2 Decomposition Framework

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithmic kind fits a decomposition-framework leaf, but no source identifies this procedure as D2. A general separator for a scenario hull need not return an inequality involving only x and theta, and the stopping conclusion requires a precisely defined projected epigraph and exact separation oracle.

children.title: Scenario Integer-Hull Closures
children.top_down_role: Integer-hull representations associated with individual scenario feasible sets.

assumptions_latex: For scenario \(s\), \(P_s(x)\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{m_s}\) is its continuous recourse relaxation at first-stage decision \(x\).
The index set \(I_s\) identifies recourse components required to be integral.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P_s^I(x)=\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{conv}\{y\in P_s(x):y_i\in\mathbb{Z}\text{ for all }i\in I_s\}\) is the scenario integer-hull closure.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closed convex hull of one scenario's mixed-integer recourse set at fixed first-stage decisions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For each fixed \(x\), define
\[
P_s^I(x):=\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{conv}\left\{y\in P_s(x):y_i\in\mathbb{Z}\ \text{for every }i\in I_s\right\}.
\]
This set is the scenario integer-hull closure. An inequality is valid for the closure exactly when it is valid for every mixed-integer point inside the braces. If the mixed-integer set is a rational polyhedron with bounded integer variables, its convex hull is polyhedral and the closure operator is redundant; without suitable rationality or boundedness, closedness must be stated separately.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A scenario integer-hull closure is the closed convex hull of the scenario recourse points satisfying all designated integrality restrictions.
knowledge_statements.title: Scenario Integer-Hull Closures

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition is mathematically standard and fits the leaf, but it has no source reference or explicit standard-field rationale. A specific authoritative locator is required for candidate-review acceptance.

children.title: Cross-Scenario Hull Coupling
children.top_down_role: Convexified scenario sets linked through shared first-stage structure.

assumptions_latex: Each scenario has a set \(E_s\) containing its local copy of the first-stage decision.
The subspace \(N\) imposes equality of all scenario copies of that decision.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Scenario-wise hull coupling is exact exactly when \((\prod_s\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{conv}(E_s))\cap N=\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{conv}((\prod_sE_s)\cap N)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exactness condition for coupling independently convexified scenario hulls through nonanticipativity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Cross-scenario hull coupling is exact when
\[
\left(\prod_s\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{conv}(E_s)\right)\cap N
=
\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{conv}\left(\left(\prod_sE_s\right)\cap N\right).
\]
The right-hand side is always contained in the left-hand side. Equality holds if every point in the left-hand side admits scenario-wise convex decompositions using a common set of weights such that, for each weight, the selected original scenario points lie jointly in \(N\). Absent this compatibility, independent hulls can combine decompositions having inconsistent first-stage components, making the inclusion strict.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Independent scenario hulls couple exactly only when their convex decompositions can be synchronized to satisfy nonanticipativity term by term.
knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Scenario Hull Coupling

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed equality is a valid formal exactness condition, but the scenario index set and its finiteness are not introduced. The synchronized-decomposition characterization also needs a source and more precise hypotheses.

children.title: Recourse Separation Cut Taxonomy
children.top_down_role: Cuts derived from recourse disjunctions, scenario integer hulls, or second-stage branching.

children.title: Disjunctive Decomposition Cuts
children.top_down_role: Scenario cuts constructed from explicit recourse disjunctions.

assumptions_latex: At a fixed first-stage point \(\bar x\), scenario recourse satisfies \(F_s(\bar x)\subseteq\bigcup_{k=1}^K P_{sk}(\bar x)\).
Each \(P_{sk}(\bar x)\) is a polyhedron arising from an exhaustive valid recourse disjunction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Any inequality valid for \(\operatorname{conv}(\bigcup_{k=1}^K P_{sk}(\bar x))\) is a valid scenario recourse cut and separates any point violating that hull.

notation.meaning: Scenario recourse set at the incumbent first-stage point

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scenario separation from an exhaustive finite disjunction at a fixed master point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given the exhaustive disjunction, form the disjunctive hull
\[
D_s(\bar x):=\operatorname{conv}\left(\bigcup_{k=1}^K P_{sk}(\bar x)\right).
\]
If a trial recourse point \(\bar y_s\notin D_s(\bar x)\), polyhedral separation produces \((\pi,ho)\) with \(\pi^{\mathsf T}y\geq\rho\) for every \(y\in D_s(\bar x)\) but \(\pi^{\mathsf T}\bar y_s<\rho\). Since \(F_s(\bar x)\subseteq D_s(\bar x)\), this inequality is valid for the scenario recourse set. A master cut requires a valid lifting of its right-hand side away from \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exhaustive recourse disjunction is convexified and separated; the resulting inequality is scenario-valid, with additional lifting needed for global master validity.
knowledge_statements.title: Disjunctive Decomposition Cuts

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The fixed-master-point separation claim is plausible, but separation from the unclosed convex hull of unbounded polyhedral branches needs appropriate closedness or recession assumptions. The record correctly notes that global master validity requires lifting, but supplies neither a rule nor supporting evidence.

children.title: Fenchel Cuts for SMIP
children.top_down_role: Integer-hull separation applied to scenario recourse sets.

assumptions_latex: For fixed \(x\), the scenario mixed-integer recourse set \(Y_s(x)\) is nonempty and the support value is finite.
A trial point \(\bar y\) belongs to the continuous relaxation but not to \(\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{conv}(Y_s(x))\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A vector \(\alpha\) satisfying \(\alpha^{\mathsf T}\bar y>\sigma_{Y_s(x)}(\alpha)\) certifies the valid Fenchel cut \(\alpha^{\mathsf T}y\leq\sigma_{Y_s(x)}(\alpha)\).

notation.meaning: Support function of the recourse set

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Support-function certificate separating a trial point from a scenario integer hull.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a chosen normal \(\alpha\), compute
\[
\sigma_{Y_s(x)}(\alpha):=\sup\{\alpha^{\mathsf T}y:y\in Y_s(x)\}.
\]
The inequality
\[
\alpha^{\mathsf T}y\leq\sigma_{Y_s(x)}(\alpha)
\]
is valid for \(Y_s(x)\) and therefore for its closed convex hull. If \(\alpha^{\mathsf T}\bar y>\sigma_{Y_s(x)}(\alpha)\), the pair consisting of \(\alpha\) and an exact support-value certificate verifies separation. Selecting \(\alpha\) to maximize normalized violation yields a Fenchel separation problem; a normalization is required to prevent arbitrary scaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Fenchel cut bounds a linear functional by its maximum over the scenario integer set and separates a trial point when that bound is violated.
knowledge_statements.title: Fenchel Cuts for SMIP

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The support-function inequality and separation certificate are mathematically plausible and the certificate kind is defensible, but no source supports its identification and use as a Fenchel cut for SMIP. The proposed normalized separation problem also leaves the normalization undefined.

children.title: Cuts from Second-Stage Branching
children.top_down_role: Feasibility and optimality cuts induced by recourse branch structures.

assumptions_latex: A finite second-stage branch-and-bound tree has leaf regions \(L_1(x),\ldots,L_K(x)\) whose union contains every feasible recourse point.
Every leaf relaxation is polyhedral and every branch disjunction is valid and exhaustive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every inequality valid for \(\operatorname{conv}(\bigcup_{k=1}^K L_k(x))\) is valid for the second-stage feasible set and may be lifted into a master feasibility or epigraph cut.

notation.meaning: Leaf region of the recourse branch tree

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Valid inequalities obtained by convexifying exhaustive leaves of a recourse branch tree.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
An exhaustive second-stage branch tree yields
\[
F_s(x)\subseteq\bigcup_{k=1}^K L_k(x).
\]
Consequently, any inequality valid for
\[
H_s(x):=\operatorname{conv}\left(\bigcup_{k=1}^K L_k(x)\right)
\]
is valid for the original scenario recourse set \(F_s(x)\). If the inequality excludes all recourse points associated with an infeasible master proposal, its valid lifting gives a feasibility cut. If it lower-bounds the recourse epigraph over the leaves, its lifting gives an optimality cut. Global master validity depends on retaining or validly bounding the parameter dependence on \(x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convexifying the exhaustive leaves of a second-stage branch tree yields valid recourse inequalities that can induce feasibility or optimality cuts after valid lifting.
knowledge_statements.title: Cuts from Second-Stage Branching

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Convexifying exhaustive branch-tree leaves gives fixed-x valid recourse inequalities, but the feasibility- and optimality-cut lifting claims require explicit hypotheses and evidence. A representation or algorithm kind may fit this cut-family leaf better than principle, depending on the sourced construction.

children.title: Lagrangian Cut Scaling Family
children.top_down_role: Cuts derived from scenario Lagrangian functions and scalable extensions beyond binary master domains.

children.title: Lagrangian Cuts
children.top_down_role: Scenario-derived master inequalities informed by Lagrangian recourse bounds.

assumptions_latex: Scenario recourse is \(Q_s(x)=\inf\{q_s^{\mathsf T}y:W_sy=h_s-T_sx,\ y\in Y_s\}\).
The set \(Y_s\) contains all non-linking recourse restrictions, including integrality, and the displayed infima are finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every multiplier \(\lambda\), \(Q_s(x)\geq\phi_s(\lambda)+\lambda^{\mathsf T}(T_sx-h_s)\), where \(\phi_s(\lambda)=\inf_{y\in Y_s}(q_s+W_s^{\mathsf T}\lambda)^{\mathsf T}y\).

notation.meaning: Multiplier for the recourse linking equation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Affine recourse lower bounds obtained by dualizing scenario linking equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For any multiplier \(\lambda\), define
\[
\phi_s(\lambda):=\inf_{y\in Y_s}(q_s+W_s^{\mathsf T}\lambda)^{\mathsf T}y.
\]
Every recourse-feasible \(y\) satisfies
\[
q_s^{\mathsf T}y=(q_s+W_s^{\mathsf T}\lambda)^{\mathsf T}y+\lambda^{\mathsf T}(T_sx-h_s).
\]
Taking the infimum first over \(Y_s\) gives the Lagrangian bound
\[
Q_s(x)\geq\phi_s(\lambda)+\lambda^{\mathsf T}(T_sx-h_s).
\]
Thus the epigraph inequality \(\theta_s\geq\phi_s(\lambda)+\lambda^{\mathsf T}(T_sx-h_s)\) is an affine scenario-derived master cut, without requiring convex recourse.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dualizing a scenario linking equation produces an affine lower bound on mixed-integer recourse and therefore a valid master epigraph cut.
knowledge_statements.title: Lagrangian Cuts

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The sign convention and affine Lagrangian lower bound are internally consistent, but no source supports the SMIP cut construction. Because the terminal container is a cut family, representation is likely more exact than duality. The assumptions should also specify for which multipliers phi_s(lambda) is finite rather than asserting undifferentiated finiteness.

children.title: Lagrangian Cut Strength-Cost Tradeoff
children.top_down_role: Variants balancing cut strength against generation cost.

children.title: Restricted Lagrangian Cuts
children.top_down_role: Lagrangian cuts generated from limited multiplier or scenario domains.

assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is the first-stage feasible set and \(Q:X\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) is the recourse value function.
Each \(\lambda\in\Lambda\) defines an affine minorant \(L_\lambda(x)=\alpha_\lambda+\beta_\lambda^\top x\le Q(x)\) for every \(x\in X\).
\(\Lambda_R\subseteq\Lambda\) is a computationally restricted multiplier set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q_R(x)\le Q_\Lambda(x)\le Q(x)\) for every \(x\in X\).

notation.meaning: Affine Lagrangian minorant indexed by a multiplier.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract multiplier-restriction formulation for two-stage recourse value functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A restricted Lagrangian cut is an inequality \(\theta\ge L_\lambda(x)\) generated with \(\lambda\in\Lambda_R\). Its associated lower envelope is \(Q_R(x)=\sup_{\lambda\in\Lambda_R}L_\lambda(x)\), whereas the unrestricted envelope is \(Q_\Lambda(x)=\sup_{\lambda\in\Lambda}L_\lambda(x)\). Because every indexed function is a valid minorant and \(\Lambda_R\subseteq\Lambda\), restriction preserves validity but can weaken the recourse approximation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Restricting admissible Lagrangian multipliers preserves cut validity, but its envelope cannot exceed the envelope generated by the full multiplier set.
knowledge_statements.title: Restricted Lagrangian Cuts

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The envelope inequalities are mathematically correct, but the cited general Lagrangian-methods section has not been shown to support the specialized SMIP term “restricted Lagrangian cut” or this exact multiplier-family interpretation.

children.title: Strengthened Lagrangian Cuts
children.top_down_role: Lagrangian cuts enhanced through tighter scenario information.

assumptions_latex: \(L_\lambda(x)\le Q(x)\) holds on \(X\) for all \(\lambda\in\Lambda_S\).
\(\Lambda_R\subseteq\Lambda_S\), and \(\bar x\in X\) is the incumbent point.
The displayed suprema are attained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_{\lambda^S}(\bar x)\ge L_{\lambda^R}(\bar x)\), while both resulting cuts remain valid on \(X\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Incumbent strengthening obtained by optimizing over a larger valid multiplier family.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\lambda^R\in\arg\max_{\lambda\in\Lambda_R}L_\lambda(\bar x)\) and \(\lambda^S\in\arg\max_{\lambda\in\Lambda_S}L_\lambda(\bar x)\). The inequality \(\theta\ge L_{\lambda^S}(x)\) is a strengthened Lagrangian cut relative to the restricted separation problem at \(\bar x\). Set inclusion gives \(L_{\lambda^S}(\bar x)\ge L_{\lambda^R}(\bar x)\); it does not by itself imply pointwise dominance away from \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Optimizing over a larger valid multiplier set produces a cut at least as strong at the incumbent, though not necessarily everywhere.
knowledge_statements.title: Strengthened Lagrangian Cuts

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The incumbent comparison follows from set inclusion, but authoritative support is needed for calling the resulting cut a “strengthened Lagrangian cut” in this exact taxonomy rather than merely a cut selected from a larger family.

children.title: Cut-Strength Cost Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Generation-cost comparisons across restricted or strengthened cut variants.

assumptions_latex: \(\Lambda_1\subseteq\Lambda_2\subseteq\cdots\subseteq\Lambda_m\) are multiplier families whose affine functions minorize \(Q\) on \(X\).
\(Q_k(x)=\sup_{\lambda\in\Lambda_k}L_\lambda(x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q_1(x)\le\cdots\le Q_m(x)\le Q(x)\) on \(X\), but multiplier-set inclusion alone gives no ordering of separation costs.

notation.meaning: Envelope generated by the kth family.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates the exact strength ordering from implementation-dependent generation cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(x\in X\), nesting of the multiplier sets implies \(Q_1(x)\le Q_2(x)\le\cdots\le Q_m(x)\le Q(x)\). Thus enlarging the separation family weakly strengthens the best obtainable Lagrangian lower bound. This mathematical ordering does not order the time or memory required to generate a cut: those costs depend on the representations of \(\Lambda_k\), the separation algorithms, and their stopping tolerances.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nested multiplier families yield monotonically stronger envelopes, while their cut-generation time and memory remain algorithm dependent.
knowledge_statements.title: Cut-Strength Cost Tradeoffs

children.title: Scaled Cuts
children.top_down_role: Cut families extending decomposition bounds to broader first-stage domains.

assumptions_latex: \(Z\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\), \(D\) is an invertible positive diagonal matrix, and \(X=d+DZ\).
\(\eta\ge a+b^\top z\) is valid for every \((z,\eta)\) in the standardized recourse epigraph.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\eta\ge a+b^\top D^{-1}(x-d)\) is valid on the corresponding epigraph over \(X\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Affine pullback form of scaled cuts; specialized SMIP conventions require source confirmation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the change of variables \(x=d+Dz\), a valid cut \(\eta\ge a+b^\top z\) has the scaled representation \(\eta\ge a+b^\top D^{-1}(x-d)\). Validity follows for the entire image domain \(X=d+DZ\), not merely for points used to generate the standardized cut. Positive diagonal scaling preserves affine-cut equivalence while permitting coordinates with different bounds or units to share one standardized cut construction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A valid affine cut on a standardized domain transfers to a scaled first-stage domain by substituting the inverse affine coordinate map.
knowledge_statements.title: Scaled Cuts

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The affine pullback is correct, but the supplied source does not establish that “Scaled Cuts” in this Lagrangian-cut taxonomy means coordinate rescaling rather than a specialized SMIP cut-scaling construction.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Integer L-Shaped Procedure with Branching and Cuts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operational pseudocode for an integer first-stage L-shaped method; the extract asserts neither finite termination nor optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(\bar z:=\infty\), \(K:=L:=0\), and let \(\mathcal P\) contain the initial problem. While \(\mathcal P\neq\varnothing\), select and remove a problem \(P\). Repeatedly solve its master for \((\widehat x,\widehat\theta)\), fathoming \(P\) if the master is infeasible or \(c^{\mathsf T}\widehat x+\widehat\theta>\bar z\). Otherwise, attempt first a feasibility cut and then, if necessary, an integrality cut. If neither is generated and \(\widehat x\) is integral, evaluate \(\mathcal Q(\widehat x)\), update \(\bar z:=\min\{\bar z,c^{\mathsf T}\widehat x+\mathcal Q(\widehat x)\}\), and fathom when \(\widehat\theta\geq\mathcal Q(\widehat x)\); if not fathomed, increment \(L\) and add \(-\beta_L^{\mathsf T}x+\theta\geq\alpha_L\). If \(\widehat x\) is nonintegral, branch into two new problems and add them to \(\mathcal P\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Start with no incumbent and a list containing the initial problem. At each selected problem, solve the master and fathom it if infeasible or worse than the incumbent. Otherwise try feasibility and integrality cuts. If neither is available, evaluate recourse and update the incumbent at an integral point, adding a recourse cut when required; at a nonintegral point, branch into two subproblems.
assumptions_latex: \mathcal P\text{ initially contains the initial problem},\quad K=L=0,\quad \bar z=\infty
\text{The master, cut-generation, recourse-evaluation, and branching operations appearing in the procedure are defined.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The procedure prescribes master solution, fathoming, cut generation, incumbent updates, and branching until the problem list is empty; no termination or optimality guarantee is asserted.}

knowledge_statements.title: Binary First-Stage Integer L-Shaped Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite binary integer L-shaped scheme using exact incumbent cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize the master with \(x\in X\) and \(\theta\ge L\). At an incumbent \(\bar x\), evaluate \(Q(\bar x)\) and add \[\theta\ge Q(\bar x)-(Q(\bar x)-L)\left(\sum_{j:\bar x_j=1}(1-x_j)+\sum_{j:\bar x_j=0}x_j\right).\] Re-solve the master and stop when its lower bound equals the best evaluated objective value. The cut is exact at \(\bar x\) and no larger than \(L\) at every other binary vector, so finite enumeration implies termination.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The binary integer L-shaped method adds a globally valid cut exact at each incumbent and terminates finitely when the master and incumbent bounds meet.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\{0,1\}^n\) is finite and nonempty, and \(c\in\mathbb{R}^n\) is the first-stage cost vector.
\(Q:X\to\mathbb{R}\) is evaluated exactly at each incumbent and \(L\le Q(x)\) for every \(x\in X\).
The master is solved exactly at each iteration.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The method returns an optimizer of \(\min_{x\in X}\{c^\top x+Q(x)\}\) after finitely many distinct incumbents.

notation.meaning: Recourse value function and its global lower bound.

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite constant L is no greater than the minimum recourse value over first-stage decisions satisfying Ax=b and x in X.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists L\in\mathbb R\text{ finite}:\quad L\leq\min_x\{\mathcal Q(x)\mid Ax=b,\ x\in X\}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Parameterized lambda-strengthened binary optimality cut
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Family of valid binary optimality cuts parameterized by an integer \(t\), using source-defined quantities \(\lambda(s,S)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x_i=1\) for \(i\in S\), \(x_i=0\) for \(i\notin S\), and \(q_S=\mathcal Q(x)\). Let \(t\in\mathbb Z\) satisfy \(1\leq t\leq|S|\), and define \[a=\max\left\{\max_{s\leq t}\frac{q_S-\lambda(s,S)}{s},\frac{q_S-L}{t+1}\right\}.\] Then the inequality (2.3), namely \[\theta\geq a\left(\sum_{i\in S}x_i-\sum_{i\notin S}x_i\right)+q_S-a|S|,\] is a valid optimality cut.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an integer t between 1 and the size of S, the displayed maximum defines a coefficient a for which inequality (2.3) is a valid optimality cut.

q_S=\mathcal Q(x)
L\in\mathbb R,\qquad L\leq\min_x\{\mathcal Q(x)\mid Ax=b,\ x\in X\}
t\in\mathbb Z,\qquad 1\leq t\leq|S|
a=\max\left\{\max_{s\leq t}\frac{q_S-\lambda(s,S)}{s},\frac{q_S-L}{t+1}\right\}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \theta\geq a\left(\sum_{i\in S}x_i-\sum_{i\notin S}x_i\right)+q_S-a|S|\quad\text{is valid}.

knowledge_statements.title: General-Integer First-Stage L-Shaped Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bounded general integers handled through an exact finite binary lifting.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Introduce \(y_{jk}\in\{0,1\}\) for \(k=\ell_j,\ldots,u_j\), impose \(\sum_k y_{jk}=1\), and set \(x_j=\sum_k k y_{jk}\). Solve the lifted master, evaluate \(Q\) at its incumbent, and add the binary integer L-shaped cut in the complete vector \(y\), using the global lower bound \(L\). Stop when the master lower bound equals the best evaluated objective. The one-hot equations give an exact finite representation, so validity and finite convergence of the binary scheme transfer to bounded general-integer decisions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bounded integer decisions can be lifted exactly to one-hot binaries, after which binary integer L-shaped cuts provide a finite decomposition method.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\prod_{j=1}^n\{\ell_j,\ldots,u_j\}\) is finite and nonempty, and \(c\in\mathbb{R}^n\) is the first-stage cost vector.
Every integer coordinate has an exact one-hot representation.
\(Q:X\to\mathbb{R}\) is evaluated exactly, a finite bound \(L\le Q(x)\) is known for every \(x\in X\), and the lifted master is solved exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The lifted method terminates finitely with an optimizer of \(\min_{x\in X}\{c^\top x+Q(x)\}\).

children.title: Integer-Recourse L-Shaped Methods
children.top_down_role: L-shaped architectures accommodating mixed-integer second-stage subproblems.

assumptions_latex: The scenario set \(S\) is finite, with probabilities \(p_s>0\) summing to one.
\(X\) is a finite first-stage set and each mixed-integer recourse value \(Q_s(x)\) is solved exactly.
Finite lower bounds \(L_s\le Q_s(x)\) are known on \(X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Incumbent-exact valid cuts and exact master solves terminate with an optimizer of \(\min_{x\in X}\{c^\top x+\sum_s p_sQ_s(x)\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-set architecture that does not require linear-programming duality in recourse.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Maintain master variables that lower-bound \(Q_s(x)\). At an incumbent \(\bar x\), solve every mixed-integer scenario subproblem exactly and add globally valid scenario or aggregated cuts that equal the computed values at \(\bar x\). Re-solve the master and stop when its lower bound equals the best evaluated objective. Because ordinary linear-dual cuts need not describe integer recourse, validity must come from integer optimality cuts, disjunctive inequalities, or scenario-epigraph convexification. On finite \(X\), incumbent-exact cuts give finite termination.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Integer-recourse L-shaped methods replace ordinary LP-dual cuts with valid integer or convexification cuts that are exact at evaluated first-stage points.
