knowledge_statements.title: Multicut Integer L-Shaped Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separate master epigraph variables and cuts for individual scenarios.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Introduce one master variable \(\theta_s\) for each scenario and minimize first-stage cost plus \(\sum_{s\in S}p_s\theta_s\). At iteration \(r\), solve each scenario subproblem, generate \(\ell_{sr}\), and add \(\theta_s\ge\ell_{sr}(x)\) separately for every selected scenario. Re-solve and stop under the master-to-incumbent gap test. The separate inequalities retain scenario information that probability aggregation discards.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A multicut method keeps separate recourse variables and lower-bounding cuts for scenarios, retaining more information in the master relaxation.
assumptions_latex: \(S\) is finite, \(p_s>0\) for every \(s\in S\), and \(\sum_{s\in S}p_s=1\).
Every generated estimator satisfies \(\ell_{sr}(x)\le Q_s(x)\) for every \(x\in X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The constraints \(\theta_s\ge\ell_{sr}(x)\) validly lower-bound expected recourse through \(\sum_{s\in S}p_s\theta_s\).

notation.meaning: Scenario lower estimator generated at iteration r.

children.title: Cut-Aggregation Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Master-size plus bound-strength differences across aggregation regimes.

assumptions_latex: The single-cut and multicut masters use the same scenario estimators \(\ell_{sr}\) and probabilities \(p_s>0\).
The single-cut variable is identified with \(\theta=\sum_s p_s\theta_s\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The projection of the multicut feasible region is contained in the corresponding single-cut feasible region.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Relaxation comparison for identical scenario estimators and aggregation weights.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If the multicut master imposes \(\theta_s\ge\ell_{sr}(x)\) for every \(s\) and \(r\), then summing with weights \(p_s\) yields \(\sum_s p_s\theta_s\ge\sum_s p_s\ell_{sr}(x)\), the corresponding single cut. Hence multicut projection weakly dominates single-cut aggregation for the same estimators. This strength requires more master variables and constraints; no universal ordering of total runtime follows from dominance alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With identical scenario estimators, the multicut relaxation dominates the single-cut relaxation but uses a larger master, so total runtime remains instance dependent.
knowledge_statements.title: Cut-Aggregation Tradeoffs

children.title: Primal Outer-Approximation Decomposition
children.top_down_role: Master approximations refined through scenario-set separation and parametric cuts.

children.title: Parametric-Cut Decomposition
children.top_down_role: Decomposition driven by iteratively generated parametric scenario cuts.

assumptions_latex: For every scenario \(s\), parameter \(\gamma\in\Gamma_s\) defines \(\phi_s(x;\gamma)\le Q_s(x)\) on \(X\).
At an incumbent \(\bar x\), the separation oracle returns a maximizing or sufficiently improving parameter.
The master and evaluated recourse problems provide valid lower and upper bounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every generated parametric cut is valid, and the algorithm stops when the certified master-to-incumbent gap meets tolerance.

notation.meaning: Admissible parameter set for scenario s.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Oracle-based outer approximation using a parameterized family of globally valid scenario cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize finite subsets \(G_s^0\subseteq\Gamma_s\) and solve a master containing \(\theta_s\ge\phi_s(x;\gamma)\) for \(\gamma\in G_s^k\). At its incumbent \(\bar x^k\), evaluate \(Q_s(\bar x^k)\) and call the parameter-separation oracle. Add returned parameters to \(G_s^{k+1}\), update the incumbent upper bound, and repeat. Stop when the difference between the incumbent value and the master lower bound is at most the prescribed tolerance; otherwise continue separation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Parametric-cut decomposition repeatedly selects valid scenario estimators from parameterized families, adds violated cuts to the master, and stops at a certified gap.
knowledge_statements.title: Parametric-Cut Decomposition

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No citation establishes which specialized parametric-cut family this leaf denotes or supports the stated oracle algorithm and stopping guarantee.

children.title: Set-Convexification Decomposition
children.top_down_role: Primal decomposition based on approximating scenario convex hulls.

assumptions_latex: For each scenario \(s\), \(E_s=\{(x,\theta_s):x\in X,\ \theta_s\ge Q_s(x)\}\).
A separation oracle returns an inequality valid for \(\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{conv}(E_s)\) and violated by the current master point when one exists.
Master and scenario problems are solved exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The maintained master is an outer approximation of every \(\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{conv}(E_s)\); finite facet generation gives finite termination when these hulls are polyhedra with finitely many facets.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal outer approximation of closed convex hulls of scenario recourse epigraphs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Begin with supersets \(P_s^0\supseteq\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{conv}(E_s)\) and solve the master over their intersection with the first-stage constraints. For each incumbent, invoke scenario separation. If a valid inequality for \(\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{conv}(E_s)\) is violated, intersect \(P_s^k\) with its halfspace and re-solve. If no scenario separates the point and the incumbent gap is zero, return it. When every hull is a finitely faceted polyhedron and new facets are generated, termination is finite.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Set-convexification decomposition outer-approximates each scenario epigraph hull, adding separating valid inequalities until no violated hull inequality remains.
knowledge_statements.title: Set-Convexification Decomposition

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The abstract outer-approximation statement is plausible, but no inspectable source supports its identification with set-convexification decomposition or the stated finite-facet termination conditions.

children.title: Disjunctive-Fenchel Separation Family
children.top_down_role: Scenario decomposition using disjunctive or Fenchel separation.

children.title: Disjunctive Decomposition
children.top_down_role: Scenario decomposition based on recourse disjunctions.

knowledge_statements.title: Disjunctive Decomposition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal decomposition using explicit scenario-wise disjunctions of mixed-integer recourse sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each scenario \(s\), suppose the recourse set is \(Y_s(x)=\bigcup_{j\in J_s}P_{sj}(x)\), where every \(P_{sj}(x)\) is a polyhedron and \(J_s\) is finite. Initialize a master relaxation containing the first-stage constraints and outer variables for scenario costs. Given a master solution \(\bar x\), solve each scenario subproblem over \(Y_s(\bar x)\). If its epigraph point violates \(\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{conv}\{(x,\theta_s):\theta_s\ge Q_s(x)\}\), derive a valid inequality from a disjunctive convex-hull formulation of \(\bigcup_{j\in J_s}P_{sj}(x)\), add it to the master, and reoptimize. Stop when every scenario admits no separating disjunctive inequality beyond the prescribed tolerance; return the incumbent feasible first-stage solution and master bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly solve scenario MIPs and strengthen the first-stage master with inequalities obtained from convexifying scenario disjunctions until no material violation remains.
assumptions_latex: \(J_s\) is finite for every scenario \(s\).
Each disjunct \(P_{sj}(x)\) has a valid polyhedral description.
Scenario subproblems and separation problems are solved to the stated tolerance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_k\le v^*\le U_k\), with termination when \(U_k-L_k\le\varepsilon\).

notation.meaning: mixed-integer feasible recourse set for scenario s
optimal recourse value in scenario s
master lower bound and incumbent upper bound at iteration k

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits the leaf, but the specific disjunctive SMIP separation procedure and its bound-gap termination claim require a direct authoritative locator.

children.title: Fenchel Decomposition
children.top_down_role: Scenario decomposition based on Fenchel separation of integer recourse sets.

knowledge_statements.title: Fenchel Decomposition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scenario decomposition using Fenchel inequalities to separate fractional recourse solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For scenario \(s\) and fixed first-stage point \(\bar x\), let \(Y_s(\bar x)\) be the bounded mixed-integer recourse set and let \(\bar y_s\) be a point in its current linear relaxation. Solve a normalized separation problem that selects \(\alpha_s\) and sets \(\beta_s=\max\{\alpha_s^{\mathsf T}y:y\in Y_s(\bar x)\}\), maximizing the violation \(\alpha_s^{\mathsf T}\bar y_s-\beta_s\). If the violation exceeds \(\varepsilon\), add the Fenchel inequality \(\alpha_s^{\mathsf T}y_s\le\beta_s\) to the scenario relaxation and regenerate the associated master outer approximation. Repeat scenario solution, separation, and master optimization until all normalized violations and the global bound gap are within tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Separate fractional scenario solutions by normalized Fenchel inequalities valid for the mixed-integer recourse hull, then propagate the strengthened scenario values to the master.
assumptions_latex: Each separated set \(Y_s(\bar x)\) is nonempty and bounded.
The normalization makes the separation problem bounded.
Scenario probabilities are positive and have finite support.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\alpha_s^{\mathsf T}y\le\beta_s\) for every \(y\in Y_s(\bar x)\), while \(\alpha_s^{\mathsf T}\bar y_s>\beta_s+\varepsilon\) whenever a cut is generated.

notation.meaning: scenario recourse set at the current first-stage point
normal vector and support value of a Fenchel inequality

source_refs.locator: 3.5 Cutting Plane Method for the Solution of the All Integer Variable Linear Programming Problem p. 76

review_flags: The locator supports integer cutting planes generally; direct confirmation of the stated Fenchel decomposition is pending.

children.title: Hybrid Separation Regimes
children.top_down_role: Decomposition settings combining multiple separation sources.

knowledge_statements.title: Hybrid Separation Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Adaptive use of disjunctive and Fenchel separators within one primal outer-approximation scheme.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Maintain a master relaxation \(M_k\) and, for every scenario \(s\), a pool of valid disjunctive and Fenchel inequalities. At iteration \(k\), solve \(M_k\), obtain \(\bar x^k\), and solve the scenario relaxations. For each violated scenario point, evaluate candidate cuts from both families using a common score \(r(c)=v(c)/(a(c)+\gamma)\), where \(v(c)\) is normalized violation, \(a(c)\) is estimated generation cost, and \(\gamma>0\). Add any cut with \(v(c)>\varepsilon\) whose score is maximal among the available candidates; if one oracle fails, invoke the other. Reoptimize and stop only when neither family finds a violation above \(\varepsilon\) and the incumbent gap is within tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At each master iterate, compare valid disjunctive and Fenchel cuts by violation and generation cost, add the preferred cuts, and stop only after both families fail.
assumptions_latex: Both separation oracles return inequalities valid for the relevant scenario recourse hull.
Cut scores use the same positive scaling convention.
The master retains every accepted inequality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M_{k+1}\subseteq M_k\) and the true feasible epigraph remains contained in every \(M_k\).

notation.meaning: master outer approximation at iteration k
normalized violation of candidate cut c
estimated computational cost of generating candidate c

review_flags: The scoring rule is a precise admissible hybrid regime, but no authoritative locator was supplied for this particular selection policy.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The hybrid algorithm fits the leaf, but the particular violation-to-cost score and fallback policy appear bespoke and have no supporting locator.

children.title: Scenario Dual-Decomposition Family
children.top_down_role: Scenario separation through relaxation of nonanticipativity.

children.title: Nonanticipativity Lagrangian Decomposition
children.top_down_role: Scenario-separable bounding through Lagrangian treatment of agreement.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonanticipativity Lagrangian Decomposition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lagrangian relaxation of scenario agreement in a finite-scenario stochastic mixed-integer program.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the deterministic equivalent be \(v^*=\min\{\sum_{s\in S}p_s f_s(x_s):x_s\in X_s,\ x_s=z\ \forall s\}\), where each \(X_s\) may contain integrality restrictions. Relax \(x_s=z\) with multipliers \(\lambda_s\). Finiteness of the infimum over the unrestricted consensus variable requires \(\sum_{s\in S}\lambda_s=0\), and the Lagrangian dual is \[d^*=\sup_{\sum_s\lambda_s=0}\sum_{s\in S}\inf_{x_s\in X_s}\bigl(p_s f_s(x_s)+\lambda_s^{\mathsf T}x_s\bigr).\] Hence evaluation of the dual function separates by scenario and \(d^*\le v^*\). Mixed-integer nonconvexity may produce a positive duality gap, so equality is not asserted without additional convexity and regularity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Relaxing scenario agreement yields independent scenario subproblems and a dual lower bound; mixed-integer structure can prevent equality with the primal optimum.
assumptions_latex: \(S\) is finite and \(p_s>0\) with \(\sum_s p_s=1\).
Every scenario infimum is well-defined in the extended-real sense.
A feasible nonanticipative solution exists with finite objective value.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d^*\le v^*\), and the dual-function evaluation is scenario separable.

children.title: Progressive Hedging for SMIP
children.top_down_role: Augmented scenario coordination adapted to discrete subproblems.

knowledge_statements.title: Progressive Hedging for SMIP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-scenario progressive hedging with mixed-integer scenario subproblems and consensus updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose \(\rho>0\), scenario probabilities \(p_s>0\), feasible initial decisions \(x_s^0\in X_s\), consensus \(z^0=\sum_s p_sx_s^0\), and multipliers \(w_s^0=0\). For \(k=0,1,\ldots\), solve in parallel \[x_s^{k+1}\in\arg\min_{x\in X_s}\left\{p_sf_s(x)+(w_s^k)^{\mathsf T}x+\frac{\rho p_s}{2}\lVert x-z^k\rVert_2^2\right\}.\] Set \(z^{k+1}=\sum_s p_sx_s^{k+1}\) and \(w_s^{k+1}=w_s^k+\rho p_s(x_s^{k+1}-z^{k+1})\). Stop when primal disagreement and successive consensus change satisfy prescribed tolerances. For nonconvex mixed-integer \(X_s\), this is a coordination heuristic unless additional convergence conditions are supplied.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Progressive hedging alternates parallel penalized scenario MIPs, probability-weighted consensus averaging, and multiplier updates; for integer models it is generally heuristic.
assumptions_latex: \(S\) is finite, \(p_s>0\), and \(\sum_s p_s=1\).
Each penalized scenario subproblem has a minimizer.
All scenario copies share the same consensus coordinates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_s w_s^k=0\) for every \(k\), and termination reports approximate nonanticipativity rather than global optimality in general SMIP.
review_flags: No progressive-hedging source locator was supplied.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The scaled progressive-hedging updates are internally consistent and appropriately described as heuristic for general SMIP, but no authoritative locator supports the algorithmic variant.

children.title: Stabilized Dual Decomposition Regimes
children.top_down_role: Stabilized nonsmooth optimization of scenario-dual bounds.

children.title: Bundle-Stabilized Dual Decomposition
children.top_down_role: Scenario-dual optimization stabilized through bundle information.

knowledge_statements.title: Bundle-Stabilized Dual Decomposition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proximal bundle maximization of the concave nonanticipativity dual function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(g\) be the concave scenario-separable dual function on \(\Lambda=\{\lambda:\sum_s\lambda_s=0\}\). From evaluated points \(\lambda^i\), values \(g_i=g(\lambda^i)\), and supergradients \(q_i\), form the cutting-plane upper model \(m_k(\lambda)=\min_{i\in B_k}\{g_i+q_i^{\mathsf T}(\lambda-\lambda^i)\}\). Given center \(\bar\lambda^k\) and \(t_k>0\), compute \[\lambda^{k+1}\in\arg\max_{\lambda\in\Lambda}\left\{m_k(\lambda)-\frac{1}{2t_k}\lVert\lambda-\bar\lambda^k\rVert_2^2\right\}.\] Evaluate all scenario subproblems at \(\lambda^{k+1}\), append the resulting cut, and accept a serious step when actual dual improvement is at least a fixed fraction of predicted improvement; otherwise retain the center. Stop when predicted improvement is below tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A proximal bundle master combines scenario-derived dual cuts, proposes a stabilized multiplier, and uses serious or null steps according to achieved dual improvement.
assumptions_latex: The dual function \(g\) is finite and concave on \(\Lambda\).
Scenario solutions provide valid supergradients of \(g\).
The bundle master has a maximizer for each \(t_k>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g(\lambda)\le m_k(\lambda)\) for every \(\lambda\in\Lambda\), so the model supplies a computable predicted-improvement bound.

notation.meaning: bundle index set at iteration k
polyhedral upper model of the concave dual function

children.title: Trust-Region Dual Decomposition
children.top_down_role: Scenario-dual optimization restricted through trust-region stabilization.

knowledge_statements.title: Trust-Region Dual Decomposition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cutting-plane dual maximization restricted to a neighborhood of the current multiplier center.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(g\) be the concave nonanticipativity dual function on \(\Lambda\), and construct the upper cutting-plane model \(m_k\) from scenario evaluations and valid supergradients. Given center \(\bar\lambda^k\), radius \(\Delta_k>0\), and norm \(\lVert\cdot\rVert\), solve \[\lambda^{k+1}\in\arg\max\{m_k(\lambda):\lambda\in\Lambda,\ \lVert\lambda-\bar\lambda^k\rVert\le\Delta_k\}.\] Evaluate \(g(\lambda^{k+1})\) by independent scenario subproblems. Accept the trial point when the ratio of actual to predicted dual improvement exceeds a prescribed threshold; enlarge or retain \(\Delta_k\) after successful steps and shrink it after unsuccessful steps. Stop when predicted improvement is within tolerance and the radius-management test is satisfied.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A trust-region master maximizes the dual cutting-plane model near the current multiplier, then accepts and resizes the region using actual versus predicted improvement.
assumptions_latex: Scenario evaluations yield finite dual values and valid supergradients.
The trust-region master is solvable.
Acceptance and radius thresholds lie in their standard ordered ranges.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g(\lambda^{k+1})-g(\bar\lambda^k)\) is compared with \(m_k(\lambda^{k+1})-g(\bar\lambda^k)\) before the center is changed.

notation.meaning: cutting-plane upper model of the concave dual function

review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports trust-region stabilization of the scenario dual.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The trust-region dual algorithm is mathematically plausible and appropriately scoped, but its acceptance and radius-management specification lacks a directly supporting source.

children.title: Stabilization-Regime Selection
children.top_down_role: Suitability of stabilization variants across nonsmooth dual landscapes.

knowledge_statements.title: Stabilization-Regime Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A model-based rule for choosing proximal-bundle or trust-region stabilization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At iteration \(k\), let \(m_k\) be the dual cutting-plane model, \(\bar\lambda^k\) the current center, and \(q_i\) the active bundle supergradients. Define the instability statistic \(D_k=\max_{i,j\in A_k}\lVert q_i-q_j\rVert_2\) and the normalized model error \(E_k=(m_k(\lambda^k)-g(\lambda^k))/(1+|g(\lambda^k)|)\). For fixed thresholds \(D_{m hi}>D_{m lo}\ge0\) and \(E_{m hi}>E_{m lo}\ge0\), select proximal-bundle stabilization when \(D_k\ge D_{m hi}\) or \(E_k\ge E_{m hi}\), and select trust-region stabilization when \(D_k\le D_{m lo}\) and \(E_k\le E_{m lo}\). In the intermediate band, retain the previous regime, giving a hysteretic and fully specified selection condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose proximal stabilization under large subgradient dispersion or model error, trust regions under small values, and retain the previous regime inside a hysteresis band.
assumptions_latex: The active-cut set \(A_k\) is nonempty.
Dual values and cutting-plane model values are finite.
Thresholds satisfy the displayed ordering.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_k\in\{\mathrm{proximal},\mathrm{trust\mbox{-}region}\}\) is uniquely determined from \((D_k,E_k,R_{k-1})\).
review_flags: This is a precise adaptive selection condition, but no supplied source identifies it as a standard SMIP regime.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The hysteretic selection rule fits a condition leaf but appears bespoke and unsupported; additionally, the evaluation point \(\lambda^k\) is not introduced or related to the stated center.

children.title: Distributed Dual Decomposition Regimes
children.top_down_role: Distributed scenario evaluation with synchronous or delayed coordination.

children.title: Parallel Dual Decomposition
children.top_down_role: Concurrent scenario evaluation under coordinated dual updates.

knowledge_statements.title: Parallel Dual Decomposition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Synchronous parallel evaluation of scenario dual subproblems followed by a centralized multiplier update.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\) be a finite scenario set with probabilities \(p_s>0\) satisfying \(\sum_{s\in S}p_s=1\), let \(v^*\) denote the nonanticipative primal optimum, and define \(\Lambda=\{\lambda:\sum_{s\in S}\lambda_s=0\}\) and \(g(\lambda)=\sum_{s\in S}\inf_{x_s\in X_s}\{p_sf_s(x_s)+\lambda_s^{\mathsf T}x_s\}\). Initialize \(\lambda^0\in\Lambda\). At synchronized iteration \(k\), broadcast \(\lambda^k\) and solve in parallel \[x_s^k\in\arg\min_{x_s\in X_s}\bigl(p_sf_s(x_s)+(\lambda_s^k)^{\mathsf T}x_s\bigr),\qquad s\in S.\] After all workers return, set \(\bar x^k=\sum_{r\in S}p_rx_r^k\), define \(q_s^k=x_s^k-\bar x^k\), and update \(\lambda^{k+1}=\Pi_\Lambda(\lambda^k+\alpha_kq^k)\) for a prescribed \(\alpha_k>0\). Record \(g(\lambda^k)\) as a dual bound. Stop under a prescribed stationarity, bound-gap, or iteration-limit rule; otherwise no worker advances until all current scenario results have been aggregated.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: All scenario dual subproblems use the same multiplier in parallel; after every worker returns, their probability-weighted disagreement vectors are aggregated for a projected multiplier update, and the common-multiplier dual value supplies a valid bound.
assumptions_latex: \(S\) is finite, \(p_s>0\), and \(\sum_{s\in S}p_s=1\).
Each scenario dual subproblem attains a finite solution at every multiplier visited.
\(\Pi_\Lambda\) denotes projection onto \(\Lambda\) in the chosen norm, and \(\alpha_k>0\).
The nonanticipative primal problem has finite optimum \(v^*\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lambda^k\in\Lambda\) and \(g(\lambda^k)\le v^*\) at every synchronized iteration.

notation.meaning: probability-weighted scenario average at iteration k
optimal value of the nonanticipative primal problem

review_flags: The synchronous parallel execution convention remains to be confirmed from full text.

children.title: Asynchronous Dual Decomposition
children.top_down_role: Scenario-dual computation permitting delayed or irregular worker communication.

knowledge_statements.title: Asynchronous Dual Decomposition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scenario dual updates using independently returned subproblem results without global synchronization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Maintain a multiplier \(\lambda^k\in\Lambda\). At update event \(k\), let \(I_k\) be the scenarios whose workers return solutions computed using possibly stale multipliers \(\lambda^{k-d_{s,k}}\). Construct an aggregate \(\widehat q^k\) by replacing the stored component for each \(s\in I_k\) with its new scenario disagreement and retaining the latest available components for other scenarios. Apply \[\lambda^{k+1}=\Pi_\Lambda(\lambda^k+\alpha_k\widehat q^k).\] Immediately dispatch new work to the available workers; no global barrier is imposed. Stop under a specified stationarity, bound-gap, or event-budget rule. A dual value is certified only when all components used in its evaluation correspond to one common multiplier.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Workers solve scenarios at possibly stale multipliers; each return refreshes the aggregate disagreement and triggers a projected update without waiting for every scenario.
assumptions_latex: Every scenario worker returns infinitely often.
Returned delays \(d_{s,k}\) satisfy the adopted staleness regime.
The stored aggregate distinguishes certified common-multiplier bounds from mixed-time estimates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lambda^k\in\Lambda\) for every event \(k\); mixed-time aggregates alone do not certify \(g(\lambda^k)\).

notation.meaning: workers returning at update event k
age of the multiplier used by scenario s

review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports asynchronous SMIP dual decomposition.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The asynchronous structure fits the leaf, but the refreshed disagreement components and adopted delay regime are not specified sufficiently to identify a supported convergence framework, and no source is supplied.

children.title: Staleness-Tolerance Regimes
children.top_down_role: Coordination regimes distinguished by permissible information delay.

knowledge_statements.title: Staleness-Tolerance Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Delay and stepsize conditions controlling errors in asynchronous scenario-dual updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For update event \(k\), let \(d_{s,k}\ge0\) be the age of scenario \(s\)'s multiplier and let \(\alpha_k>0\) be the multiplier stepsize. A bounded-staleness regime requires a finite \(\tau\) such that \(d_{s,k}\le\tau\) for every used return, together with \(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\alpha_k=\infty\) and \(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\alpha_k^2<\infty\). A diminishing-unbounded-staleness regime instead requires every scenario to return infinitely often and \[\alpha_k\sum_{j=k-d_{s,k}}^{k-1}\alpha_j\longrightarrow0\quad\text{for every }s.\] These predicates ensure that multiplier motion accumulated over the information delay becomes asymptotically negligible; they do not by themselves remove a mixed-integer Lagrangian duality gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Permit uniformly bounded delays with square-summable diminishing steps, or growing delays whose accumulated multiplier motion vanishes; neither regime guarantees zero mixed-integer duality gap.
assumptions_latex: Every used delay \(d_{s,k}\) is finite.
Scenario supergradients are uniformly bounded on the visited multiplier set.
Projection onto the multiplier domain is nonexpansive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\alpha_k\sum_{j=k-d_{s,k}}^{k-1}\alpha_j\to0\) controls the asymptotic perturbation caused by stale information.

notation.meaning: uniform delay bound in the bounded-staleness regime

review_flags: The asynchronous convergence conditions require a directly supporting source and exact theorem context.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: These delay and stepsize predicates depend on the precise asynchronous subgradient theorem and update model; a direct theorem-level source is required before treating them as a valid staleness regime.

children.title: Dantzig–Wolfe Decomposition for SMIP
children.top_down_role: Inner approximations built from scenario-feasible mixed-integer solutions.

children.title: Scenario Dantzig–Wolfe Reformulations
children.top_down_role: Master formulations generated from scenario-feasible columns.

knowledge_statements.title: Scenario Dantzig–Wolfe Reformulations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convexification of finite-scenario mixed-integer feasible sets by scenario-feasible columns.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each scenario \(s\), let \(X_s\) be a nonempty bounded mixed-integer polyhedron with extreme-point columns \(v_{sr}\), indexed by \(r\in R_s\). Replacing each scenario copy by \(x_s=\sum_{r\in R_s}v_{sr}\theta_{sr}\), with \(\sum_{r\in R_s}\theta_{sr}=1\) and \(\theta_{sr}\ge0\), yields \(x_s\in\operatorname{conv}(X_s)\). Thus the convexified deterministic equivalent has a master over column weights, the original cross-scenario linking or nonanticipativity equations, and one convexity equation per scenario. Restricted masters use subsets \(R_s^k\subset R_s\); pricing for scenario \(s\) minimizes reduced cost over \(X_s\). A column with negative reduced cost is appended, and absence of such columns certifies optimality of the full linear convexified master.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Represent each convexified scenario set by weights on scenario-feasible columns; solve restricted linking masters and generate missing columns through independent reduced-cost pricing problems.
assumptions_latex: Every \(X_s\) is nonempty and bounded.
The scenario set is finite.
Pricing problems are solved globally over their mixed-integer sets.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_s\in\operatorname{conv}(X_s)\iff x_s=\sum_r v_{sr}\theta_{sr},\ \sum_r\theta_{sr}=1,\ \theta_{sr}\ge0\).

notation.meaning: master weight assigned to a scenario column
scenario columns present in the restricted master

children.title: Dantzig–Wolfe Dual Decomposition
children.top_down_role: Dual-decomposition organization linked to Dantzig–Wolfe master-pricing structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Dantzig–Wolfe Dual Decomposition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-scenario convex-hull reformulation of the linear relaxation of a two-stage SMIP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(S\) be a finite scenario set. For each \(s\in S\), let \(p_s>0\), let \(X_s\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{n_s}\) be a nonempty bounded mixed-integer polyhedron, and let \(K_s\) index the vertices \(v_{sk}\), \(k\in K_s\), of \(\operatorname{conv}(X_s)\). Given \(c_s\in\mathbb{R}^{n_s}\), \(A_s\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n_s}\), and \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\), the relaxation
\[\min\left\{\sum_{s\in S}p_sc_s^Tz_s:\sum_{s\in S}A_sz_s=b,\ z_s\in\operatorname{conv}(X_s)\ \text{for all }s\in S\right\}\]
is equivalently
\[\min_{\lambda\ge0}\left\{\sum_{s\in S}\sum_{k\in K_s}p_sc_s^Tv_{sk}\lambda_{sk}:\sum_{s\in S}\sum_{k\in K_s}A_sv_{sk}\lambda_{sk}=b,\ \sum_{k\in K_s}\lambda_{sk}=1\ \text{for all }s\in S\right\}.\]
For an unrestricted coupling dual \(\pi\in\mathbb{R}^m\) and unrestricted convexity duals \(\alpha_s\), scenario \(s\) prices a column by minimizing \((p_sc_s-A_s^T\pi)^Tz-\alpha_s\) over \(z\in X_s\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each scenario convex hull is represented by its vertex columns. The coupling and convexity dual multipliers make the search for an omitted improving column separable by scenario.
assumptions_latex: \(S\) is finite, \(p_s>0\) for every \(s\in S\), and \(\sum_{s\in S}p_s=1\).
Each \(X_s\) is a nonempty bounded mixed-integer polyhedron.
The only cross-scenario constraints are represented by \(\sum_{s\in S}A_sz_s=b\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The convex-hull relaxation has the displayed Dantzig–Wolfe master representation and scenario-separable reduced-cost pricing problems.

notation.meaning: index set of the vertices of the scenario-s convex hull
vertex column of the convex hull of scenario s

children.title: Tree-Integrated Column Generation
children.top_down_role: Column generation embedded in exact tree search.

children.title: SMIP Column Pricing
children.top_down_role: Scenario-structured generation of columns during tree search.

knowledge_statements.title: SMIP Column Pricing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact scenario pricing for a restricted Dantzig–Wolfe master at one search-tree node.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given restricted-master duals \(\pi\) and \(\alpha_s\), solve for every scenario \(s\)
\[z_s^*\in\arg\min_{z\in X_s^N}(p_sc_s-A_s^T\pi)^Tz-\alpha_s,\]
where \(X_s^N\) includes the branching restrictions active at node \(N\). If the optimal reduced cost \(\bar c_s<0\), append column \(v=z_s^*\) to the scenario block of the master and reoptimize. Stop when \(\bar c_s\ge0\) for every scenario; then the restricted-master solution is optimal for the node’s full current Dantzig–Wolfe relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve one mixed-integer reduced-cost problem per scenario, add every improving scenario solution as a column, and stop when no scenario has a negative reduced-cost column.
assumptions_latex: Each pricing problem over \(X_s^N\) is solved globally.
The restricted master and pricing problems use consistent dual and reduced-cost signs.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Absence of a negative reduced-cost scenario column certifies optimality for the full current node relaxation.

notation.meaning: scenario feasible set restricted by node N

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm is mathematically plausible, but the cited generic Dantzig–Wolfe section does not establish node-restricted SMIP pricing or the tree-node optimality certificate. A branch-and-price or tree-integrated SMIP source is required.

children.title: Branching-Compatible Columns
children.top_down_role: Column representations that remain usable under search-tree restrictions.

knowledge_statements.title: Branching-Compatible Columns
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compatibility condition ensuring generated columns respect the active branch-and-bound node.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let node \(N\) impose a branching predicate \(B_N(z)=1\). A scenario column \(v_{sk}\in X_s\) is branching-compatible at \(N\) exactly when \(B_N(v_{sk})=1\). A column-generation formulation is branching-compatible if every active branching disjunction can be enforced both in the restricted master and in each affected pricing domain \(X_s^N=\{z\in X_s:B_N(z)=1\}\). Consequently, all newly generated columns satisfy the node restrictions, and columns violating them are fixed to zero or removed from the node master.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A node may use only columns satisfying its branching decisions, and pricing must impose those same decisions so that it cannot regenerate forbidden columns.
assumptions_latex: The active branching predicate is well defined on complete scenario columns.
Each affected pricing problem can represent the predicate without changing its intended feasible set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every column available at node \(N\) represents a point feasible for that node’s branching restrictions.

notation.meaning: predicate formed by branching decisions active at node N

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source is supplied. Moreover, not every branching rule is representable by a predicate on individual scenario columns; support is needed for the stated compatibility condition and the treatment of existing columns.

children.title: Tree-Integrated Pricing
children.top_down_role: Placement of pricing operations within exact mixed-integer search.

knowledge_statements.title: Tree-Integrated Pricing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Column pricing embedded in branch-and-bound with node-specific domains and inherited columns.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
At a branch-and-bound node \(N\), inherit all ancestor columns satisfying \(B_N\), solve the restricted node master, and obtain duals \((\pi_N,\alpha_{sN})\). For each scenario solve
\[\bar c_{sN}=\min_{z\in X_s^N}(p_sc_s-A_s^T\pi_N)^Tz-\alpha_{sN}.\]
Add an optimizer whenever \(\bar c_{sN}<0\), then reoptimize and repeat. Fathom by the relaxation bound only after every exact pricing problem returns \(\bar c_{sN}\ge0\); otherwise branch from a fully priced fractional solution or accept a valid incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At each tree node, price over the node-restricted scenario sets and permit bound-based pruning only after exact pricing proves that no improving column remains.
assumptions_latex: Branching-compatible node domains \(X_s^N\) are available.
Pricing is exact before a node is pruned by its bound.
Inherited columns are filtered against the node predicate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The bound used for node fathoming equals the optimum of the node’s full current Dantzig–Wolfe relaxation.

notation.meaning: minimum reduced cost for scenario s at node N

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The content kind and local topic fit, but the correctness of inherited-column filtering, exact node pricing, and bound-based fathoming requires an authoritative branch-and-price or tree-integrated decomposition source.

children.title: Column-Cut Generation Coupling
children.top_down_role: Hybrid enrichment of primal columns and dual inequalities.

children.title: Scenario Column Generation
children.top_down_role: Primal enrichment through scenario-derived columns.

knowledge_statements.title: Scenario Column Generation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scenario-wise column generation inside a master that may also accumulate valid cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize finite column pools \(K_s^0\subset X_s\) giving a feasible restricted master. At iteration \(t\), optimize the master over \(K_s^t\), including every currently retained valid cut, and obtain dual multipliers. For each scenario solve its reduced-cost problem over \(X_s\). If an optimizer has negative reduced cost, set \(K_s^{t+1}=K_s^t\cup\{z_s^t\}\); otherwise leave that pool unchanged. After all pools have no improving column, invoke the designated cut-separation oracle. Terminate only when neither pricing nor separation finds a violation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Alternate master optimization with scenario pricing, adding improving scenario columns; when pricing closes, check whether the current master solution violates any designated valid cut.
assumptions_latex: The initial restricted master is feasible or a feasibility-pricing phase is used.
Scenario pricing and the designated separation oracle are exact at termination.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At termination, no omitted scenario column has negative reduced cost and no cut in the designated separated family is violated.

notation.meaning: scenario-s column pool at iteration t
scenario pricing optimizer generated at iteration t

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cited Dantzig–Wolfe section may support scenario pricing but does not by itself support the added cut-separation phase or the joint termination rule. A source treating combined column-and-cut generation is required.

children.title: Dual Cut Generation
children.top_down_role: Dual enrichment through scenario-valid inequalities.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual Cut Generation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separation of omitted inequalities in a dual master associated with scenario column generation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the current restricted dual master have feasible region \(D_t\), and let \(D\) denote the dual region obtained when all primal scenario columns are present. Given an optimizer \(u^t\in D_t\), call a separation oracle for \(D\). If it returns a valid inequality \(a^Tu\le\beta\) with \(a^Tu^t>\beta\), append that inequality and reoptimize; otherwise declare \(u^t\in D\). Under primal-dual correspondence, the separating inequality is the dual constraint induced by a scenario column whose reduced cost has the improving sign.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A restricted dual solution is tested against omitted dual constraints. Each violation adds a cut, equivalently revealing an improving primal scenario column.
assumptions_latex: The primal restricted master and displayed dual use mutually consistent signs.
The separation oracle distinguishes membership in the full dual region \(D\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Oracle acceptance certifies dual feasibility with respect to every omitted scenario-column constraint.

notation.meaning: restricted dual feasible region at iteration t

source_refs.locator: 3.5 Cutting Plane Method for the Solution of the All Integer Variable Linear Programming Problem p. 76

source_witnesses.locator: 3.5 Cutting Plane Method for the Solution of the All Integer Variable Linear Programming Problem p. 76

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The primal-column/dual-constraint correspondence is plausible, but the cited generic integer cutting-plane and Dantzig–Wolfe sections do not reliably establish this exact dual-master separation algorithm or its sign conventions.

children.title: Column–Cut Coordination
children.top_down_role: Interaction between primal columns plus dual inequalities during decomposition.

knowledge_statements.title: Column–Cut Coordination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Joint closure rule for a restricted master under column pricing and valid-inequality separation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Starting from a feasible restricted master, repeat: optimize it; call all scenario pricing oracles; add every selected negative-reduced-cost column; reoptimize if any column was added; then call the cut-separation oracle at the resulting solution and add every selected violated valid cut. Because a new cut changes master dual multipliers and a new column changes the point being separated, restart pricing after cuts and restart separation after columns. Terminate only after one complete cycle returns neither an improving column nor a violated cut.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Columns and cuts are generated in a feedback loop because either addition can invalidate the other oracle’s previous conclusion; termination requires a complete clean cycle.
assumptions_latex: Every added column belongs to its full scenario set.
Every added inequality is valid for the full master formulation.
All required oracles are exact when termination is declared.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The terminal master solution is closed under both the chosen column-pricing problems and the chosen cut family.

notation.meaning: reduced cost reported by a pricing oracle
inequality returned by the separation oracle

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No evidence supports the prescribed oracle ordering, restart rules, or clean-cycle closure claim. A source for coordinated column-and-cut generation is needed.

children.title: Branch-Integrated SMIP Methods
children.top_down_role: Exact tree-search frameworks integrating recourse separation or scenario bounds.

children.title: Tree-Integrated Benders Separation
children.top_down_role: Benders separation embedded within mixed-integer branch-and-cut.

children.title: Tree-Based Benders Separation
children.top_down_role: Benders cut generation at nodes of a mixed-integer search tree.

knowledge_statements.title: Tree-Based Benders Separation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Benders feasibility and optimality separation performed at branch-and-bound node relaxations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At node \(N\), solve the current master relaxation and obtain \((x^N,\theta_s^N)\). For every scenario, solve the linear recourse problem at \(x^N\). An unbounded dual ray \(r_s\) yields the feasibility cut \(r_s^T(h_s-T_sx)\le0\). A dual optimal solution \(\pi_s\) with \(\pi_s^T(h_s-T_sx^N)>\theta_s^N\) yields the optimality cut \(\theta_s\ge\pi_s^T(h_s-T_sx)\). Add all violated cuts and reoptimize before bounding, branching, or accepting an incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At every tree node, scenario recourse duals separate infeasible first-stage points and underestimated recourse values before the node is otherwise processed.
assumptions_latex: For each scenario, recourse is a linear program with dual-feasible set independent of \(x\).
Strong duality applies whenever the recourse problem is feasible and bounded.
Node master variables satisfy the first-stage constraints active at \(N\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: After exact separation, the node solution violates neither a scenario feasibility cut nor a scenario optimality cut from the full recourse dual sets.

notation.meaning: current node master solution and scenario recourse estimate
optimal recourse-dual solution for scenario s
recourse-dual extreme ray for scenario s

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The recourse citation is insufficient for tree-integrated Benders separation. The feasibility-ray convention and requirement to separate before bounding, branching, or incumbent acceptance must be checked against a source specifying the recourse primal and dual.

children.title: Node-Level Recourse Evaluation
children.top_down_role: Recourse assessment associated with partial or integral node solutions.

knowledge_statements.title: Node-Level Recourse Evaluation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact scenario recourse evaluation for a candidate first-stage solution at one tree node.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(S\) be finite with probabilities \(p_s>0\) satisfying \(\sum_{s\in S}p_s=1\). Given a node solution \(x^N\in\mathbb{R}^n\), define for every \(s\in S\)
\[Q_s(x^N)=\min\left\{q_s^Ty:W_sy=h_s-T_sx^N,\ y\in Y_s\right\},\]
where \(q_s\in\mathbb{R}^{m_s}\), \(Y_s\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{m_s}\), \(W_s\in\mathbb{R}^{\ell_s\times m_s}\), \(h_s\in\mathbb{R}^{\ell_s}\), and \(T_s\in\mathbb{R}^{\ell_s\times n}\). Solve every scenario problem to a certified global result. If one is infeasible, return its scenario index and the available solver-verifiable infeasibility certificate. Otherwise return \(Q(x^N)=\sum_{s\in S}p_sQ_s(x^N)\) and globally optimal recourse solutions. When \(Y_s\) defines a continuous linear program, valid optimal dual solutions or rays may additionally be returned for Benders separation; no such LP-dual conclusion is implied for mixed-integer \(Y_s\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a tree node, solve every scenario recourse problem globally. Report certified infeasibility if any scenario fails; otherwise return the exact probability-weighted recourse value. LP dual separation objects are returned only for continuous linear recourse.
assumptions_latex: \(S\) is finite, \(p_s>0\) for every \(s\in S\), and \(\sum_{s\in S}p_s=1\).
Each scenario solver certifies infeasibility or global optimality.
Dual separation objects are claimed only when the corresponding recourse problem is a continuous linear program and the relevant duality conditions hold.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The procedure returns either certified recourse infeasibility or the exact expected recourse value at \(x^N\), without treating mixed-integer recourse as an LP-dual subproblem.

notation.meaning: probability-weighted recourse value at the node solution

children.title: Benders Cut Persistence
children.top_down_role: Validity plus reuse of Benders cuts across search-tree nodes.

knowledge_statements.title: Benders Cut Persistence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity and reuse of globally or locally derived Benders cuts across a search tree.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F_N\) be the projected feasible set at node \(N\). A Benders cut \(a^Tx+b^T\theta\le d\) is globally persistent if it is valid for the root set \(F_0\); then it remains valid for every descendant because \(F_N\subseteq F_0\). A cut derived using node-local bounds or assumptions is persistent only within a subtree whose feasible sets satisfy those assumptions. Such a local cut must not be enforced at an unrelated node unless its validity for that node is established independently.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Root-valid Benders cuts remain valid throughout the tree. Cuts relying on local bounds may be reused only in descendants where those bounds or assumptions still hold.
assumptions_latex: Every descendant feasible set is contained in its ancestor feasible set.
The cut’s derivation records all bounds and assumptions used to establish validity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Global cuts may be retained at all nodes, whereas local cuts may be retained only on validity-preserving descendant subtrees.

notation.meaning: projected feasible set at node N

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The set-inclusion argument is plausible, but the record has no citation for distinguishing globally valid Benders cuts from cuts whose validity depends on node-local assumptions. A branch-and-Benders source is required.

children.title: Deferred-Check Tree Search
children.top_down_role: Deferred recourse evaluation and cut enforcement during tree search.

children.title: Deferred Recourse Checking
children.top_down_role: Recourse evaluation postponed until selected search-tree solutions.

knowledge_statements.title: Deferred Recourse Checking
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lazy recourse validation postponed until a tree solution reaches a prescribed checking event.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Solve a first-stage master in which some recourse constraints or value-function inequalities are initially omitted. Whenever the search produces a checking point \((\hat x,\hat\theta)\), solve every required scenario recourse problem at \(\hat x\). If recourse is infeasible, reject the point and add a valid feasibility constraint; if \(\hat\theta_s<Q_s(\hat x)\), add a valid recourse-value constraint and reject or reoptimize. Accept the point only when all scenarios are feasible and every retained recourse estimate satisfies \(\hat\theta_s\ge Q_s(\hat x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Recourse is omitted temporarily, then evaluated at designated candidate points; infeasible or underestimated candidates are rejected and repaired with valid constraints.
assumptions_latex: Every potentially accepted incumbent triggers exact checking of all required scenarios.
Generated feasibility and recourse-value constraints are valid for the intended tree scope.
The algorithm cannot terminate while an unchecked incumbent could improve the objective.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every accepted incumbent is recourse-feasible and carries no underestimated scenario recourse value.

notation.meaning: first-stage candidate subjected to deferred checking
master estimate of scenario-s recourse value
exact scenario-s recourse value at the candidate

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source supports the deferred checking protocol. In particular, the existence and tree scope of a valid feasibility or recourse-value constraint depends on whether recourse is linear or mixed-integer and on the chosen decomposition method.

children.title: Incumbent Feasibility Checks
children.top_down_role: Recourse validation focused on candidate integer incumbents.

knowledge_statements.title: Incumbent Feasibility Checks
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Acceptance certificate for a candidate first-stage incumbent under finite-scenario recourse.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(S\) be finite, let \(p_s\ge0\) satisfy \(\sum_{s\in S}p_s=1\), and consider a two-stage minimization model with first-stage feasible set \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\), first-stage cost \(c\in\mathbb{R}^n\), and, for each \(s\in S\), recourse domain \(Y_s\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{m_s}\), cost \(q_s\in\mathbb{R}^{m_s}\), and constraint \(W_sy_s=h_s-T_sx\). For a candidate integer first-stage point \(\hat x\), a recourse-feasibility certificate consists of verification that \(\hat x\in X\) and vectors \(\hat y_s\in Y_s\) satisfying
\[W_s\hat y_s=h_s-T_s\hat x\qquad\text{for every }s\in S.\]
These vectors certify feasibility of \((\hat x,(\hat y_s)_{s\in S})\). For the stated minimization model they also provide the feasible objective value
\[c^T\hat x+\sum_{s\in S}p_sq_s^T\hat y_s,\]
which is an upper bound on the optimal objective value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An incumbent is feasible when its first-stage constraints hold and an explicit feasible recourse vector is verified for every scenario. The supplied vectors also give a feasible objective value and hence an upper bound for the minimization model.
assumptions_latex: \(S\) is finite, \(p_s\ge0\) for every \(s\in S\), and \(\sum_{s\in S}p_s=1\).
The candidate \(\hat x\) satisfies all first-stage integrality and deterministic constraints represented by \(X\).
Every supplied \(\hat y_s\) is checked against the original domain \(Y_s\) and recourse equality.
The objective-bound statement concerns a minimization model with finite displayed costs.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The supplied first- and second-stage vectors constitute a directly verifiable feasibility certificate and yield a feasible upper bound for the finite-scenario minimization model.

notation.meaning: supplied feasible recourse vector for scenario s
first-stage feasible set, including its integrality restrictions

children.title: Tree-Level Cut Enforcement
children.top_down_role: Placement of recourse-derived cuts within mixed-integer search.

assumptions_latex: \(N\) is a node of a minimization branch-and-bound tree with region \(D_N\).
Every generated inequality is proved valid either on the full feasible set or on a recorded ancestor region.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_M\le z_M^*\) remains valid for every processed node \(M\).

notation.meaning: Region represented by tree node N
Certified lower bound at node N

review_flags: missing_method_specific_source: authoritative source for deferred-check SMIP tree enforcement is required
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity rule for globally and locally generated recourse cuts in a minimization tree.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a processed node \(N\), each recourse or feasibility cut \(a^{\mathsf T}x\ge b\) shall carry a validity region \(D_A\), where \(A\) is the node at which local validity was established; globally valid cuts use the root region. The cut is enforced at node \(M\) exactly when \(D_M\subseteq D_A\). If a deferred recourse check finds that an incumbent or relaxation point violates such a cut, every open node \(M\) satisfying \(D_M\subseteq D_A\) must incorporate the cut or be reprocessed before its bound can certify pruning. Bounds computed without all applicable cuts are provisional and cannot justify permanent fathoming.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each cut is enforced throughout its certified subtree; bounds missing an applicable cut cannot permanently prune nodes.
knowledge_statements.title: Tree-Level Cut Enforcement

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The principle fits the leaf, but no citation supports the deferred-check enforcement rule. The conclusion also uses M, L_M, and z_M^* without introducing them consistently.

children.title: Spatial Branching Bound System
children.top_down_role: Branching frameworks used when decomposition relaxations do not enforce the full master domain.

children.title: Spatial Branching for SMIP
children.top_down_role: Domain partitioning for stochastic mixed-integer decomposition relaxations.

assumptions_latex: The node region restricts a bounded continuous coordinate by \(\ell_j<u_j\).
Node lower bounds are obtained from valid relaxations of the restricted SMIP.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D_{N^-}\cup D_{N^+}=D_N\) and \(D_{N^-}\cap D_{N^+}=\varnothing\) under the stated half-open convention.

notation.meaning: Feasible domain represented by node N
Selected branching coordinate and split value

review_flags: missing_method_specific_source: spatial branch-and-bound formulation for stochastic MIP requires confirmation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Binary spatial branching on bounded nonintegral domains within a stochastic branch-and-bound tree.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given an unfathomed node \(N\), choose a coordinate \(j\) and split point \(\tau\in(\ell_j,u_j)\), preferably using relaxation violation or scenario disagreement. Create children \(N^-\) and \(N^+\) with \(D_{N^-}=D_N\cap\{x:x_j\le\tau\}\) and \(D_{N^+}=D_N\cap\{x:x_j>\tau\}\). Recompute a valid stochastic relaxation bound in each child, including all cuts valid on that child. Fathom a child only if its relaxation is infeasible or its lower bound is no smaller than the incumbent value. Otherwise continue splitting until integrality and recourse feasibility are certified.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Split a bounded coordinate, recompute valid stochastic lower bounds in both children, and prune only by certified infeasibility or dominance.
knowledge_statements.title: Spatial Branching for SMIP

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithmic kind and partitioning rule fit spatial branching, but the SMIP-specific branching, bounding, and fathoming procedure has no inspectable source.

children.title: Spatial Lower Bounds
children.top_down_role: Node bounds derived from restricted spatial regions.

assumptions_latex: The original node problem is a minimization problem with feasible set \(F_N\).
The relaxation satisfies \(F_N\subseteq R_N\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_N:=\inf_{x\in R_N}f(x)\le z_N^*:=\inf_{x\in F_N}f(x)\).

notation.meaning: Original feasible set at node N
Relaxed feasible set at node N

review_flags: missing_source: exact spatial-relaxation bound system intended by the taxonomy is not identified
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lower-bound property for domain and recourse relaxations at an SMIP tree node.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a node \(N\), let \(F_N\) contain all first-stage restrictions, integrality conditions, and scenario-wise recourse constraints applicable at that node. Any tractable set \(R_N\) obtained by relaxing integrality, nonanticipativity, nonconvex constraints, or recourse conditions is a valid lower-bound relaxation when \(F_N\subseteq R_N\) and the objective is unchanged or replaced by a pointwise lower estimator. Its optimal value \(L_N=\inf_{x\in R_N}f(x)\) is then no greater than the node optimum \(z_N^*=\inf_{x\in F_N}f(x)\). Tightening \(R_N\) while retaining \(F_N\subseteq R_N\) cannot decrease \(L_N\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Optimizing over any valid superset of the node-feasible set gives a lower bound; tightening that superset can only improve the bound.
knowledge_statements.title: Spatial Lower Bounds

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The lower-bound and monotonicity claims are mathematically standard, but no source identifies this generic relaxation property as the intended spatial lower-bound system in the local taxonomy.

children.title: Domain-Relaxation Gaps
children.top_down_role: Residual gaps caused by incomplete enforcement of the master domain.

assumptions_latex: Both values refer to the same minimization node and objective.
The relaxation contains the original node-feasible set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Delta_N=z_N^*-L_N\ge0\), with \(\Delta_N=0\) exactly when the relaxation value is exact.

notation.meaning: Optimal value of the original node problem
Optimal value of the node relaxation

review_flags: missing_source: terminology and normalization for domain-relaxation gaps require source confirmation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Absolute and relative gaps between a node problem and its spatial relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a minimization node \(N\) with finite original optimum \(z_N^*\) and valid relaxation value \(L_N\), the absolute domain-relaxation gap is \(\Delta_N:=z_N^*-L_N\). When a scale-free measure is required and \(|z_N^*|>0\), define \(\delta_N:=\Delta_N/|z_N^*|\). If \(z_N^*=L_N\), the relaxation is value-exact at \(N\), although a relaxed optimizer need not itself satisfy integrality or recourse feasibility. If \(L_N=-\infty\) while \(z_N^*\) is finite, the absolute gap is \(+\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The domain-relaxation gap is the node optimum minus its relaxation bound; a zero value gap does not guarantee a feasible relaxed optimizer.
knowledge_statements.title: Domain-Relaxation Gaps

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition is internally coherent, including the infinite-gap convention, but the claimed domain-relaxation terminology and relative-gap normalization lack a source.

children.title: Progressive-Hedging Tree Search
children.top_down_role: Exact tree-search frameworks using progressive-hedging information and bounds.

children.title: Progressive-Hedging Tree Guidance
children.top_down_role: Scenario-consensus information used to guide exact tree search.

assumptions_latex: Scenario probabilities satisfy \(p_s>0\) and \(\sum_s p_s=1\).
Each scenario subproblem respects the current tree-node restrictions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The iteration returns scenario solutions, consensus values, and disagreement scores usable as tree-search guidance, not as feasibility certificates.
review_flags: missing_method_specific_source: use of progressive hedging as branch-tree guidance needs an authoritative algorithm reference
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Progressive-hedging iterates used heuristically to prioritize nodes and branching variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At tree node \(N\), initialize \(\bar x^0\), multipliers \(w_s^0\) satisfying \(\sum_s p_s w_s^0=0\), and \(\rho>0\). At iteration \(k\), solve each restricted scenario problem minimizing \(F_s(x_s)+(w_s^k)^{\mathsf T}x_s+(\rho/2)\|x_s-\bar x^k\|_2^2\). A forward pass solves the root and successive node problems using \(\underline V_n\), producing trial states \(r_n^k\) and a feasible policy when possible. children.title: Nonconvex Nested Benders

assumptions_latex: A minimization master uses cuts intended to underestimate a continuation value.
The continuation value need not be convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The affine function \(z\) is not a valid global lower estimator of \(Q\) on \([0,1]\).
review_flags: missing_source: concrete nonconvex nested-Benders failure example requires external verification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of ordinary convex Benders supporting cuts for a nonconvex value function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(Q(z)=\min\{z,1-z\}\) on \([0,1]\). At \(z=0\), the active affine piece has slope \(1\), so the ordinary convex-Benders construction would propose \(Q(z)\ge Q(0)+1(z-0)=z\), represented in a master by \(\theta\ge z\). This inequality is false: at \(z=3/4\), \(Q(3/4)=1/4<3/4\). Hence a local slope or active-piece affine function need not be a global lower estimator when the stage value function is nonconvex. Valid nonconvex nested decomposition must instead use globally valid disjunctive, enumerative, or other certified underestimators.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a nonconvex continuation value, an affine cut derived from a local active piece can overestimate the value and invalidate the master bound.
knowledge_statements.title: Nonconvex Nested Benders

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The counterexample is mathematically correct, but a failure boundary alone does not fill a topic whose stated role is nonconvex nested-Benders frameworks. A source is needed before deciding whether this example belongs here or should support a framework-level record.

children.title: Binary-State SDDiP
children.top_down_role: SDDiP architectures specialized to binary linking states.

knowledge_statements.title: Binary-State SDDiP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Forward-backward SDDiP using valid integer-optimality cuts on finite binary linking states.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let the stage-t linking state satisfy \(s_t\in\{0,1\}^{m_t}\), and let \(L_t\le Q_t(s)\) for every binary state. Initialize \(\widehat Q_t^0=L_t\). At iteration \(k\), simulate a forward policy using \(\widehat Q_{t+1}^{k-1}\). In the backward pass, evaluate \(q=Q_t(\bar s)\) at each sampled predecessor state \(\bar s\) and append the valid cut
\[Q_t(s)\ge q-(q-L_t)\left(\sum_{i:\bar s_i=0}s_i+\sum_{i:\bar s_i=1}(1-s_i)\right).\]
Set \(\widehat Q_t^k\) equal to the maximum of all accumulated lower cuts, and output the incumbent forward policy when the prescribed iteration or statistical stopping rule is met.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Forward simulation chooses decisions; backward evaluation adds binary-state integer-optimality cuts whose maximum is a lower value-function approximation.
assumptions_latex: \(L_t\le Q_t(s)\quad\forall s\in\{0,1\}^{m_t}\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat Q_t^k(s)\le Q_t(s)\quad\forall s\in\{0,1\}^{m_t}\)

notation.meaning: global lower bound on the cost-to-go

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The binary-state cut is mathematically valid on the stated finite domain, but the complete SDDiP forward-backward algorithm and stopping description have no cited source.

children.title: General-Integer-State SDDiP

knowledge_statements.title: General-Integer-State SDDiP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: SDDiP lower approximations for bounded integer linking states.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(z_t\in\mathbb Z^{m_t}\) satisfy finite bounds and let \(L_t\le Q_t(z)\) on that integer box. Initialize \(\widehat Q_t^0=L_t\), perform an approximate forward simulation, and in the backward pass evaluate \(q=Q_t(\bar z)\) at each sampled integer state. Append
\[Q_t(z)\ge q-(q-L_t)\sum_{i=1}^{m_t}|z_i-\bar z_i|,\]
using standard linear epigraph variables for the absolute values. Update \(\widehat Q_t^k\) as the maximum of accumulated cuts. Stop under a declared iteration or statistical rule and return the best forward policy found.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The method extends SDDiP to bounded integer states by adding valid cuts that separate every integer state from the evaluated state.
assumptions_latex: \(z_t\in\{z\in\mathbb Z^{m_t}:\ell_t\le z\le u_t\}\)
\(L_t\le Q_t(z)\quad\forall z\in[\ell_t,u_t]\cap\mathbb Z^{m_t}\)

knowledge_statements.title: Mixed-Integer-State Value Approximations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: State-indexed approximations preserving discrete state distinctions and continuous-state dependence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Partition the linking state as \((z,y)\), where \(z\) ranges over a finite integer set \(Z\) and \(y\in Y_z\subseteq\mathbb R^p\). A mixed-integer-state polyhedral lower approximation has the representation
\[\widehat Q(z,y)=\max_{j\in J_z}\{\alpha_{zj}+\beta_{zj}^{\mathsf T}y\},\qquad z\in Z,\ y\in Y_z.\]
If every indexed affine function satisfies \(\alpha_{zj}+\beta_{zj}^{\mathsf T}y\le Q(z,y)\) on \(Y_z\), then \(\widehat Q\le Q\). In a finite-scenario model, the index selection can be implemented by state indicators or disjunctive mixed-integer constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Separate affine cut collections are retained for each discrete state, while continuous state components enter each cut affinely.
assumptions_latex: \(Z\subset\mathbb Z^m\text{ is finite}\)
\(Y_z\subseteq\mathbb R^p\quad\forall z\in Z\)
\(\alpha_{zj}+\beta_{zj}^{\mathsf T}y\le Q(z,y)\quad\forall y\in Y_z\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat Q(z,y)\le Q(z,y)\quad\forall z\in Z,\ y\in Y_z\)

notation.meaning: discrete and continuous components of the linking state
cut indices associated with discrete state z

The implementation claim also requires representability and typically boundedness assumptions not stated here.

children.title: Stagewise Resource Decomposition
children.top_down_role: Multistage decomposition organized around stage-specific resource allocations.

knowledge_statements.title: Stagewise Resource Decomposition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bellman decomposition using inherited resources as the interstage state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For stages \(t=1,\ldots,T\), let \(r_t\) be the resource inherited from stage \(t-1\). Under stagewise conditional independence and a Markov transition \(r_{t+1}=R_t(r_t,x_t,\xi_t)\), define \(V_{T+1}=0\) and
\[V_t(r_t,\xi_t)=\min_{x_t\in X_t(r_t,\xi_t)}\left\{c_t(x_t,\xi_t)+\mathbb E\left[V_{t+1}(R_t(r_t,x_t,\xi_t),\xi_{t+1})\mid\xi_t\right]\right\}.\]
Thus each stage subproblem communicates with adjacent stages only through the resource state and its continuation value; integrality may be imposed in \(X_t\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The multistage model decomposes by stage when inherited resources form a sufficient Markov state for future costs and feasibility.
assumptions_latex: \(x_t\in X_t(r_t,\xi_t)\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(V_t(r_t,\xi_t)=\min_{x_t\in X_t(r_t,\xi_t)}\{c_t(x_t,\xi_t)+\mathbb E[V_{t+1}(r_{t+1},\xi_{t+1})\mid\xi_t]\}\)

children.title: Resource-Coupling Master Problems
children.top_down_role: Master representations coordinating resources shared across stages or scenarios.

knowledge_statements.title: Resource-Coupling Master Problems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Master formulation coordinating stage or scenario subproblems through shared resource allocations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(N\) index decomposed subproblems, let \(r_n\) be their allocated resources, and let \(Q_n(r_n)\) denote their optimal costs. A resource-coupling master problem is
\[\min_{r,\theta}\ \sum_{n\in N}p_n\theta_n\quad\text{subject to}\quad \sum_{n\in N}A_nr_n=b,\quad r_n\in R_n,\quad \theta_n\ge \phi_{nj}(r_n)\ \ (j\in J_n).\]
Each \(\phi_{nj}\) is a valid lower estimator of \(Q_n\). Consequently the master objective is a lower bound on the coupled problem; exactness holds when the accumulated estimators reproduce every \(Q_n\) at an optimal resource allocation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A master allocates coupled resources and represents each subproblem cost through valid lower estimators, yielding a global lower bound.
assumptions_latex: \(p_n\ge0\quad\forall n\in N\)
\(\phi_{nj}(r_n)\le Q_n(r_n)\quad\forall r_n\in R_n\)
\(\sum_{n\in N}A_nr_n=b\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v_{\mathrm{master}}\le\min\{\sum_{n\in N}p_nQ_n(r_n):r_n\in R_n,\ \sum_{n\in N}A_nr_n=b\}\)

notation.meaning: master epigraph variable for subproblem cost

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The lower-bound direction follows from nonnegative weights and valid subproblem minorants, but no source supports the named resource-coupling master architecture or its exactness characterization.

children.title: Binary Expansion of Integer States

knowledge_statements.title: Binary Expansion of Integer States
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact radix-two encoding of bounded nonnegative integer linking states.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For an integer state component \(z_i\) with \(0\le z_i\le U_i\), set \(K_i=\lceil\log_2(U_i+1)\rceil\) and introduce \(b_{ik}\in\{0,1\}\). The exact encoding is
\[z_i=\sum_{k=0}^{K_i-1}2^k b_{ik},\qquad \sum_{k=0}^{K_i-1}2^k b_{ik}\le U_i.\]
For a general bound \(L_i\le z_i\le U_i\), encode \(z_i-L_i\) analogously. Replacing every occurrence of \(z_i\) by this expression preserves feasible integer states and objective values, although the encoding need not be one-to-one if redundant bits are introduced.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A bounded integer state is represented exactly by binary digits plus an upper-bound constraint, enabling binary-state decomposition machinery.

\(0\le z_i\le U_i<\infty\)

knowledge_statements.title: Multistage State Lifting
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact reformulation by embedding each stage state in an extended space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let the original stage state be \(s_t\in S_t\). A multistage lifting introduces \(y_t\in Y_t\) and constraints \((s_t,y_t)\in L_t\) such that the projection satisfies
\[\operatorname{proj}_{s_t}(L_t)=S_t.\]
Original transitions and costs are replaced by extended constraints and functions whose restrictions on \(L_t\) agree with the originals. If every feasible original state trajectory admits a compatible lifted trajectory and every feasible lifted trajectory projects to an original feasible trajectory with the same objective value, then the lifted and original multistage problems have equal optimal values and corresponding projected policies.

children.title: Multistage State Augmentation

knowledge_statements.title: Multistage State Augmentation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Adding recursively updated information to obtain a sufficient multistage state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given an original state \(s_t\) and observed history \(h_t\), choose an auxiliary statistic \(a_t=A_t(h_t)\) with recursion \(a_{t+1}=F_t(a_t,x_t,\xi_{t+1})\). The augmented state is \(\widetilde s_t=(s_t,a_t)\). It is a valid Markov augmentation when, for every admissible policy, the conditional distribution of future disturbances, feasible actions, transitions, and costs given \(h_t\) depends on the history only through \(\widetilde s_t\). Under this sufficiency condition, policies measurable in \(\widetilde s_t\) attain the same optimum as history-dependent policies.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: State augmentation adds a recursively updated statistic that makes future feasibility, costs, and uncertainty conditionally independent of the remaining history.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_{\pi\in\Pi_{\mathrm{Markov}}(\widetilde s)}J(\pi)=\inf_{\pi\in\Pi_{\mathrm{history}}}J(\pi)\)

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition is mathematically plausible, but a section on post-decision states does not clearly support the general history-sufficiency condition or equality between Markov and history-dependent policy optima.

children.title: Lifted-State Projection

knowledge_statements.title: Lifted-State Projection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditions under which projection recovers the original feasible policies and value.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\) be an original multistage problem and \(\widetilde P\) a lifted problem with trajectory projection \(\rho(\widetilde s,\widetilde x)=(s,x)\). Suppose \(rho\) maps every nonanticipative feasible lifted trajectory to a feasible trajectory of \(P\), every feasible trajectory of \(P\) has a nonanticipative lifted preimage, and corresponding trajectories have identical scenario-wise costs. Then projection preserves feasibility, nonanticipativity, and expected objective values. Hence the optimal values coincide, and the projection of any optimal lifted policy is optimal for \(P\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A lifted formulation is exact when projection is feasible and cost-preserving and every original trajectory has a nonanticipative lifted preimage.
assumptions_latex: \(\rho(\mathcal F_{\widetilde P})=\mathcal F_P\)
\(C_{\widetilde P}(\widetilde s,\widetilde x,\omega)=C_P(\rho(\widetilde s,\widetilde x),\omega)\quad\text{a.s.}\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v(\widetilde P)=v(P)\quad\text{and}\quad\rho(\operatorname{Opt}(\widetilde P))\subseteq\operatorname{Opt}(P)\)

children.title: Restricted Adaptive Policies
children.top_down_role: Multistage discrete policies limited to selected adaptive structures.

knowledge_statements.title: Restricted Adaptive Policies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optimization over a prescribed subclass of feasible nonanticipative history-dependent policies.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For each stage \(t=1,\ldots,T\), let \(H_t\) be the history space, let \(\mathcal A_t\) be an ambient mixed-integer action space, and let \(X_t(h_t)\subseteq\mathcal A_t\) be the feasible action set at history \(h_t\in H_t\). A restricted adaptive policy class is a specified family
\[\Pi_\Theta=\left\{\pi^\theta:\theta\in\Theta,\ \pi_t^\theta:H_t\to\mathcal A_t,\ \pi_t^\theta(h_t)\in X_t(h_t)\ \text{for all }h_t\in H_t,\ t=1,\ldots,T\right\},\]
where every \(\pi_t^\theta\) is measurable and nonanticipative. If \(\Pi\) denotes the full class of feasible nonanticipative policies and \(\Pi_\Theta\subseteq\Pi\), the restricted stochastic program minimizes \(J(\pi^\theta)=\mathbb E[C(\pi^\theta,\xi)]\) over \(\theta\in\Theta\). Consequently, for a minimization problem, its optimal value is no smaller than the optimum over \(\Pi\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A restricted adaptive policy is a measurable, feasible, nonanticipative policy selected from a parameterized subclass of the full admissible policy space.
assumptions_latex: \(\pi_t^\theta(h_t)\in X_t(h_t)\subseteq\mathcal A_t\quad\forall h_t\in H_t\)
\(\pi_t^\theta\text{ is measurable and nonanticipative}\)
\(\Pi_\Theta\subseteq\Pi\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_{\theta\in\Theta}J(\pi^\theta)\ge\inf_{\pi\in\Pi}J(\pi)\)
