children.title: Decision-Rule SMIP
children.top_down_role: Stochastic mixed-integer models using parameterized decision rules.

knowledge_statements.title: Decision-Rule SMIP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-scenario SMIP obtained by parameterizing adaptive decisions with prescribed decision rules.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
On a finite scenario tree, let \(h_n\) be the information at node \(n\), and prescribe \(x_n=f_t(h_n;\theta_t)\) for every node in stage \(t\). Substitution into the deterministic equivalent gives
\[\min_{\theta}\ \sum_{n}p_n c_n^{\mathsf T}f_{t(n)}(h_n;\theta_{t(n)})\quad\text{subject to}\quad f_{t(n)}(h_n;\theta_{t(n)})\in X_n\ \ \forall n.\]
Shared parameters for nodes with identical histories enforce nonanticipativity. If each \(f_t\) is mixed-integer representable and \(X_n\) is a mixed-integer linear set, this restricted model is an SMIP-representable deterministic equivalent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adaptive decisions are replaced by parameterized history-based rules; finite scenario constraints produce a restricted mixed-integer stochastic program.
assumptions_latex: \(p_n\ge0\quad\text{and}\quad\sum_np_n=1\)
\(f_t(\cdot;\theta_t)\text{ is nonanticipative and mixed-integer representable}\)
\(X_n\text{ is mixed-integer linear}\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v_{\mathrm{rule}}\ge v_{\mathrm{SMIP}}\)

notation.meaning: information observed at scenario-tree node n

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cited generic sections do not establish the mixed-integer decision-rule formulation. Nonanticipativity is induced by a common history-based rule or node decisions, not merely by sharing parameters between nodes with identical histories, and the displayed model omits the original interstage coupling constraints unless these are explicitly included in X_n.

children.title: Policy-Class Approximation Gaps
children.top_down_role: Losses attributable to restrictions on multistage adaptive decisions.

knowledge_statements.title: Policy-Class Approximation Gaps
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optimal-value loss caused by restricting the admissible adaptive-policy class.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a minimization problem with admissible policy class \(\Pi\) and restricted subclass \(\Pi_\Theta\subseteq\Pi\), define
\[v^*=\inf_{\pi\in\Pi}J(\pi),\qquad v_\Theta=\inf_{\pi\in\Pi_\Theta}J(\pi),\qquad \Delta_\Theta=v_\Theta-v^*.\]
Whenever both values are finite, \(\Delta_\Theta\ge0\). If \(\Pi_{\Theta_1}\subseteq\Pi_{\Theta_2}\subseteq\Pi\), then \(\Delta_{\Theta_1}\ge\Delta_{\Theta_2}\). The gap is zero exactly when the restricted class contains policies whose objective values approach \(v^*\); if an optimal policy exists, inclusion of one such policy is sufficient.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Restricting policies cannot improve a minimization optimum; enlarging the policy class can only reduce the approximation gap.
assumptions_latex: \(\Pi_\Theta\subseteq\Pi\)
\(-\infty<v^*\le v_\Theta<\infty\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Delta_\Theta=v_\Theta-v^*\ge0\)

notation.meaning: optimal value over all admissible policies
optimal value over the restricted class

children.title: Multistage Benders Cuts
children.top_down_role: Stagewise cuts derived from continuous recourse relaxations.

knowledge_statements.title: Multistage Benders Cuts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Aggregated dual cuts for a finite-scenario child-stage linear recourse relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
At a scenario-tree node, let child \(j\) have conditional probability \(p_j\) and relaxed recourse value \(Q_j(x)=\min\{q_j^\top y:W_jy=h_j-T_jx,\ y\geq0\}\). If \(\pi_j\) is dual feasible, so \(W_j^\top\pi_j\leq q_j\), then weak duality gives \(Q_j(x)\geq\pi_j^\top(h_j-T_jx)\). Hence the multistage Benders inequality is
\[\theta\geq\sum_jp_j\pi_j^\top(h_j-T_jx).\]
It is a valid lower approximation of the conditional expected relaxed cost-to-go; equality holds at a trial state when every selected \(\pi_j\) is optimal there.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Child-recursion dual solutions produce an affine lower bound on conditional expected recourse, exact at a trial state when all child dual solutions are optimal.
assumptions_latex: \(p_j\geq0\) and \(\sum_jp_j=1\).
Each child linear recourse problem has a finite optimum at the states under consideration.
\(\pi_j\) is feasible for the displayed child dual.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\theta\geq\sum_jp_j\pi_j^\top(h_j-T_jx)\) is valid.

children.title: Strengthened Multistage Benders Cuts
children.top_down_role: Stagewise Benders cuts enhanced with mixed-integer recourse information.

knowledge_statements.title: Strengthened Multistage Benders Cuts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dominance criterion for replacing a baseline cost-to-go cut by a stronger valid cut.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D\) be the admissible state domain and let \(Q:D\to\mathbb R\) be the true conditional cost-to-go. Suppose \(b(x)=\alpha+\beta^\top x\) is a baseline Benders lower bound and \(s(x)=\bar\alpha+\bar\beta^\top x\) is another valid lower bound. The cut \(\theta\geq s(x)\) strengthens \(\theta\geq b(x)\) on \(D\) exactly when \(s(x)\geq b(x)\) for every \(x\in D\); the strengthening is strict when this inequality is strict for at least one feasible state. Adding the strengthened cut cannot decrease the master lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A valid cut strengthens a baseline cut when it dominates it throughout the state domain, with strict gain wherever the dominance is strict.
assumptions_latex: \(b(x)\leq Q(x)\) and \(s(x)\leq Q(x)\) for every \(x\in D\).
The master minimizes with \(\theta\) constrained below by accumulated cuts.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(s\geq b\) on \(D\) implies that replacing or supplementing \(b\) with \(s\) weakly raises the master bound.

children.title: Strengthening-Gain Regimes
children.top_down_role: Problem structures governing gains from stronger stage cuts.

knowledge_statements.title: Strengthening-Gain Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise and optimization-level regimes induced by nested lower approximations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D\) be a nonempty state domain, let \(Q:D\to\mathbb R\), and let \(b,s:D\to\mathbb R\) satisfy \(b(x)\leq s(x)\leq Q(x)\) for every \(x\in D\). Define the pointwise strengthening gain by \(g(x)=s(x)-b(x)\). Thus \(g(x)=0\) is the zero-gain regime and \(g(x)>0\) is the strict pointwise-gain regime. Let \(M\subseteq D\times\mathbb R\) be a common master feasible set and let \(c:D\to\mathbb R\). Define \[z_b=\inf\{c(x)+\theta:(x,\theta)\in M,\ \theta\geq b(x)\}\] and define \(z_s\) by replacing \(b\) with \(s\). Then \(z_s\geq z_b\). Moreover, if some \(\varepsilon>0\) satisfies \(c(x)+\theta\geq z_b+\varepsilon\) for every \((x,\theta)\in M\) with \(\theta\geq s(x)\), then \(z_s\geq z_b+\varepsilon\); pointwise strict gain at only one state need not produce strict master-value gain.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A dominating lower approximation has nonnegative pointwise gain and cannot lower the minimization master value. Strict gain at an isolated state need not raise the master optimum; a uniform positive separation of the strengthened feasible objectives does.
assumptions_latex: \(D\neq\varnothing\) and \(b(x)\leq s(x)\leq Q(x)\) for every \(x\in D\).
Both master infima use the same set \(M\) and objective \(c\) and are finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g(x)\geq0\) on \(D\) and \(z_s\geq z_b\).

children.title: Multistage Integer Optimality Cuts
children.top_down_role: Enumerative value cuts for discrete state points.

knowledge_statements.title: Multistage Integer Optimality Cuts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact point-value cut for a binary linking state and a known global lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(Q:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R\) be a stage cost-to-go function with known lower bound \(L\leq Q(x)\) for every binary state. After evaluating \(Q(\bar x)\), define the Hamming mismatch
\[\Delta(x,\bar x)=\sum_{i:\bar x_i=1}(1-x_i)+\sum_{i:\bar x_i=0}x_i.\]
Then
\[\theta\geq Q(\bar x)-\bigl(Q(\bar x)-L\bigr)\Delta(x,\bar x)\]
is valid for all binary states and certifies \(\theta\geq Q(\bar x)\) at \(x=\bar x\). For every other state, its right-hand side is at most \(L\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Hamming-distance cut records the exact cost-to-go at one binary state while falling to a valid global lower bound at every other state.
assumptions_latex: \(Q(x)\geq L\) for all \(x\in\{0,1\}^n\).
The evaluated value \(Q(\bar x)\) is exact and finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed inequality is valid and exact at \(\bar x\).

notation.meaning: Hamming distance from the evaluated state

children.title: Multistage Lagrangian Cuts
children.top_down_role: Stage cuts generated through Lagrangian treatment of linking states.

knowledge_statements.title: Multistage Lagrangian Cuts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Affine stage lower bounds obtained by dualizing the incoming-state linking equation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let
\[Q(x)=\inf\{f(y,z): (y,z)\in Y,\ z=x\}\]
be a stage value function, where \(x\) is the incoming linking state. For any multiplier \(\lambda\), define
\[\phi(\lambda)=\inf_{(y,z)\in Y}\bigl(f(y,z)-\lambda^\top z\bigr).\]
The Lagrangian cut
\[\theta\geq\lambda^\top x+\phi(\lambda)\]
is valid wherever \(Q(x)\) is finite. Taking the supremum over an available multiplier set produces the lower approximation \(Q(x)\geq\sup_\lambda\{\lambda^\top x+\phi(\lambda)\}\), without requiring convexity or integrality relaxation of \(Y\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dualizing the equality between incoming and local state copies yields affine lower bounds on the stage value function, including when local decisions are integer.
assumptions_latex: \(Y\) is nonempty and may contain integrality restrictions.
\(\phi(\lambda)>-\infty\) for each multiplier used to generate a cut.
\(Q(x)<+\infty\) at the state being bounded.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q(x)\geq\lambda^\top x+\phi(\lambda)\) for every admissible multiplier \(\lambda\).

notation.meaning: local copy of the linking state
multiplier for the equation equating the state copies

children.title: Finite-Convergence Families

children.title: Finite Convergence on Discrete Master Domains
children.top_down_role: Termination families exploiting finite or effectively enumerable master decisions.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite Convergence on Discrete Master Domains
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite termination through exact evaluation of previously unresolved master points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D\) be a finite nonempty master domain, let \(c:D\to\mathbb R\), and let \(Q:D\to\mathbb R\) be finite. At iteration \(k\), suppose a decomposition method retains a lower approximation \(\underline Q_k:D\to\mathbb R\) satisfying \(\underline Q_k(x)\leq Q(x)\) for every \(x\in D\), and globally selects \[x^k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in D}\{c(x)+\underline Q_k(x)\}.\] If \(\underline Q_k(x^k)<Q(x^k)\), suppose it adds and retains a valid cut such that \(\underline Q_{k+1}(x^k)=Q(x^k)\); otherwise it terminates. Then the method terminates after at most \(|D|\) strict-improvement evaluations, and its terminating state minimizes \(c(x)+Q(x)\) over \(D\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a finite master domain, a retained exact point cut prevents the same state from producing a second strict improvement. Exact global master solution therefore gives termination after at most one improvement per state, and a zero incumbent gap certifies global optimality.
assumptions_latex: \(D\) is finite and nonempty, and \(c(x)\) and \(Q(x)\) are finite for every \(x\in D\).
Every master problem and incumbent value evaluation is solved exactly.
All retained approximations are valid lower bounds, and each strict evaluation makes the approximation exact at its generating state.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The method terminates at a global minimizer of \(c+Q\) after at most \(|D|\) strict-improvement evaluations.

children.title: Finite Convergence by Scenario-Hull Recovery
children.top_down_role: Termination through progressive recovery of scenario integer-hull information.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite Convergence by Scenario-Hull Recovery
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite termination when scenario integer hulls have finitely many discoverable facets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each scenario \(s\), let the bounded mixed-integer feasible set \(X_s\) have a polyhedral hull \(P_s=\operatorname{conv}(X_s)\) described by a finite facet set \(F_s\). Suppose an algorithm solves its current master exactly and, whenever its scenario point lies outside \(P_s\), adds a previously absent violated inequality from \(F_s\). If termination occurs only after all scenario points satisfy their hulls and the remaining nonanticipative convexified master is solved exactly, then the algorithm terminates after at most \(\sum_s|F_s|\) hull-separation additions and returns the optimum of the scenario-hull formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If every scenario integer hull has finitely many facets and separation always adds a new violated facet, progressive hull recovery terminates finitely at the convexified optimum.
assumptions_latex: Every \(P_s=\operatorname{conv}(X_s)\) is a polytope with finite facet family \(F_s\).
Hull separation is exact and never adds a duplicate inequality.
Each intermediate and final master is solved globally.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At most \(\sum_s|F_s|\) distinct hull cuts are added before exact scenario-hull recovery.

children.title: Finite Convergence of Branch-Decomposition Hybrids
children.top_down_role: Termination combining finite tree search with valid recourse separation.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite Convergence of Branch-Decomposition Hybrids
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite termination of exact branch search augmented by valid recourse cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a bounded rational stochastic mixed-integer program solved by branch-and-bound over its integer master variables. Suppose the branching rule yields a finite tree; every node relaxation is solved exactly; recourse cuts are globally valid lower-bounding inequalities; and separation at a node either certifies its recourse approximation or adds one of finitely many relevant cuts. If nodes are fathomed only by infeasibility, integrality with verified recourse, or a valid bound not better than the incumbent, then the hybrid algorithm terminates after finitely many node and cut-processing steps and returns a globally optimal feasible solution, or correctly certifies infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite exact branch tree remains finitely convergent when decomposition adds only valid cuts from finite families and fathoming uses certified bounds or feasibility.
assumptions_latex: Branching produces finitely many nodes and node relaxations are solved exactly.
Only globally valid recourse cuts are retained, with finitely many relevant cuts per node.
Incumbents are feasible and pruning uses valid lower bounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The branch-decomposition hybrid terminates finitely with a global optimum or an infeasibility certificate.

notation.meaning: objective value of the current feasible incumbent
valid lower bound at branch node \(N\)

children.title: Finite Convergence of Binary-State SDDiP
children.top_down_role: Termination theory for multistage decomposition over binary linking states.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite Convergence of Binary-State SDDiP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic finite termination with exact cuts over finite binary linking-state spaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a finite-horizon scenario tree whose linking state at every nonterminal node \(n\) belongs to \(D_n=\{0,1\}^{d_n}\). Suppose a deterministic SDDiP variant solves all forward and backward subproblems globally, retains valid lower approximations, and, whenever a visited state has a positive approximation gap, adds a cut exact at that node-state pair. If its state-selection rule eventually visits every unresolved pair, then only finitely many strict cut improvements are possible. Specifically, their number is at most \(\sum_n2^{d_n}\); afterward all reachable node-state values are exact and an optimal policy is recovered.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact point cuts over finitely many binary node-state pairs permit only finitely many strict improvements; exhaustive unresolved-state selection therefore recovers an optimal policy.
assumptions_latex: The horizon and scenario tree are finite, with \(D_n=\{0,1\}^{d_n}\).
All subproblems are solved globally and every generated cut is valid and exact at its generating state.
Every unresolved reachable node-state pair is eventually selected.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At most \(\sum_n2^{d_n}\) strict pointwise improvements occur before optimal-policy recovery.

notation.meaning: number of binary state components at node \(n\)

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The explicit bound on strict improvements and the claim of optimal-policy recovery concern a specialized deterministic binary-state SDDiP variant. The cited finite-state and dynamic-programming sections do not establish these algorithmic hypotheses, and the meaning of reachable pairs under the selection rule affects the conclusion. A direct SDDiP convergence source is needed.

children.title: SMIP Dual-Information Bound Hierarchy
children.top_down_role: Lower bounds arising from continuous relaxation, scenario convexification, and information relaxation.

children.title: Continuous-Relaxation Bounds
children.top_down_role: Bounds from extensive-form and recourse relaxations.

knowledge_statements.title: Continuous-Relaxation Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lower bounds obtained by dropping integrality in a minimization-form extensive formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(z_{\mathrm{SMIP}}=\inf\{c^\top x:x\in X\}\), where \(X\) is the nonanticipative feasible set of a minimization stochastic mixed-integer program. Let \(X^{\mathrm{LP}}\) be obtained by replacing every integrality restriction by membership in its continuous relaxation while retaining all other constraints. Since \(X\subseteq X^{\mathrm{LP}}\), the relaxation value
\[z_{\mathrm{LP}}=\inf\{c^\top x:x\in X^{\mathrm{LP}}\}\]
satisfies \(z_{\mathrm{LP}}\leq z_{\mathrm{SMIP}}\). Equality holds precisely when the relaxation admits an optimal solution feasible for \(X\), assuming both optima are attained.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dropping integrality enlarges the feasible set, so the continuous extensive-form or recourse relaxation gives a lower bound for a minimization SMIP.
assumptions_latex: The stochastic mixed-integer model is written as a minimization problem.
The continuous relaxation retains nonanticipativity and all non-integrality constraints.
The compared optimal values are well-defined in the extended real sense.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(z_{\mathrm{LP}}\leq z_{\mathrm{SMIP}}\).

notation.meaning: continuous relaxation of the feasible set

children.title: Nonanticipativity Lagrangian Bounds
children.top_down_role: Scenario-separable bounds from relaxed agreement.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonanticipativity Lagrangian Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scenario-separable lower bound obtained by dualizing cross-scenario agreement constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\) be a finite scenario set, let \(p_s\geq0\) with \(\sum_{s\in S}p_s=1\), let \(X_s\subseteq\mathbb R^{n_s}\), let \(c_s\in\mathbb R^{n_s}\), and let \(A_s:\mathbb R^{n_s}\to\mathbb R^m\) be linear. Consider the minimization problem \[z^*=\inf\left\{\sum_{s\in S}p_sc_s^\top x_s:x_s\in X_s\ \text{for all }s,\ \sum_{s\in S}A_sx_s=0\right\},\] where the equality encodes nonanticipativity. For \(\lambda\in\mathbb R^m\), define \[L(\lambda)=\sum_{s\in S}\inf_{x_s\in X_s}\left(p_sc_s^\top x_s+\lambda^\top A_sx_s\right).\] Then \(L(\lambda)\leq z^*\) for every \(\lambda\in\mathbb R^m\), so \[z_{\mathrm{NA}}^{\mathrm{LD}}=\sup_{\lambda\in\mathbb R^m}L(\lambda)\leq z^*.\] The final inequality can be strict when the scenario sets are nonconvex.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dualizing linear nonanticipativity equations separates the finite scenario-copy problem and gives a Lagrangian lower bound. Nonconvex mixed-integer scenario sets can produce a positive duality gap.
assumptions_latex: \(S\) is finite, \(p_s\geq0\), and \(\sum_{s\in S}p_s=1\).
The scenario-copy formulation represents the original minimization problem.
The extended-real scenario infima defining \(L(\lambda)\) are well-defined.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L(\lambda)\leq z_{\mathrm{NA}}^{\mathrm{LD}}\leq z^*\) for every \(\lambda\in\mathbb R^m\).

notation.meaning: scenario-specific feasible set in Euclidean space
linear scenario block of the nonanticipativity operator

children.title: Scenario Convex-Hull Bounds
children.top_down_role: Bounds based on convexification of scenario feasible sets.

knowledge_statements.title: Scenario Convex-Hull Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bound hierarchy from convexifying each scenario feasible set before enforcing nonanticipativity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\) be a finite scenario set, let \(p_s\geq0\), let \(X_s\subseteq\mathbb R^{n_s}\), let \(c_s\in\mathbb R^{n_s}\), and let \(A_s:\mathbb R^{n_s}\to\mathbb R^m\) be linear. Define \[z^*=\inf\left\{\sum_{s\in S}p_sc_s^\top x_s:x_s\in X_s\ \text{for all }s,\ \sum_{s\in S}A_sx_s=0\right\}.\] Replacing each scenario set by its convex hull gives \[z_{\mathrm{CH}}=\inf\left\{\sum_{s\in S}p_sc_s^\top x_s:x_s\in\operatorname{conv}(X_s)\ \text{for all }s,\ \sum_{s\in S}A_sx_s=0\right\}\leq z^*.\] If \(R_s\subseteq\mathbb R^{n_s}\) satisfies \(\operatorname{conv}(X_s)\subseteq R_s\) for every \(s\in S\), and \(z_{\mathrm{LP}}\) is the corresponding relaxation value obtained using the sets \(R_s\), then \[z_{\mathrm{LP}}\leq z_{\mathrm{CH}}\leq z^*.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convexifying each scenario mixed-integer feasible set gives a valid minimization lower bound, and that bound is at least as strong as any scenario relaxation containing the corresponding convex hulls.
assumptions_latex: \(S\) is finite and the model has linear scenario costs and linear nonanticipativity equations.
Every \(X_s\) is nonempty and all displayed infima are well-defined as extended-real values.
\(\operatorname{conv}(X_s)\subseteq R_s\) for every \(s\in S\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(z_{\mathrm{LP}}\leq z_{\mathrm{CH}}\leq z^*\).

notation.meaning: scenario continuous relaxation containing the convex hull

children.title: Information-Relaxation Bound Hierarchies
children.top_down_role: Hierarchies formed by relaxing selected nonanticipativity or filtration structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Information-Relaxation Bound Hierarchies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Monotonic lower-bound hierarchy for finite-horizon minimization under progressively enlarged information filtrations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal F=(\mathcal F_t)_{t=0}^T\) be the original filtration and let \(\mathcal F_t\subseteq\mathcal G_t^1\subseteq\cdots\subseteq\mathcal G_t^m\) for every \(t\). Denote by \(\Pi(\mathcal H)\) the feasible policies adapted to filtration \(\mathcal H\), and set \(v_k=\inf_{\pi\in\Pi(\mathcal G^k)}\mathbb E[C(\pi,\xi)]\), with \(v_0\) defined using \(\mathcal F\). Because \(\Pi(\mathcal F)\subseteq\Pi(\mathcal G^1)\subseteq\cdots\subseteq\Pi(\mathcal G^m)\), one has \[v_m\leq\cdots\leq v_1\leq v_0.\] Thus every information relaxation supplies a lower bound, and relaxing more nonanticipativity constraints cannot strengthen that unpenalized bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Enlarging the information available to minimization policies expands their feasible set, producing a monotone sequence of lower bounds on the original nonanticipative optimum.
assumptions_latex: \(C(\pi,\xi)\) is measurable and has a well-defined expectation for every feasible policy.
All policy classes \(\Pi(\mathcal G^k)\) are nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v_m\leq\cdots\leq v_1\leq v_0\).

notation.meaning: Optimal value under the kth information relaxation

children.title: Duality-Gap Regimes
children.top_down_role: Structural regimes governing exact or inexact scenario-dual bounds.

knowledge_statements.title: Duality-Gap Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonanticipativity Lagrangian duality for finite-scenario mixed-integer formulations and their convexification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For compact scenario sets \(X_s\), probabilities \(p_s>0\), costs \(c_s\), and linear nonanticipativity equations \(Ax=0\), consider \(z^*=\min\{\sum_s p_sc_s^{\mathsf T}x_s:x_s\in X_s,\ Ax=0\}\). Its nonanticipativity Lagrangian value is \[z_D=\sup_{\lambda}\inf_{x_s\in X_s}\left\{\sum_s p_sc_s^{\mathsf T}x_s+\lambda^{\mathsf T}Ax\right\}.\] If the corresponding convexified problem satisfies a relative-interior constraint qualification, then \(z_D\) equals its optimum \(z_{\mathrm{conv}}\), obtained by replacing each \(X_s\) by \(\operatorname{clconv}(X_s)\). Hence \(z_D=z_{\mathrm{conv}}\leq z^*\), and the scenario-dual gap is zero exactly when \(z_{mathrm{conv}}=z^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The nonanticipativity dual solves the scenario-wise convexification. Its gap vanishes precisely when convexifying the mixed-integer scenario sets does not improve the primal optimum.
assumptions_latex: Each \(X_s\) is nonempty and compact.
The convexified formulation satisfies the stated relative-interior constraint qualification.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(z_D=z_{\mathrm{conv}}\leq z^*\), with zero gap if and only if \(z_{\mathrm{conv}}=z^*\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The stated convexification identity is plausible under an appropriate Lagrangian-duality constraint qualification, but the cited general duality section has not been shown to support this exact mixed-integer scenario-wise convexification theorem and its hypotheses.

children.title: Optimality Certificate Families
children.top_down_role: Evidence supporting deterministic or statistically assessed solution quality.

children.title: Deterministic Bound Certificates
children.top_down_role: Global lower and upper bounds from exact SMIP algorithms.

knowledge_statements.title: Deterministic Bound Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global primal-dual bound certificate for an exact minimization algorithm.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(z^*=\min\{F(x):x\in X\}\). A deterministic bound certificate consists of a feasible incumbent \(\hat x\in X\), its finite value \(U=F(\hat x)\), and a globally valid lower bound \(L\) satisfying \(L\leq F(x)\) for every \(x\in X\). These data verify \[L\leq z^*\leq U.\] For an absolute tolerance \(\varepsilon\geq0\), the certificate establishes \(F(\hat x)-z^*\leq\varepsilon\) whenever \(U-L\leq\varepsilon\). For a relative tolerance \(\rho\geq0\), it establishes \(F(\hat x)-z^*\leq\rho\max\{1,|U|\}\) whenever \(U-L\leq\rho\max\{1,|U|\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible incumbent supplies an upper bound and a globally valid lower bound supplies a lower bound; their difference certifies deterministic absolute or explicitly scaled relative optimality.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is nonempty and the minimization problem has a finite optimal value.
The incumbent \(\hat x\) is feasible and has finite objective value.
The lower bound \(L\) is valid for the entire feasible set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L\leq z^*\leq U\), and \(U-L\) bounds the incumbent's absolute optimality gap.

notation.meaning: Certified global lower and upper bounds

children.title: Scenario Recourse Certificates
children.top_down_role: Scenario-level feasibility, optimality, and hull evidence supporting master decisions.

knowledge_statements.title: Scenario Recourse Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scenario-wise lower models and feasible recourse witnesses for a two-stage finite-scenario SMIP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal S\) be a finite scenario set with probabilities \(p_s\geq0\) satisfying \(\sum_{s\in\mathcal S}p_s=1\). For \(s\in\mathcal S\), define \(Q_s(x)=\min\{q_s^{\mathsf T}y:W_sy\geq h_s-T_sx,\ y\in Y_s\}\), and define the two-stage optimum by \[z^*=\min_{x\in X}\left(c^{\mathsf T}x+\sum_{s\in\mathcal S}p_sQ_s(x)\right).\] If \(\ell_s(x)\leq Q_s(x)\) for every \(x\in X\) and \(s\in\mathcal S\), then \[L=\min_{x\in X}\left(c^{\mathsf T}x+\sum_{s\in\mathcal S}p_s\ell_s(x)\right)\leq z^*.\] If \(\hat x\in X\) and \(\hat y_s\in Y_s\) satisfy \(W_s\hat y_s\geq h_s-T_s\hat x\) for every \(s\in\mathcal S\), then \[U=c^{\mathsf T}\hat x+\sum_{s\in\mathcal S}p_sq_s^{\mathsf T}\hat y_s\geq z^*.\] Consequently, the scenario lower models and recourse-feasibility witnesses certify \(L\leq z^*\leq U\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a finite-scenario two-stage problem, globally valid scenario lower models certify a master lower bound, while feasible recourse witnesses for a chosen first-stage decision certify an upper bound.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal S\) is finite, \(p_s\geq0\), and \(\sum_{s\in\mathcal S}p_s=1\).
Each \(\ell_s\) is a globally valid lower model of \(Q_s\) on \(X\).
The displayed minima and certificate values are well defined and finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L\leq z^*\leq U\).

notation.meaning: Optimal recourse value in scenario s
Globally valid lower model of scenario recourse
Certified master lower and incumbent upper bounds
Optimal value of the two-stage stochastic program

children.title: Statistical Optimality Certificates
children.top_down_role: Sampling-based validation and optimality-gap assessment.

knowledge_statements.title: Statistical Optimality Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-sample confidence certificate combining independent upper and lower estimators.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U_1,\ldots,U_m\) and \(L_1,\ldots,L_n\) be independent i.i.d. samples with \(U_i\in[a_U,b_U]\), \(L_j\in[a_L,b_L]\), \(\mathbb E[U_i]=F(\hat x)\), and \(\mathbb E[L_j]\leq z^*\). For \(\alpha_U+\alpha_L=\alpha\), define \(r_U=(b_U-a_U)\sqrt{\log(1/\alpha_U)/(2m)}\) and \(r_L=(b_L-a_L)\sqrt{\log(1/\alpha_L)/(2n)}\). Hoeffding bounds and a union bound give, with probability at least \(1-\alpha\), \[F(\hat x)-z^*\leq (\bar U+r_U)-(\bar L-r_L).\] The displayed quantity is therefore a one-sided statistical optimality-gap certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Independent bounded estimators of candidate performance and a valid expected lower bound yield a finite-sample, one-sided confidence bound on the optimality gap.
assumptions_latex: The candidate \(\hat x\) is fixed independently of the validation samples.
The upper and lower samples obey the stated almost-sure bounds and expectation relations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Pr\{F(\hat x)-z^*\leq(\bar U+r_U)-(\bar L-r_L)\}\geq1-\alpha\).

notation.meaning: Sample means of upper and lower estimators

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The one-sided Hoeffding construction is mathematically plausible, but no source is supplied for the statistical optimality-gap certificate. A sourced version should also state that the split failure probabilities are strictly between zero and one.

children.title: SMIP Complexity Families
children.top_down_role: Complexity distinctions arising from integrality, stochastic representation, stage count, and recourse evaluation.

children.title: Deterministic-Equivalent Complexity
children.top_down_role: Difficulty induced by scenario-expanded mixed-integer formulations.

knowledge_statements.title: Deterministic-Equivalent Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Encoding growth and worst-case hardness of an explicitly enumerated finite-scenario deterministic equivalent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a scenario tree with node set \(\mathcal N\), a deterministic equivalent containing \(n_v\) variables and \(m_v\) local constraints at node \(v\) has \(\sum_{v\in\mathcal N}n_v\) node variables and \(\sum_{v\in\mathcal N}m_v\), plus nonanticipativity-linking constraints. Thus its explicit encoding size is linear in the enumerated tree size but may be exponential in the horizon when the tree branches. Exact solution is NP-hard even for one scenario, because the one-scenario subclass contains rational binary linear programming. Scenario expansion therefore increases instance size without removing the underlying mixed-integer worst-case hardness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A deterministic equivalent grows linearly with the explicit scenario tree, potentially exponentially with horizon, and remains NP-hard because one-scenario instances include binary linear programs.
assumptions_latex: The scenario tree and all rational coefficients are represented explicitly.
Node-model dimensions are counted before presolve or structural aggregation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The formulation size is \(O(\sum_{v\in\mathcal N}(n_v+m_v))\) plus linking constraints, while exact solution is NP-hard.

notation.meaning: Numbers of local variables and constraints at node v

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The encoding-growth and NP-hardness claims fit the complexity container, but the branch-and-bound locator does not demonstrably support the scenario-tree size analysis or NP-hardness reduction. The number of linking constraints also needs an explicit bound before the overall encoding claim is fully precise.

children.title: Integer Recourse Evaluation-Separation Complexity
children.top_down_role: Difficulty of evaluating or separating expected mixed-integer recourse.

children.title: Integer Recourse Evaluation Complexity
children.top_down_role: Computational difficulty of obtaining expected mixed-integer recourse values.

knowledge_statements.title: Integer Recourse Evaluation Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case complexity of evaluating a fixed first-stage decision with binary recourse.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given rational data and fixed \(x\), define \(Q(x)=\min\{q^{\mathsf T}y:Wy\geq h-Tx,\ y\in\{0,1\}^r\}\). The threshold question \(Q(x)\leq K\) belongs to NP because a binary vector \(y\) is a polynomially checkable witness. It is NP-hard by the special case \(T=0\), which is binary linear programming; hence the threshold problem is NP-complete and exact evaluation of \(Q(x)\) is NP-hard. This remains true for a single scenario, so neither expectation aggregation nor nonanticipativity is required for the hardness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Evaluating binary recourse at a fixed first-stage decision is NP-hard; its bounded rational threshold version is NP-complete by direct inclusion of binary linear programming.
assumptions_latex: All coefficients and the threshold \(K\) are rational and binary encoded.
Recourse variables are binary, so witnesses have polynomial encoding length.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Deciding whether \(Q(x)\leq K\) is NP-complete, and exactly computing \(Q(x)\) is NP-hard.

notation.meaning: Integer recourse value at fixed first-stage decision x

source_refs.locator: 3.5 Cutting Plane Method for the Solution of the All Integer Variable Linear Programming Problem p. 76

source_witnesses.locator: 3.5 Cutting Plane Method for the Solution of the All Integer Variable Linear Programming Problem p. 76

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The binary-recourse threshold argument is standard and fits the terminal container, but the cited cutting-plane section has not been shown to establish NP-completeness or the claimed reduction. An authoritative complexity locator is required.

children.title: Integer Recourse Separation Complexity
children.top_down_role: Computational difficulty of identifying violated recourse inequalities.

knowledge_statements.title: Integer Recourse Separation Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Hardness of exact separation over a rational integer-recourse convex hull.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P=\operatorname{conv}\{y\in\{0,1\}^r:Wy\geq h\}\). An exact strong separation oracle, given rational \(\bar y\), either confirms \(\bar y\in P\) or returns rational \((a,\beta)\) with \(a^{\mathsf T}y\geq\beta>a^{\mathsf T}\bar y\) for all \(y\in P\). For rational bounded polytopes, polynomial-time strong separation implies polynomial-time linear optimization through the separation-to-optimization oracle reduction. Since choosing \(W,h\\) can make linear optimization over \(P\) an arbitrary binary linear program, exact separation over this family is NP-hard unless \(\mathrm P=\mathrm{NP}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact separation over general binary recourse hulls is NP-hard because a polynomial separation oracle would yield polynomial optimization for arbitrary binary linear programs.
assumptions_latex: The hull is nonempty, bounded, rational, and supplied through its integer description.
Oracle running time includes the binary encoding length of returned inequalities.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: General exact strong separation over \(P\) is NP-hard unless \(\mathrm P=\mathrm{NP}\).

notation.meaning: Convex hull of feasible binary recourse vectors

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The optimization-to-separation argument requires a precise oracle and bit-complexity theorem from an authoritative source. The statement also contains malformed LaTeX after \(W,h\), and the type of reduction underlying the NP-hardness claim must be specified.

children.title: Evaluation–Separation Reductions
children.top_down_role: Complexity relationships linking recourse evaluation to separation.

knowledge_statements.title: Evaluation–Separation Reductions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Oracle reductions for the convex closure of integer recourse, with the required subgradient information explicit.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f\) be a proper closed convex function on a bounded rational domain \(D\), with known rational value bounds. A value-subgradient oracle returning \(f(x)\) and \(g\in\partial f(x)\) separates \((x,\theta)\) from \(\operatorname{epi}f\): if \(\theta<f(x)\), the inequality \(\eta\geq f(x)+g^{\mathsf T}(u-x)\) is valid and violated. Conversely, an epigraph separation oracle permits weak evaluation of \(f(x)\) to accuracy \(\varepsilon\) by bisection in \(\theta\), using polynomially many oracle calls in the encoding length and \(\log(1/\varepsilon)\). For nonconvex integer recourse, this applies to its closed convex envelope, not automatically to the raw value function.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Value plus subgradient yields epigraph separation, while epigraph separation yields approximate evaluation by bisection. For integer recourse, the equivalence concerns the convex envelope.
assumptions_latex: The domain and epigraph portion queried are rationally bounded.
Weak oracle answers use a specified tolerance \(\varepsilon>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Weak evaluation with subgradients and weak epigraph separation are polynomially interreducible for \(f\); raw nonconvex evaluation alone is insufficient.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source supports the claimed bit-complexity reductions. Moreover, the stated converse derives approximate values from epigraph separation but does not derive subgradients, so it does not justify the conclusion that value-subgradient evaluation and separation are fully interreducible. The epigraph coordinates \(u\) and \(\eta\) also require introduction.

children.title: Multistage Information Complexity
children.top_down_role: Growth caused by adaptive discrete decisions and scenario-tree information.

knowledge_statements.title: Multistage Information Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case scenario-tree growth induced by stagewise branching and adaptive node decisions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a \(T\)-stage scenario tree in which every nonterminal node has at most \(b\) children, and let \(\mathcal N\) be its node set. Then, for \(b>1\), \[|\mathcal N|\leq1+b+\cdots+b^{T-1}=\frac{b^T-1}{b-1}.\] If a node-based deterministic equivalent has at most \(d\) adaptive decision variables per node, it has at most \(d(b^T-1)/(b-1)\) such variables before auxiliary variables and constraints. A full \(b\)-ary tree attains the displayed node count, so for fixed \(b>1\) the worst-case representation size is exponential in \(T\), although it is linear in the size of an explicitly supplied tree. Discrete adaptive decisions can additionally retain mixed-integer worst-case hardness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A branching cap gives an exponential worst-case upper bound on multistage tree size. A full fixed-branching tree attains that growth, while a node-based formulation remains linear in an explicitly supplied tree.
assumptions_latex: \(T\geq1\) and \(b>1\) are integers.
Every nonterminal node has at most \(b\) children.
Each information node carries at most \(d\) adaptive decision variables.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(|\mathcal N|=O(b^T)\) and the adaptive node-decision count is \(O(db^T)\); both bounds are attained up to constants by full \(b\)-ary trees.

notation.meaning: Number of stages and maximum branching factor
Maximum adaptive decision dimension per node

children.title: Structural Solvability Classes
children.top_down_role: Restricted recourse, matrix, distributional, or state structures with improved solvability.

children.title: Tractable Structural Subclasses
children.top_down_role: Restricted SMIP structures admitting improved exact solvability.

knowledge_statements.title: Tractable Structural Subclasses
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Polynomially solvable finite-scenario subclass obtained from an integral deterministic-equivalent polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the finite-scenario deterministic equivalent be \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}z:Az\geq b,\ z\geq0,\ z_i\in\mathbb Z\text{ for }i\in I\}\), with rational \(c\), integral \(b\), and totally unimodular \(A\). If the relaxation polyhedron is nonempty and bounded, every vertex is integral in all coordinates. Consequently, the integer restrictions are redundant, and solving the linear programming relaxation returns an optimal mixed-integer solution in time polynomial in the binary encoding length under the standard rational linear-programming model. This defines a tractable structural subclass despite scenario expansion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite-scenario deterministic equivalent with totally unimodular constraints and integral right-hand side is integral, so linear programming solves the mixed-integer model polynomially.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) is totally unimodular and \(b\) is integral.
The rational relaxation is nonempty and bounded.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The LP relaxation has an integral optimum and solves the stated SMIP deterministic equivalent in polynomial time.

notation.meaning: Deterministic-equivalent constraint matrix, right-hand side, and objective

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The total-unimodularity condition defines an appropriate tractable subclass and the mathematical claim is standard, but no source is supplied for the integrality theorem and polynomial-time linear-programming conclusion.

children.title: Approximable Structural Subclasses
children.top_down_role: Restricted SMIP structures supporting controlled approximation quality.

knowledge_statements.title: Approximable Structural Subclasses
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform-sampling additive approximation for a finite policy class with bounded costs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Pi\) be a finite feasible policy class with \(|\Pi|=N\), and suppose \(C(\pi,\xi)\in[0,1]\) almost surely. From \(m\) independent scenarios, define \(\widehat F_m(\pi)=m^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^m C(\pi,\xi_i)\) and choose \(\hat\pi\in\arg\min_{pi\in\Pi}\widehat F_m(\pi)\). If \[m\geq\frac{2}{\varepsilon^2}\log\left(\frac{2N}{\delta}\right),\] then a union of Hoeffding bounds implies \[\Pr\left\{F(\hat\pi)\leq\min_{\pi\in\Pi}F(\pi)+\varepsilon\right\}\geq1-\delta.\] Thus this subclass admits an additive randomized approximation using a number of samples polynomial in \(\varepsilon^{-1}\), \(\log N\), and \(\log(\delta^{-1})\), assuming empirical optimization is tractable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For finitely many policies with bounded costs, empirical optimization achieves additive accuracy with high probability using polynomially many samples, provided the empirical problem is tractable.
assumptions_latex: Scenario samples are independent and identically distributed.
Policy costs lie in \([0,1]\), and empirical minimization over \(\Pi\) is exact.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For the stated \(m\), \(F(\hat\pi)\leq\min_{pi\in\Pi}F(\pi)+\varepsilon\) with probability at least \(1-\delta\).

notation.meaning: Finite policy class and its cardinality

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite-class Hoeffding sample bound is plausible, but no source is supplied. The statement and conclusion also use literal \(pi\) instead of \(\pi\) in two optimization domains, and \(F(\pi)=\mathbb E[C(\pi,\xi)]\) is not explicitly defined.

children.title: Recourse-Based Solvability Regimes
children.top_down_role: Improved solvability arising from specialized recourse structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Recourse-Based Solvability Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classifies two-stage SMIPs by the domain over which their second-stage integer recourse problems are feasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D\) be the ambient first-stage decision domain, let \(X\subseteq D\) be the set satisfying the deterministic first-stage constraints, let \(P\) be the uncertainty law with support \(\Xi\), and let \(Y(x,\xi)\) be the feasible second-stage set. Complete recourse means \(Y(x,\xi)\neq\varnothing\) for every \((x,\xi)\in D\times\Xi\). Relatively complete recourse means \(Y(x,\xi)\neq\varnothing\) for every \(x\in X\) and for \(P\)-almost every \(\xi\). Recourse is incomplete when relatively complete recourse fails. A finite expected recourse objective additionally requires the recourse value to be measurable and integrable at the decisions under consideration.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Complete recourse requires feasibility throughout the ambient first-stage and uncertainty domains, whereas relatively complete recourse requires almost-sure feasibility only for deterministically feasible first-stage decisions. Incomplete recourse means the latter condition fails.
assumptions_latex: \(D\neq\varnothing\), \(X\neq\varnothing\), and \(X\subseteq D\).
\(P\) is a probability law with support \(\Xi\).
The recourse value may initially be extended-real-valued.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\text{complete recourse}\Rightarrow\text{relatively complete recourse}\).

notation.meaning: Feasible set of second-stage integer or mixed-integer decisions.

source_refs.locator: 1.7.1 The Feasible Set and Solvability p. 54

source_witnesses.locator: 1.7.1 The Feasible Set and Solvability p. 54

children.title: Distribution-Based Solvability Regimes
children.top_down_role: Improved solvability arising from restricted uncertainty distributions.

knowledge_statements.title: Distribution-Based Solvability Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classifies SMIP solvability by the available representation and regularity of the uncertainty law.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F(x)=\mathbb E_P[f(x,\xi)]\). The finite-support regime has \(P=\sum_{s=1}^S p_s\delta_{\xi_s}\), so \(F(x)=\sum_{s=1}^S p_s f(x,\xi_s)\). The evaluable-density regime permits deterministic integration or quadrature under a known law \(P\). The sampling-oracle regime supplies independent observations from \(P\) but not exact expectations. In each regime the stochastic program is well posed only when \(f(x,\cdot)\) is measurable, its negative part is integrable, and the infimum over admissible \(x\) is not \(-\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Distributional regimes separate finite scenario laws, evaluable laws, and sampling-only laws; every regime still requires measurable, integrable objectives and a finite lower value.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a nonempty admissible decision set.
\(P\) is a probability law on the uncertainty space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The representation of \(P\) determines whether exact scenario summation, numerical integration, or sampling approximation is available.

notation.meaning: Dirac probability measure at scenario s.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The formulas are plausible, but the three-way regime classification and associated well-posedness conditions have no inspectable citation and are not a uniquely standard taxonomy.

children.title: SMIP Sampling-Approximation Calculus
children.top_down_role: Discrete-specific sampling theory, uncertainty approximation, recourse convexification, and validation.

children.title: Sample Average Approximation for Stochastic Discrete Optimization
children.top_down_role: Sampling regimes specialized to finite or mixed discrete decision domains.

children.title: Finite-Decision-Set SAA
children.top_down_role: Sampling theory exploiting a finite set of candidate decisions.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Decision-Set SAA
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-set uniform concentration guarantee for bounded stochastic objective observations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be finite with \(|X|=M\), let \(F(x)=\mathbb E[f(x,\xi)]\), and let \(\widehat F_N(x)=N^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^N f(x,\xi_i)\) for independent samples. Suppose \(f(x,\xi)\in[a,b]\) almost surely for every \(x\in X\), and choose \(\widehat x_N\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}\widehat F_N(x)\). Then, for every \(\varepsilon>0\), \[\mathbb P\!\left(F(\widehat x_N)>\min_{x\in X}F(x)+2\varepsilon\right)\le 2M\exp\!\left(-\frac{2N\varepsilon^2}{(b-a)^2}\right).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For finitely many bounded candidate decisions, an SAA optimizer is within twice the uniform estimation tolerance with exponentially increasing reliability.
assumptions_latex: The observations \(\xi_1,\ldots,\xi_N\) are independent and identically distributed.
A common almost-sure range \([a,b]\) applies to every candidate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb P(F(\widehat x_N)>F^*+2\varepsilon)\le 2M\exp(-2N\varepsilon^2/(b-a)^2)\).

notation.meaning: Minimum true expected objective over the finite set.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite-set Hoeffding and union-bound statement is mathematically coherent and the theorem kind fits, but no source with a specific locator supports the exact constant and formulation.

children.title: Mixed Continuous–Discrete SAA
children.top_down_role: Sampling behavior when discrete choices coexist with continuous master variables.

knowledge_statements.title: Mixed Continuous–Discrete SAA
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consistency of SAA on a compact mixed continuous–integer decision set under uniform convergence and minimizer attainment.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^p\times\mathbb Z^q\) be nonempty and compact, define \(F(x)=\mathbb E[f(x,\xi)]\), and let \(\widehat F_N\) be the sample-average objective formed from independent identically distributed observations. Assume \(F\) is finite and lower semicontinuous on \(X\), each \(\widehat F_N\) attains its minimum on \(X\), and \(\sup_{x\in X}|\widehat F_N(x)-F(x)|\to0\) almost surely. With \(S=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}F(x)\) and \(S_N=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}\widehat F_N(x)\), one has \(\min_{x\in X}\widehat F_N(x)\to\min_{x\in X}F(x)\) and \(\sup_{x\in S_N}\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\to0\) almost surely.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform almost-sure convergence on a compact mixed decision set, together with attainment of the sample minima, yields convergence of SAA optimal values and convergence of all SAA minimizers toward the true solution set.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^p\times\mathbb Z^q\) is nonempty and compact.
\(F\) is finite and lower semicontinuous on \(X\).
Every \(\widehat F_N\) attains its minimum on \(X\).
\(\sup_{x\in X}|\widehat F_N(x)-F(x)|\to0\) almost surely.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min_X\widehat F_N\to\min_XF\) and \(\sup_{x\in S_N}\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\to0\) almost surely.

notation.meaning: Distance from x to the true solution set.

children.title: Finite-Sample Rate-Size Guarantee Family
children.top_down_role: Rate and sample-size result families for sampled stochastic discrete models.

children.title: Exponential-Rate Families
children.top_down_role: Exponential probability-rate results for sampled stochastic discrete models.

knowledge_statements.title: Exponential-Rate Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exponential probability bound for incorrect finite-set SAA selection under a positive objective gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) contain \(M\) decisions, let \(f(x,\xi)\in[a,b]\) almost surely, and define the strict optimality gap \(\Delta=\min_{x\notin S}(F(x)-F^*)>0\), where \(S=\operatorname*{argmin}_X F\). For any SAA minimizer \(\widehat x_N\), Hoeffding concentration and a union bound give \[\mathbb P(\widehat x_N\notin S)\le 2M\exp\!\left(-\frac{N\Delta^2}{2(b-a)^2}\right).\] Thus the probability of selecting a truly suboptimal decision decreases exponentially with sample size.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With bounded observations and a positive true objective gap, the probability that SAA selects a suboptimal finite-set decision decays exponentially.
assumptions_latex: The sample is independent and identically distributed.
\(X\) is finite and the strict gap \(\Delta\) is positive.
All observations share the almost-sure range \([a,b]\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb P(\widehat x_N\notin S)\le 2M\exp(-N\Delta^2/(2(b-a)^2))\).

notation.meaning: Smallest objective gap between an optimal and a suboptimal decision.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The exponential bound and its constants follow coherently from a uniform Hoeffding bound at tolerance Δ/2, and complexity_bound fits the leaf, but no citation supports the exact statement.

children.title: Sample-Size Families
children.top_down_role: Sample requirements associated with prescribed statistical reliability.

knowledge_statements.title: Sample-Size Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sample complexity for bounded finite-decision SAA with prescribed objective accuracy and confidence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the finite-decision assumptions with \(|X|=M\) and \(f(x,\xi)\in[a,b]\) almost surely, fix accuracy \(\epsilon>0\) and failure probability \(\delta\in(0,1)\). If \[N\ge \frac{2(b-a)^2}{\epsilon^2}\log\!\left(\frac{2M}{\delta}\right),\] then every SAA minimizer \(\widehat x_N\) satisfies \(F(\widehat x_N)\le F^*+\epsilon\) with probability at least \(1-\delta\). The resource counted is the number of independent sampled scenarios; objective evaluations total \(NM\) under exhaustive finite-set evaluation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A logarithmic dependence on the number of decisions and confidence, and quadratic dependence on inverse accuracy, suffices for bounded finite-set SAA.
assumptions_latex: Samples are independent and identically distributed.
The decision set has cardinality \(M<\infty\).
The stochastic objective has common range width \(b-a\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N\ge 2(b-a)^2\epsilon^{-2}\log(2M/\delta)\Rightarrow\mathbb P(F(\widehat x_N)\le F^*+\epsilon)\ge1-\delta\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The sample-size expression is consistent with the preceding finite-set bound after using uniform tolerance ε/2, but its exact constants and evaluation-count claim lack an inspectable source.

children.title: Finite-Sample Reliability Regimes
children.top_down_role: Reliability behavior across discrete decision spaces plus sampling distributions.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Sample Reliability Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A uniform-deviation event yields a theoretical finite-sample SAA reliability certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be a decision set, let \(F\) and \(\widehat F_N\) be true and sample-average objectives that attain their minima on \(X\), and let \(r_N\ge0\). Define \(F^*=\min_{x\in X}F(x)\), choose \(\widehat x_N\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}\widehat F_N(x)\), and define \(E_N=\{\sup_{x\in X}|\widehat F_N(x)-F(x)|\le r_N\}\). On \(E_N\), one has \(F(\widehat x_N)-F^*\le2r_N\) and \(|\min_{x\in X}\widehat F_N(x)-F^*|\le r_N\). Thus any valid bound \(\mathbb P(E_N)\ge1-\delta\) gives a \((2r_N,1-\delta)\) reliability guarantee. Because \(E_N\) involves \(F\), it is directly observable only when a computable valid bound for its deviation is available.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A uniform true-versus-sample objective bound implies sample-value accuracy and twice that radius as true suboptimality. The event is a theoretical certificate unless its radius can be bounded from observable information.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) and \(\widehat F_N\) attain their minima on \(X\).
A valid lower bound on \(\mathbb P(E_N)\) is available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(E_N\Rightarrow F(\widehat x_N)-F^*\le2r_N\) and \(|\min_X\widehat F_N-F^*|\le r_N\).

notation.meaning: Minimum true objective value over X.

children.title: Uncertainty Approximation for Integer Recourse
children.top_down_role: Discrete probability approximations accounting for discontinuity and lattice sensitivity.

children.title: Distribution Discretization for Integer Recourse
children.top_down_role: Finite distributions constructed for discontinuous recourse functions.

knowledge_statements.title: Distribution Discretization for Integer Recourse
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient convergence conditions for discrete approximations of a possibly discontinuous integer-recourse expectation at a fixed decision.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a decision \(x\). Let \(P_m=\sum_{j=1}^{k_m}p_{mj}\delta_{\xi_{mj}}\) converge weakly to a probability law \(P\), and let \(Q(x,\xi)\) be a measurable integer-recourse value. If the discontinuity set \(D_x\) of \(Q(x,\cdot)\) satisfies \(P(D_x)=0\) and \(\lim_{K\to\infty}\sup_m\int |Q(x,\xi)|\mathbf 1_{\{|Q(x,\xi)|>K\}}\,P_m(d\xi)=0\), then \[\sum_{j=1}^{k_m}p_{mj}Q(x,\xi_{mj})\longrightarrow\int Q(x,\xi)\,P(d\xi).\] Weak convergence alone need not imply convergence of these expectations when recourse discontinuities carry positive limiting probability or the tail condition fails.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a fixed decision, discrete laws approximate the integer-recourse expectation when the recourse value is almost surely continuous under the limiting law and its tails are uniformly integrable under the approximating laws.
assumptions_latex: \(P_m\Rightarrow P\).
\(Q(x,\cdot)\) is measurable and \(P(D_x)=0\).
\(\lim_{K\to\infty}\sup_m\int |Q(x,\xi)|\mathbf 1_{\{|Q(x,\xi)|>K\}}\,P_m(d\xi)=0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E_{P_m}[Q(x,\xi)]\to\mathbb E_P[Q(x,\xi)]\).

notation.meaning: Finite discrete approximation of the uncertainty law.
Integer-recourse value at the fixed decision and realization.
Discontinuity set of the recourse function in uncertainty at x.

children.title: Scenario Reduction for SMIP
children.top_down_role: Scenario compression accounting for discrete solution instability.

knowledge_statements.title: Scenario Reduction for SMIP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Greedy forward scenario reduction with probability reassignment and a conditional decision-value error bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given scenarios \((\xi_s,p_s)_{s=1}^S\), a target \(K\in\{1,\ldots,S\}\), and a metric \(d\), set \(J=\varnothing\). For every nonempty candidate set \(A\subseteq\{1,\ldots,S\}\), define \(C(A)=\sum_{s=1}^S p_s\min_{j\in A}d(\xi_s,\xi_j)\). While \(|J|<K\), choose \(j^*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{j\notin J}C(J\cup\{j\})\) and replace \(J\) by \(J\cup\{j^*\}\). Assign every scenario \(s\) to a nearest retained index \(j(s)\in J\), set \(\widetilde p_j=\sum_{s:j(s)=j}p_s\), and output \(\widetilde P=\sum_{j\in J}\widetilde p_j\delta_{\xi_j}\). If \(|Q(x,\xi)-Q(x,\xi')|\le Ld(\xi,\xi')\) for every relevant \(x,\xi,\xi'\), then \(|\mathbb E_P[Q(x,\xi)]-\mathbb E_{\widetilde P}[Q(x,\xi)]|\le L\sum_{s=1}^S p_s d(\xi_s,\xi_{j(s)})\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Greedily add the scenario producing the smallest assignment cost, transfer removed probability to nearest retained scenarios, and invoke the transport-cost error bound only when recourse is uniformly Lipschitz.
assumptions_latex: \(P=\sum_{s=1}^S p_s\delta_{\xi_s}\) has finite support.
\(1\le K\le S\), and nearest retained scenarios exist under \(d\).
The uniform Lipschitz condition is required only for the stated objective-error guarantee.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output has exactly \(K\) retained scenarios and satisfies the stated transport-cost error bound under uniform Lipschitz recourse.

notation.meaning: Weighted assignment cost for candidate retained set A.
Nearest retained representative of scenario s.

children.title: Scenario-Tree Approximation for Multistage SMIP
children.top_down_role: Tree approximation preserving decision-relevant multistage information.

knowledge_statements.title: Scenario-Tree Approximation for Multistage SMIP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-tree representation of adapted mixed-integer policies and their expected multistage cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A depth-\(T\) scenario tree has node sets \(\mathcal N_t\), root \(r\), parent map \(a(n)\), conditional arc probabilities, and node probabilities \(p_n\). Associate a mixed-integer decision \(x_n\) with each node and impose the stage constraints using only data along the root-to-\(n\) history. The approximation is \[\min_{(x_n)}\sum_{t=1}^T\sum_{n\in\mathcal N_t}p_nc_n^{\mathsf T}x_n,\] subject to nodewise constraints and integrality. Decisions sharing the same observed history use the same node variable, which enforces nonanticipativity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite scenario tree represents each information history by a node, weights node costs by path probabilities, and enforces adaptation through shared history-indexed decisions.
assumptions_latex: The tree is finite and its outgoing conditional probabilities sum to one.
Every node records exactly the information available when its decision is made.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The deterministic equivalent represents a nonanticipative mixed-integer policy on the approximating tree.

children.title: Convex Approximations of Integer Recourse
children.top_down_role: Tractable convex surrogates for nonconvex expected integer recourse.

children.title: Simple Integer Recourse Convexification
children.top_down_role: Convex approximation families specialized to separable integer recourse.

knowledge_statements.title: Simple Integer Recourse Convexification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Continuous positive-part relaxation of scalar separable simple integer recourse with an explicit additive error bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For residual \(u\in\mathbb R\) and costs \(q^+,q^-\ge0\), scalar simple integer recourse has value \[Q(u)=q^+\lceil u_+\rceil+q^-\lceil(-u)_+\rceil,\qquad u_+=\max\{u,0\}.\] Its continuous-recourse convexification is \(\widetilde Q(u)=q^+u_++q^-(-u)_+\). It is convex and satisfies \(0\le Q(u)-\widetilde Q(u)<q^++q^-\). For separable residuals, summing these functions gives a convex approximation whose pointwise and expected errors are bounded by the sum of the component cost bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Replacing integer ceiling terms by positive parts gives a convex separable recourse approximation with a direct additive error bound.
assumptions_latex: Shortage and surplus recourse variables are nonnegative integers.
The recourse costs \(q^+\) and \(q^-\) are nonnegative.
The multidimensional extension is separable by residual component.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widetilde Q\) is convex and \(0\le Q-\widetilde Q<q^++q^-\) componentwise.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The ceiling-based formula and continuous positive-part approximation are plausible under an inequality-based simple-integer-recourse convention, but the exact recourse constraints and sign convention are not stated or cited. A source is needed before the formula can be trusted in this container.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact simple-recourse convexification under S=1
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A global underestimation and convex-hull result for a rooted rho-approximation under the source's S=1 condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let $\xi$ be a random variable with $S=1$, and let $\rho$ be a $\rho$-approximation of $\Psi$ rooted at a point in the support of $\xi$. Then
\[
\rho(x)\le \Psi(x)\qquad\forall x\in\mathbb R.
\]
Moreover, $\rho$ is the convex hull of $\Psi$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Let ξ be a random variable satisfying S=1. If ρ is a ρ-approximation of Ψ rooted at a support point of ξ, then ρ(x)≤Ψ(x) for every real x, and ρ is the convex hull of Ψ.
assumptions_latex: \xi\text{ is a random variable}
\rho\text{ is a $\rho$-approximation of }\Psi
\rho\text{ is rooted at a point in }\operatorname{supp}(\xi)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \rho(x)\le\Psi(x)\ \forall x\in\mathbb R\quad\text{and}\quad \rho=\operatorname{conv}(\Psi)

source_evidence.locator: Stochastic Integer Programs / 7.5. Simple Integer Recourse / Corollary 16

source_refs.locator: Stochastic Integer Programs / 7.5. Simple Integer Recourse / Corollary 16

knowledge_statements.title: Exact simple-recourse convexification under S=1

source_witnesses.locator: Stochastic Integer Programs / 7.5. Simple Integer Recourse / Corollary 16

children.title: Totally Unimodular Integer Recourse Approximations
children.top_down_role: Convex approximations exploiting totally unimodular recourse structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Totally Unimodular Integer Recourse Approximations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exactness boundary for the linear relaxation of integer recourse with a totally unimodular constraint matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(Q_{\mathrm{IP}}(r)=\min\{q^{\mathsf T}y:Wy=r,\ y\ge0,\ y\in\mathbb Z^m\}\) and its linear relaxation \(Q_{\mathrm{LP}}(r)\). If \(W\) is totally unimodular, \(r\) is integral, and the recourse polyhedron is nonempty with a finite optimum, then every extreme point of \(\{y\ge0:Wy=r\}\) is integral. Hence \(Q_{\mathrm{IP}}(r)=Q_{\mathrm{LP}}(r)\). For nonintegral random residuals this equality is not guaranteed, so an LP-based convex approximation requires an additional rounding, interpolation, or distributional error analysis.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Total unimodularity makes the LP recourse relaxation exact for integral residuals, but does not by itself cover nonintegral random right-hand sides.
assumptions_latex: \(W\) is totally unimodular.
\(r\) is integral.
The recourse problem is feasible and has a finite optimum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q_{\mathrm{IP}}(r)=Q_{\mathrm{LP}}(r)\) for integral \(r\); exactness may fail for nonintegral \(r\).

notation.meaning: Value of the continuous recourse relaxation.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The total-unimodularity exactness boundary for integral right-hand sides is standard and the property kind fits, but the candidate provides no citation with a specific locator.

children.title: Approximation Error Certificate Families
children.top_down_role: Guarantee families assessing convex integer-recourse approximations.

knowledge_statements.title: Approximation Error Certificate Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic pointwise and expectation-level certificates for a convex approximation of integer recourse.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q:X\times\Xi\to\mathbb R\) be an integer-recourse value function and \(\widetilde Q:X\times\Xi\to\mathbb R\) a finite convex approximation. Functions \(\ell,u:X\times\Xi\to[0,\infty)\) form a pointwise error-certificate family when \(-\ell(x,\xi)\le Q(x,\xi)-\widetilde Q(x,\xi)\le u(x,\xi)\) for every \((x,\xi)\). If the bounds are integrable, then \(-\mathbb E[\ell(x,\xi)]\le\mathbb E[Q(x,\xi)]-\mathbb E[\widetilde Q(x,\xi)]\le\mathbb E[u(x,\xi)]\). Consequently, \(\max\{\mathbb E[\ell(x,\xi)],\mathbb E[u(x,\xi)]\}\le\varepsilon\) certifies absolute expected-recourse error at most \(\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pointwise lower and upper error bounds induce expected-error bounds; their expected maximum certifies the approximation tolerance.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is the first-stage feasible set and \(Q,\widetilde Q\) are finite on \(X\times\Xi\).
\(\ell(x,\xi)\) and \(u(x,\xi)\) are measurable and integrable for each assessed \(x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\left|\mathbb E[Q(x,\xi)]-\mathbb E[\widetilde Q(x,\xi)]\right|\le\varepsilon\) whenever both expected one-sided certificates do not exceed \(\varepsilon\).

notation.meaning: Exact integer-recourse value and its convex approximation.
Nonnegative lower-side and upper-side error certificates.

review_flags: Exact certificate families for the intended recourse convexifications require a directly supporting source.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate is mathematically coherent and correctly typed, but no source supports its use as a certificate family for the intended convex integer-recourse approximations.

children.title: Sampled Solution Validation
children.top_down_role: Independent assessment of sampled SMIP solutions and discrete selection reliability.

children.title: Optimality-Gap Estimation for SMIP
children.top_down_role: Statistical assessment of candidate stochastic integer solutions.

knowledge_statements.title: Optimality-Gap Estimation for SMIP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-sided statistical certificate using independent replications of a candidate-value estimate and a stochastic lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(z^*=\inf_{x\in X}F(x)\) and fix a feasible candidate \(\bar x\). For independent replications \(i=1,\ldots,m\), let \(U_i\) be an unbiased evaluation of \(F(\bar x)\), let \(L_i\) satisfy \(\mathbb E[L_i]\le z^*\), and set \(D_i=U_i-L_i\). Then \(F(\bar x)-z^*\le\mathbb E[D_i]\). If the \(D_i\) are independent normal observations, the quantity \(G_{1-\alpha}=\bar D+t_{m-1,1-\alpha}S_D/\sqrt m\) is a one-sided \((1-\alpha)\)-confidence upper bound for \(\mathbb E[D_i]\), and hence a conservative certificate for the optimality gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Independent candidate evaluations paired with valid stochastic lower bounds yield a conservative one-sided confidence bound on the true optimality gap.
assumptions_latex: \(\bar x\in X\) is fixed independently of the validation replications.
\((U_i,L_i)\) are independent and identically distributed across replications, with finite variance.
\(D_i=U_i-L_i\) is normally distributed for the exact Student confidence statement.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb P\{F(\bar x)-z^*\le G_{1-\alpha}\}\ge 1-\alpha\).

notation.meaning: Candidate-value estimate and valid stochastic lower bound in replication i.
Sample mean and sample standard deviation of paired differences.

review_flags: A source specific to replicated lower-bound optimality-gap estimation for stochastic mixed-integer programs is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Under the stated unbiasedness, lower-bound, independence, and normality assumptions, the one-sided Student bound is coherent. A source specific to replicated SMIP optimality-gap estimation is still required.

children.title: Out-of-Sample Feasibility Validation
children.top_down_role: Validation of recourse feasibility and service performance on independent scenarios.

knowledge_statements.title: Out-of-Sample Feasibility Validation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact binomial validation of recourse feasibility or a specified service event on independent scenarios.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a candidate decision \(\bar x\) independently of validation scenarios \(\xi_1,\ldots,\xi_m\). Define \(I(\bar x,\xi)=1\) when the recourse problem for \((\bar x,\xi)\) is feasible and the prescribed service requirements hold, and define it to be zero otherwise. Let \(I_i=I(\bar x,\xi_i)\), \(K=\sum_{i=1}^m I_i\), and \(p=\mathbb P\{I(\bar x,\xi)=1\}\). For independent identically distributed scenarios, \(K\sim\operatorname{Binomial}(m,p)\). The one-sided Clopper--Pearson lower limit \(p_L=\operatorname{Beta}^{-1}(\alpha;K,m-K+1)\) for \(K>0\), with \(p_L=0\) for \(K=0\), satisfies \(\mathbb P_p\{p_L\le p\}\ge 1-\alpha\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Independent validation scenarios give an exact binomial lower confidence bound for the candidate's recourse-feasibility and service probability.
assumptions_latex: \(\bar x\) is selected without using the validation sample.
\(\xi_1,\ldots,\xi_m\) are independent draws from the deployment distribution.
The validation event is evaluated unambiguously for every sampled scenario.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p_L\ge p_0\) certifies service probability at least \(p_0\) with confidence \(1-\alpha\).

notation.meaning: Indicator of feasible recourse and successful service for the candidate under scenario xi.
One-sided exact binomial lower confidence limit.

review_flags: A source connecting the exact binomial certificate explicitly to SMIP out-of-sample feasibility validation is needed.

children.title: Discrete Solution-Selection Stability
children.top_down_role: Reliability of selected integer decisions under resampling.

knowledge_statements.title: Discrete Solution-Selection Stability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-sample lower confidence certificate for the probability that resampling selects the same integer decision.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A(S)\in\mathcal X_I\) be a deterministic selection rule applied to a random training sample \(S\), including fixed tie-breaking, and fix a reference decision \(x^\circ\in\mathcal X_I\). For independent resamples \(S_1,\ldots,S_B\), define \(J_b=\mathbf 1\{A(S_b)=x^\circ\}\), \(\widehat p=B^{-1}\sum_{b=1}^B J_b\), and \(p=\mathbb P\{A(S)=x^\circ\}\). Hoeffding's inequality gives \(\mathbb P\{p<\widehat p-\sqrt{\log(1/\alpha)/(2B)}\}\le\alpha\). Thus the truncated quantity \(p_L=\max\{0,\widehat p-\sqrt{\log(1/\alpha)/(2B)}\}\) is a distribution-free lower confidence certificate for selection stability.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeated independent resampling estimates how often the same integer decision is selected and supplies a distribution-free lower confidence bound.
assumptions_latex: The resamples \(S_1,\ldots,S_B\) are independent and follow the intended sampling law.
The solution-selection rule and tie-breaking convention are fixed before validation.
The reference decision \(x^\circ\) is fixed independently of these stability resamples.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb P\{p\ge p_L\}\ge1-\alpha\).

notation.meaning: Integer-solution selection rule for sample S.
Probability of selecting the reference decision under resampling.
Distribution-free lower confidence bound for selection probability.

review_flags: A dedicated source for resampling-based discrete SMIP selection stability is needed.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The Hoeffding lower bound is correct for independent Bernoulli repetitions with a reference decision fixed independently of validation. A dedicated source is needed for this resampling-based notion of discrete SMIP selection stability.
