children.title: Stochastic Model Generation
children.top_down_role: Preservation of stage, scenario, and nonanticipativity structure in solver-ready models.

children.title: Scenario-Tree Data Models
children.top_down_role: Data organizations for histories, probabilities, and stagewise decisions.

knowledge_statements.title: Scenario-Tree Data Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite rooted-tree representation of histories, conditional probabilities, data realizations, and adapted decisions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A finite scenario-tree model is a rooted directed tree \(T=(N,E)\) with stage map \(t:N\to\{0,\ldots,H\}\), parent map \(a(n)\) for nonroot nodes, conditional probabilities \(q_{n\mid a(n)}\ge0\), and node data \(\xi_n\). Children of each nonleaf node satisfy \(\sum_{n:a(n)=m}q_{n\mid m}=1\). The probability of node \(n\) is \(p_n=\prod_{v\in P(n)\setminus\{r\}}q_{v\mid a(v)}\). A node decision \(x_n\) is adapted because it depends only on the root-to-\(n\) history; scenarios sharing node \(n\) therefore share the same decision through stage \(t(n)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A scenario tree stores histories as nodes, conditional probabilities on arcs, realized data at nodes, and history-adapted decisions.
assumptions_latex: \(T\) is finite, rooted, and every nonroot node has exactly one parent.
Outgoing conditional probabilities at every nonleaf node sum to one.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p_n=\prod_{v\in P(n)\setminus\{r\}}q_{v\mid a(v)}\), and node-indexed decisions encode nonanticipativity.

notation.meaning: Unique root-to-node path ending at n.
Conditional arc probability and induced node probability.
Decision associated with the information history at node n.

children.title: Stochastic Structure Annotation System
children.top_down_role: Modeling-language metadata preserving stochastic block structure.

children.title: Stage Annotations
children.top_down_role: Modeling-language metadata identifying stage membership plus temporal structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Stage Annotations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Metadata assigning each model entity to the stage at which it is revealed or chosen.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For stages \(\mathcal T=\{0,\ldots,H\}\), a stage annotation consists of maps \(\tau_v:V\to\mathcal T\), \(\tau_c:C\to\mathcal T\), and \(\tau_d:D\to\mathcal T\), assigning each decision variable, constraint, and random-data item its decision, enforcement, or revelation stage. The annotation is temporally admissible when every coefficient used by constraint \(c\) is revealed no later than \(\tau_c(c)\), and every variable occurring in \(c\) satisfies \(\tau_v(v)\le\tau_c(c)\). Variables with the same stage and observable history are instances of one adapted decision rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stage annotations identify when variables are chosen, constraints enforced, and random data revealed, thereby defining temporal information availability.
assumptions_latex: \(V\), \(C\), and \(D\) are finite sets of variables, constraints, and random-data items.
Every model entity receives exactly one stage label.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The maps \(\tau_v,\tau_c,\tau_d\) define the stage partition and its temporal admissibility predicate.

notation.meaning: Stage maps for variables, constraints, and random data.
Model variables, constraints, and random-data items.

review_flags: Annotation semantics are implementation-dependent and need a specific stochastic-modeling interface source.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The annotation semantics are implementation-dependent and uncited. Moreover, variables sharing a stage and observable history need not be instances of one decision rule merely on that basis; variable identity or an explicit copy relation is also required.

children.title: Scenario Annotations
children.top_down_role: Modeling-language metadata identifying scenario membership plus uncertainty structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Scenario Annotations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Metadata associating model instances with scenario-tree nodes, histories, and probabilities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a scenario tree \(T=(N,E)\), a scenario annotation assigns each replicated model entity \(e\) a node \(\nu(e)\in N\), or equivalently a compatible history, and assigns each leaf scenario \(s\) a probability \(p_s\ge0\) with \(\sum_s p_s=1\). An entity annotated by node \(n\) is present precisely in descendant scenarios of \(n\). Decision-variable copies attached to the same node represent one history-adapted decision and must be identified or linked by nonanticipativity equalities; copies at distinct nodes may differ after their histories diverge.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Scenario annotations attach entity copies to tree nodes and probabilities, determining scenario membership and which decisions must satisfy nonanticipativity.
assumptions_latex: \(T\) is a finite rooted scenario tree.
Each replicated entity has one unambiguous node or history annotation.
Leaf probabilities are nonnegative and normalized.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\nu(e)\) determines scenario membership, while common-node decision copies represent the same nonanticipative decision.

notation.meaning: Scenario-tree node assigned to model entity e.
Probability assigned to leaf scenario s.

review_flags: The precise annotation API remains implementation-dependent.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cited scenario-tree section supports histories and probabilities but does not establish the proposed annotation API, entity-membership semantics, or copy-linking convention. Interface-specific documentation is required.

children.title: Annotation Consistency Checks
children.top_down_role: Structural validation of stage metadata relative to scenario metadata.

knowledge_statements.title: Annotation Consistency Checks
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural predicates required before compiling annotated stochastic models into an extensive form.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An annotated finite-stage stochastic model is consistent exactly when: every entity has one valid stage and node label; each node label has the annotated stage of that tree node; leaf probabilities are nonnegative and sum to one; every coefficient is revealed no later than the constraint using it; every variable in a constraint is chosen no later than that constraint's enforcement stage; and decision copies are identified if and only if their observable histories coincide at the decision stage. Failure of any predicate makes the annotated information structure or its deterministic-equivalent compilation ill-defined.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Consistency requires valid unique labels, normalized probabilities, causal data use, temporally valid constraints, and correct nonanticipativity classes.
assumptions_latex: The scenario tree and all stage and scenario annotations are finite.
Each constraint exposes its variables and random coefficients to the checker.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: All listed predicates hold if and only if the annotation system passes the structural consistency check.
review_flags: The completeness of these checks depends on the intended annotation system and requires interface documentation.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The exact completeness claim depends on the intended annotation system and is unsupported. The if-and-only-if identification rule also risks equating distinct decisions that merely share an observable history unless decision identity or copy classes are specified.

children.title: Deterministic-Equivalent Generation
children.top_down_role: Compilation into solver-ready scenario extensive forms.

knowledge_statements.title: Deterministic-Equivalent Generation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extensive-form compilation of a finite scenario-tree stochastic mixed-integer program.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite scenario tree with node probabilities \(p_n\), local feasible sets \(X_n\), node costs \(c_n\), and ancestor-coupling constraints, deterministic-equivalent generation creates one variable vector \(x_n\) per node and solves \(\min\sum_{n\in N}p_n c_n^\top x_n\) subject to every node-local and ancestor-coupling constraint. If leafwise copies \(x_{s,t}\) are generated instead, it additionally imposes \(x_{s,t}=x_{s',t}\) whenever scenarios \(s,s'\) share the same history through stage \(t\). Integrality declarations are preserved for every copy of an integer decision. The resulting finite mixed-integer program has the same feasible adapted policies and objective values as the tree model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compilation replicates variables and constraints over tree nodes, weights costs by probabilities, preserves integrality, and enforces nonanticipativity.
assumptions_latex: The scenario tree is finite and all node models are finite-dimensional.
The annotations identify stages, histories, probabilities, and integer-variable domains consistently.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The generated extensive-form mixed-integer program is policy- and objective-equivalent to the annotated finite-tree model.

children.title: Decomposition–Solver Integration
children.top_down_role: Interfaces between decomposition logic and mixed-integer tree search.

children.title: Lazy Recourse Separation
children.top_down_role: Deferred recourse evaluation and cut enforcement in solver callbacks.

knowledge_statements.title: Lazy Recourse Separation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Integer-incumbent callback procedure that evaluates deferred scenario recourse and adds globally valid violated cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a master mixed-integer model, scenario recourse oracles, and tolerance \(\varepsilon>0\). Whenever the solver produces an integer-feasible candidate \((\bar x,\bar\theta)\), solve each deferred recourse problem \(Q_s(\bar x)\). If scenario \(s\) is infeasible, obtain a globally valid feasibility inequality \(a_s^\top x\le b_s\) violated by \(\bar x\). If it is feasible and \(\bar\theta_s<Q_s(\bar x)-\varepsilon\), obtain a globally valid epigraph inequality \(\theta_s\ge\alpha_s+\beta_s^\top x\) violated by the candidate. Submit all such inequalities as lazy constraints. Accept the incumbent only when every scenario passes both tests; terminate under the host solver's stopping rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At each integer incumbent, solve deferred recourse problems, add violated valid feasibility or epigraph cuts, and accept only scenario-valid candidates.
assumptions_latex: Each recourse oracle either returns feasibility and value information or a valid infeasibility certificate.
Every submitted inequality is globally valid for the original SMIP formulation.
The solver invokes the lazy-constraint callback at every candidate incumbent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every accepted incumbent satisfies all deferred recourse conditions within tolerance \(\varepsilon\).

notation.meaning: Master variable approximating scenario-s recourse cost.

review_flags: Validity conditions differ between continuous and integer recourse; a source for the intended SMIP callback scheme is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind and callback role fit the container, but feasibility and epigraph-cut construction differ materially between continuous and integer recourse. A source establishing the intended globally valid callback scheme is required.

children.title: Relaxation Cut Separation
children.top_down_role: Scenario-aware strengthening during relaxation processing.

knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation Cut Separation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Node-relaxation callback that generates scenario-valid inequalities to strengthen the SMIP master relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a master relaxation, scenario separation oracles, a cut-validity domain \(D\), and tolerance \(\varepsilon>0\). At a relaxation solution \((\bar x,\bar\theta)\in D\), query each selected scenario oracle for an inequality \(g_s(x,\theta_s)\le0\) that is valid for every feasible integer solution in \(D\). Add the inequality as a user cut only if \(g_s(\bar x,\bar\theta_s)>\varepsilon\), optionally retaining the most violated cuts subject to a fixed budget. Reoptimize the relaxation and repeat until no oracle returns an eligible violated inequality, then return control to branch-and-bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Scenario oracles separate globally valid cuts at fractional nodes; violated eligible cuts are added until no useful strengthening remains.
assumptions_latex: Every generated cut is valid for all feasible integer solutions in its declared domain \(D\).
The callback distinguishes user cuts from incumbent-enforcing lazy constraints.
Separation and numerical acceptance use a fixed positive tolerance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: On exit, no queried oracle supplies an eligible cut violated by more than \(\varepsilon\) at the current relaxation solution.

notation.meaning: Domain on which generated cuts are guaranteed valid.
Scenario-s cut function, with validity convention g_s at most zero.

review_flags: A source is needed for scenario-aware user-cut validity and callback requirements in SMIP.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The generic separation loop is coherent, but user-cut admissibility, the meaning of the validity domain, and callback behavior are solver- and formulation-dependent. A specific SMIP source is required.

children.title: Scenario-Solution Reuse Interface
children.top_down_role: Reuse of subproblem solutions and incumbent information.

children.title: SMIP Warm Starts
children.top_down_role: Reuse of incumbent or relaxation information across repeated SMIP solves.

knowledge_statements.title: SMIP Warm Starts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasibility-checked reuse of incumbent policies, master states, and scenario subproblem states across related SMIP solves.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a new SMIP instance \(P'\), a previously stored first-stage decision \(x^0\), optional scenario decisions \(y_s^0\), and cached solver states. First map stored variables and scenarios to \(P'\). Project or repair \(x^0\) to satisfy the new first-stage bounds and integrality restrictions. For every scenario, recompute or repair \(y_s^0\) so that the new recourse constraints and nonanticipativity conditions hold. Submit the resulting policy only if it is feasible for \(P'\). Reuse a basis, node state, or cut only after verifying dimensional compatibility and continued validity; otherwise discard it. Initialize the solve with the accepted artifacts and use the host solver's ordinary termination rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Map, repair, and validate an old policy and solver state before using them to initialize a related SMIP instance.
assumptions_latex: A mapping between old and new variables, stages, and scenarios is available.
Feasibility and cut validity can be checked against the new instance \(P'\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every submitted incumbent is feasible for \(P'\), and every reused cut remains valid for \(P'\).
review_flags: Warm-start artifact semantics are solver-dependent and require a dedicated SMIP implementation source.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits the warm-start container, but reuse of bases, node states, cuts, and scenario artifacts is solver-dependent. A dedicated implementation source must specify compatibility and validity checks.

children.title: Scenario-Solution Transfer
children.top_down_role: Transfer of subproblem solutions across related scenarios.

knowledge_statements.title: Scenario-Solution Transfer
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reuse of scenario subproblem solutions at a new master iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a new first-stage point \(x'\) and a stored scenario solution \(y_s\) obtained at \(x\), first test \(y_s\in Y_s(x')\). If feasible, use \(y_s\) as the incumbent or warm start for scenario \(s\); otherwise retain only solver state that remains structurally valid. Solve the scenario subproblem from that state, producing \(y'_s\) and value \(Q_s(x')\). Any transferred cut is accepted only after its validity for the current formulation and parameterization is established. The output is \((y'_s,Q_s(x'))\), together with reusable certified solver information.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Test a stored scenario solution at the new first-stage point, reuse it when feasible, and transfer cuts or solver state only when their validity is preserved.
assumptions_latex: \(Y_s(x')\) is the feasible set of scenario \(s\) at the new first-stage point.
The scenario formulation and transferred solver-state semantics are known.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((y'_s,Q_s(x'))\) is obtained without treating an uncertified transferred object as valid.

notation.meaning: scenario-s feasible set at the new point
optimal scenario value at the new point

children.title: Transferability Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Structural differences limiting reuse across scenarios or planning iterations.

knowledge_statements.title: Transferability Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditions under which scenario solutions, bases, or cuts cease to transfer safely.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A stored scenario solution may be transferred from \(x\) to \(x'\) only if it satisfies the new constraints, hence \(y_s\in Y_s(x')\). A basis, node, or presolve state is transferable only when its referenced rows, columns, bounds, and variable meanings remain compatible. A cut \(\alpha+\beta^{\mathsf T}x\leq 0\) is transferable only if it is valid for every feasible first-stage point in the current formulation. Failure of any corresponding test is a boundary: the object may guide a heuristic, but it cannot certify feasibility, a bound, or optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reuse becomes uncertified when feasibility changes, solver-state structure becomes incompatible, or a cut is not globally valid for the current formulation.
assumptions_latex: The original and current scenario formulations can be compared.
Transferred objects are tagged with their formulation dependencies.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Failure of compatibility or validity prevents certified transfer.

notation.meaning: current feasible set for scenario s

children.title: SMIP Cut-Pool Management
children.top_down_role: Selection, aggregation, aging, and deletion of scenario-derived cuts.

knowledge_statements.title: SMIP Cut-Pool Management
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity-preserving selection, aggregation, aging, and deletion of scenario-derived cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Maintain a pool \(P_k\) of valid cuts, each with scenario tag, age, activity, and violation statistics. At iteration \(k\), evaluate violation \(v_j(x^k)\) for eligible cuts \(j\in P_k\), select a bounded subset with largest positive violation or recent activity, and add it to the master. Aggregate cuts only when the chosen nonnegative weights preserve validity. Reset the age of an active cut and increment other ages. Delete a cut when its age exceeds a threshold and it is neither active nor required for a recorded bound certificate. Never delete validity metadata for any retained or aggregated cut.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Score and select valid scenario cuts, aggregate them with validity-preserving weights, age inactive cuts, and delete only cuts not needed by certificates.
assumptions_latex: Every admitted cut is valid for the current master feasible set.
Aggregation weights are nonnegative.
Certificate-dependent cuts are identifiable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every cut inserted into the master remains valid, and certificate-dependent cuts remain available.

source_refs.locator: 3.5 Cutting Plane Method for the Solution of the All Integer Variable Linear Programming Problem p. 76

children.title: Parallel Scenario Computing
children.top_down_role: Computing patterns exploiting scenario and node separability.

children.title: Master–Worker Scenario Parallelism
children.top_down_role: Central coordination with distributed scenario evaluation.

knowledge_statements.title: Master–Worker Scenario Parallelism
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Synchronous central coordination of independently evaluated scenario subproblems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Partition the scenario set \(S\) among workers. At master iteration \(k\), the master broadcasts \(x^k\); each worker solves every assigned subproblem and returns scenario values, feasible solutions, and valid cuts tagged by \((s,k)\). The master waits for all required responses, forms \(\widehat Q(x^k)=\sum_{s\in S}p_sQ_s(x^k)\), inserts accepted cuts, and updates the master problem. Stop when the prescribed feasibility and bound-gap tests hold; otherwise broadcast the next point. The final output records the incumbent, certified bounds, and scenario response set used by the terminating test.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A central master broadcasts decisions, workers solve assigned scenarios, and the master synchronizes their tagged results before updating bounds and decisions.
assumptions_latex: \(S\) is finite and \(p_s\geq0\) with \(\sum_{s\in S}p_s=1\).
Scenario subproblems are conditionally independent given \(x^k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat Q(x^k)=\sum_{s\in S}p_sQ_s(x^k)\) uses a complete iteration-consistent response set.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: conditional scenario independence permits distributed evaluation followed by weighted aggregation

children.title: Batched Scenario Processing
children.top_down_role: Scenario grouping for communication control and workload balance.

knowledge_statements.title: Batched Scenario Processing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scenario grouping for bounded communication and balanced parallel work.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose a partition \(S=B_1\mathbin{\dot\cup}\cdots\mathbin{\dot\cup}B_m\) using estimated scenario costs. For a master point \(x^k\), assign each batch to a worker, solve all scenarios in that batch, and return one tagged message containing \(Q_s(x^k)\) and valid scenario information for every \(s\in B_i\). The coordinator accepts a batch only if its tag matches the intended iteration. It then computes each batch contribution \(q_i^k=\sum_{s\in B_i}p_sQ_s(x^k)\) and aggregates \(\sum_{i=1}^m q_i^k\). Repartition only between coordination epochs, preserving complete scenario coverage.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Partition scenarios into workload-balanced batches, process each batch as one communication unit, and aggregate only complete, correctly tagged batch results.
assumptions_latex: The batches form a disjoint cover of the finite scenario set.
Each returned scenario value corresponds to the broadcast point \(x^k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_{i=1}^m q_i^k=\sum_{s\in S}p_sQ_s(x^k)\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: a disjoint scenario partition preserves the full weighted sum while reducing message frequency
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

children.title: Asynchronous Scenario Processing
children.top_down_role: Coordination admitting delayed and uneven scenario results.

knowledge_statements.title: Asynchronous Scenario Processing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Master coordination with delayed, uneven, and out-of-order scenario responses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The master broadcasts tagged points \((x^k,k)\) without requiring all earlier workers to finish. Each worker returns scenario results tagged by \((s,k)\). The master may immediately accept any cut whose validity is global and independent of the current iterate; an iterate-specific value or feasibility result contributes to an aggregate only for its matching tag. Maintain bounded delay \(k-\tau_s(k)\leq D\), or explicitly exclude stale scenarios from stopping tests. Terminate only when the incumbent and certified bounds are computed from a response set satisfying the declared freshness and coverage rule; otherwise continue dispatching work.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Process tagged scenario results as they arrive, use globally valid cuts immediately, and apply freshness and coverage requirements before certifying termination.
assumptions_latex: Every response carries an unambiguous scenario and iterate tag.
Accepted cuts are valid for the current master formulation.
The stopping rule declares its scenario coverage and delay limit.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No stale iterate-specific result is used as if it belonged to the current aggregate or termination certificate.

knowledge_statements.title: SMIP Test Libraries

An experimental use of \(\mathcal L\) identifies the exact instance and metadata versions, preprocessing, scenario subsampling, resource limits, and computing environment, so that reported comparisons refer to the same mathematical instances.

children.title: SMIP Quality-Reporting System

children.title: Bound Reporting
children.top_down_role: Presentation of deterministic, dual, statistical, or incumbent bounds.

knowledge_statements.title: Bound Reporting
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consistent reporting of certified primal and dual bounds for minimization SMIPs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a minimization SMIP with optimal value \(z^*\), report a primal bound \(U\) only when it is the objective value of a policy feasible under the declared model and validation convention. Report a dual bound \(L\) only when its construction certifies \(L\leq z^*\). A bound record must state the optimization sense, units, time, scenario set or sampling scheme, confidence qualification if statistical, and whether the bound is deterministic or probabilistic. The consistency condition is \(L\leq z^*\leq U\); missing or uncertified endpoints are reported as unavailable, not as numerical bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For minimization, report only certified lower and feasible-policy upper bounds, together with their model, sampling, timing, units, and statistical qualifications.
assumptions_latex: The optimization problem is stated in minimization form.
Feasibility and bound certificates use the declared model and probability convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L\leq z^*\leq U\) whenever both reported endpoints are certified.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits reporting requirements, and the deterministic inequality is standard. The cited branch-and-bound section does not establish the broader SMIP reporting requirements concerning sampling, statistical confidence, timing, units, and provenance.

children.title: Optimality Gap Reporting
children.top_down_role: Comparable absolute, relative, solver-reported, or externally computed gaps.

knowledge_statements.title: Optimality Gap Reporting
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Absolute and scale-normalized gaps derived from compatible certified bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given compatible certified bounds \(L\leq z^*\leq U\) for a minimization problem, the absolute optimality gap is \(g_{\mathrm{abs}}=U-L\). For a declared scale \(d>0\), the relative gap is \(g_{\mathrm{rel}}=(U-L)/d\); a common convention is \(d=\max\{|U|,|L|,\varepsilon\}\) with fixed \(\varepsilon>0\). A report states the denominator convention and whether the displayed value is a fraction or percentage. If either bound is uncertified, statistically incompatible, or based on a different model or scenario sample, no certified optimality gap is reported.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The certified absolute gap is upper minus lower bound; a relative gap additionally requires an explicit positive scaling and compatible bound provenance.
assumptions_latex: \(L\) and \(U\) are certified for the same minimization problem.
The normalization scale satisfies \(d>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g_{\mathrm{abs}}=U-L\geq0\) and \(g_{\mathrm{rel}}=(U-L)/d\geq0\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition kind fits the leaf, but relative-gap conventions vary. The cited branch-and-bound section is not shown to support the stated max-magnitude denominator or the compatibility rules for statistical bounds.

children.title: Validation Reporting

knowledge_statements.title: Validation Reporting
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Out-of-sample assessment of a candidate SMIP policy under explicit sampling uncertainty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x\) be a candidate policy and let \(Z_1(x),\ldots,Z_n(x)\) be independent validation losses generated independently of policy selection. Report \(\bar Z_n(x)=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n Z_i(x)\), the sample size, sampling distribution, random seed, feasibility-violation rate, and an uncertainty interval with its construction and nominal coverage. Under finite variance, a standard approximate interval is \(\bar Z_n(x)\pm t_{n-1,1-\alpha/2}S_n/\sqrt n\). Training-sample performance must be labeled separately and must not be presented as independent validation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Report independent validation performance, sampling design, violations, and a qualified uncertainty interval; distinguish it from the sample used to select the policy.
assumptions_latex: The validation losses are independent and identically distributed with finite variance.
The validation sample is independent of policy selection.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The reported interval quantifies sampling uncertainty for the expected loss of the fixed policy \(x\), subject to its stated approximation.

knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Metric Comparability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compatibility conditions for comparing bounds, gaps, validation quality, and run time.

knowledge_statements.title: Decomposition Performance Profiles

The measure, success criterion, time limit, hardware, parallel resources, and treatment of failures must accompany every profile.

children.title: SMIP Computational Failure Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Boundaries where formulations, decompositions, or sampled models become weak, unstable, or impractical.

children.title: Relaxation-Duality Failure Regimes
children.top_down_role: Regimes where tractable relaxations poorly represent stochastic integer structure.

children.title: Large Integrality Gaps
children.top_down_role: Weak bounds from scenario-wise or extensive-form relaxation.

knowledge_statements.title: Large Integrality Gaps
knowledge_statements.scope_note: An explicit one-scenario SMIP family with an unbounded LP-relaxation ratio.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For each real parameter \(M\ge 1\), consider the one-scenario stochastic mixed-integer program
\[
z_{\mathrm{IP}}(M)=\min\{z:Mz\ge 1,\ z\in\{0,1\}\}.
\]
Its extensive-form LP relaxation replaces \(z\in\{0,1\}\) by \(0\le z\le 1\), giving
\[
z_{\mathrm{IP}}(M)=1,\qquad z_{\mathrm{LP}}(M)=\frac1M,\qquad \frac{z_{\mathrm{IP}}(M)}{z_{\mathrm{LP}}(M)}=M.
\]
Thus scenario-wise or extensive-form continuous relaxation has no uniform multiplicative approximation guarantee over this family: its integrality gap becomes arbitrarily large as \(M\to\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A binary one-scenario model can have integer optimum 1 and LP optimum 1/M, so its relaxation gap is unbounded as M grows.
assumptions_latex: The LP relaxation preserves the constraints and relaxes only integrality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(z_{\mathrm{IP}}(M)/z_{\mathrm{LP}}(M)=M\to\infty\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: explicit parametric MILP computation establishes the stated relaxation failure
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

children.title: Weak Benders Masters
children.top_down_role: Slow progress when continuous cuts poorly represent discrete recourse costs.

knowledge_statements.title: Weak Benders Masters
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Discrete recourse whose exact LP-relaxation underestimator remains arbitrarily weak.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(M>0\) and \(y\in[0,1]\), define the binary-recourse value
\[
Q_M(y)=M\min\{z:z\ge 1-y,\ z\in\{0,1\}\}.
\]
Then \(Q_M(y)=M\) for \(0\le y<1\) and \(Q_M(1)=0\). Relaxing \(z\in\{0,1\}\) to \(z\in[0,1]\) gives
\[
\bar Q_M(y)=M(1-y).
\]
Consequently, a Benders master whose LP-derived cuts exactly represent \(\bar Q_M\) underestimates the discrete recourse at every \(y\in(0,1)\) by
\[
Q_M(y)-\bar Q_M(y)=My.
\]
Thus \(\sup_{0<y<1}(Q_M(y)-\bar Q_M(y))=M\), and the weakness of this continuous-recourse master bound is unbounded over \(M\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When LP-derived cuts exactly represent the continuous recourse relaxation, they give a linear underestimator of the jumping binary-recourse function, and the resulting underestimation can be arbitrarily large.
assumptions_latex: The LP-derived cuts retained by the master exactly represent the displayed continuous-relaxation value function \(\bar Q_M\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sup_{0<y<1}(Q_M(y)-\bar Q_M(y))=M\), which is unbounded over \(M\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: explicit binary-recourse value function exhibits the weak-master mechanism

children.title: Nonanticipativity Duality Gaps
children.top_down_role: Persistent gaps caused by scenario separation of nonconvex feasible regions.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonanticipativity Duality Gaps
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A two-scenario nonconvex consensus model with an arbitrarily large Lagrangian duality gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(M>0\), \(X=\{0,1,2\}\), and define scenario costs by \(f_1(0)=f_1(2)=0\), \(f_1(1)=M\), \(f_2(1)=0\), and \(f_2(0)=f_2(2)=M\). The nonanticipative problem
\[
z_P=\min\{f_1(x_1)+f_2(x_2):x_1=x_2,\ x_1,x_2\in X\}
\]
has \(z_P=M\). After dualizing \(x_1=x_2\), its dual value is
\[
z_D=\sup_{\lambda\in\mathbb R}\min_{x_1,x_2\in X}\{f_1(x_1)+f_2(x_2)+\lambda(x_1-x_2)\}=0.
\]
Hence the nonanticipativity duality gap equals \(M\) and can be arbitrarily large.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Scenario separation convexifies incompatible discrete preferences: the consensus optimum costs M, while the nonanticipativity Lagrangian dual remains zero.
assumptions_latex: Scenario decisions have the common discrete domain \(X=\{0,1,2\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(z_P-z_D=M\), so the gap is unbounded over \(M\).

notation.meaning: Lagrangian dual optimum after relaxing consensus.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: finite explicit instance permits direct evaluation of primal and dual values

children.title: Decomposition Scaling Pathologies
children.top_down_role: Failures caused by scenario count, subproblem difficulty, cut growth, or coordination overhead.

children.title: Scenario-Tree Scaling Failure Boundary
children.top_down_role: Memory and coordination growth in large finite-scenario and multistage models.

children.title: Scenario-Set Explosion
children.top_down_role: Size growth caused by large finite scenario collections.

knowledge_statements.title: Scenario-Set Explosion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Enumeration complexity for independent finite-support uncertainty components.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose a stochastic program contains \(d\) independent uncertainty components, each having exactly \(q\ge2\) possible realizations with positive probability. Their Cartesian product contains
\[
S=q^d
\]
distinct joint scenarios. Any deterministic equivalent that explicitly materializes one variable-and-constraint block of at least \(n_s\) scalar entries for every joint scenario requires at least \(n_s q^d\) stored scalar entries and at least \(q^d\) scenario-block construction operations. Consequently, explicit scenario enumeration has exponential space and construction complexity in \(d\) when \(q\) and \(n_s\) are fixed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With d independent q-valued uncertainties, explicit enumeration creates q^d scenarios and therefore exponential model construction and storage.
assumptions_latex: \(d\in\mathbb N\) and \(q\ge2\).
Every joint realization is retained as a distinct scenario.
Each scenario block contains at least \(n_s\ge1\) scalar entries.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S=q^d\) and explicit representation requires \(\Omega(n_s q^d)\) storage.

children.title: Scenario-Tree Explosion
children.top_down_role: Node growth caused by branching across multistage uncertainty.

knowledge_statements.title: Scenario-Tree Explosion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact node growth across finitely many branching stages of a scenario tree.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider a rooted scenario tree with its root at stage \(0\) and \(T\) branching stages. Suppose every node at stage \(t-1\) has exactly \(b_t\ge1\) children for \(t=1,\ldots,T\). The total number of nodes from stage \(0\) through stage \(T\) is
\[
N_T=1+\sum_{t=1}^{T}\prod_{j=1}^{t}b_j.
\]
If \(b_t=b>1\) for every \(t\), then
\[
N_T=\frac{b^{T+1}-1}{b-1}.
\]
Thus any extensive formulation storing at least one distinct state, decision, or constraint block per node has space and construction requirements in \(\Omega(N_T)\), which are exponential in \(T\) for fixed \(b>1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A scenario tree with a root at stage zero and T constant-b branching stages has a geometric number of nodes, forcing exponential-in-T storage for node-explicit formulations.
assumptions_latex: \(T\in\mathbb N\).
For each \(t=1,\ldots,T\), every stage-\(t-1\) node has exactly \(b_t\ge1\) children.
The formulation explicitly stores at least one block per node.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(b_t=b>1\) for all \(t\), then \(N_T=(b^{T+1}-1)/(b-1)=\Theta(b^T)\), and node-explicit storage is \(\Omega(N_T)\).

notation.meaning: Total number of nodes from stage zero through stage T.
Branching factor from stage t-1 to stage t.
Number of branching stages after the root.

children.title: Memory Saturation Regimes
children.top_down_role: Storage limits arising from scenario data, node states, subproblems, or replicated model structures.

knowledge_statements.title: Memory Saturation Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: An in-core feasibility boundary for node-explicit stochastic formulations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let an explicit scenario-tree formulation contain \(N\) node blocks, and suppose every block requires at least \(m>0\) bytes for variables, constraints, coefficients, and indexing metadata. If available in-core memory is \(B>0\) bytes, then the representation requires at least \(mN\) bytes. Hence
\[
mN>B
\]
is a sufficient boundary for failure of any implementation that must retain all node blocks simultaneously in memory. For a constant-branching tree with \(N=(b^{T+1}-1)/(b-1)\), in-core storage is impossible whenever
\[
T>\log_b\!\left(1+\frac{(b-1)B}{m}\right)-1.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A node-explicit formulation cannot fit in memory once its per-node storage times the tree-node count exceeds the memory budget.
assumptions_latex: All \(N\) node blocks must be resident simultaneously.
For the horizon formula, \(b>1\) is constant.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(mN>B\) rules out an in-core node-explicit representation under the stated storage model.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: deterministic storage accounting yields the stated sufficient boundary
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

children.title: Coordination Bottlenecks
children.top_down_role: Synchronization or communication burdens induced by large scenario structures.

knowledge_statements.title: Coordination Bottlenecks
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A synchronous decomposition bound exposing communication and straggler limitations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
In one synchronous decomposition iteration, let \(S\in\mathbb N\) scenario subproblems have processing times \(\tau_1,\ldots,\tau_S\ge0\). Suppose a nonoverlapping aggregation, communication, and synchronization phase of duration \(c(S)\ge0\) begins only after every scenario result is available. Even with one dedicated worker per scenario, the iteration time satisfies
\[
T_{\mathrm{par}}\ge \max_{1\le s\le S}\tau_s+c(S).
\]
Relative to the serial scenario-processing time \(T_{\mathrm{ser}}=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\tau_s\), the speedup therefore satisfies
\[
\frac{T_{\mathrm{ser}}}{T_{\mathrm{par}}}\le
\frac{\sum_{s=1}^{S}\tau_s}{\max_{1\le s\le S}\tau_s+c(S)}.
\]
Thus additional workers cannot eliminate either the slowest-scenario delay or the subsequent coordination cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When synchronous coordination starts only after all scenario tasks finish, an iteration must include both the slowest scenario time and the nonoverlapping coordination time, which bounds parallel speedup.
assumptions_latex: \(S\in\mathbb N\) and \(\tau_s\ge0\) for \(s=1,\ldots,S\).
Scenario results are synchronized before the next iteration.
The coordination phase of duration \(c(S)\ge0\) starts after every scenario task finishes and does not overlap scenario processing.
At most one complete copy of each scenario task is used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_{\mathrm{par}}\ge\max_{1\le s\le S}\tau_s+c(S)\).

notation.meaning: Duration of the nonoverlapping coordination phase.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: critical-path scheduling bound for synchronous scenario decomposition

children.title: Integer Subproblem Bottlenecks
children.top_down_role: Decomposition dominated by repeated difficult scenario MIPs.

knowledge_statements.title: Integer Subproblem Bottlenecks
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Work and wall-time bounds for repeated scenario MIP solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose a synchronous decomposition method performs \(K\) iterations and solves \(S\) scenario mixed-integer subproblems in every iteration. Let \(T_{ks}\ge0\) be the time required to solve scenario \(s\) at iteration \(k\) to the prescribed optimality tolerance. The total scenario-solution work is
\[
W=\sum_{k=1}^{K}\sum_{s=1}^{S}T_{ks}.
\]
Even with \(S\) dedicated workers and no communication cost, synchronous wall time satisfies
\[
T_{\mathrm{wall}}\ge\sum_{k=1}^{K}\max_{1\le s\le S}T_{ks}.
\]
Therefore one repeatedly difficult scenario MIP can dominate every iteration and prevent proportional parallel scaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeated scenario MIPs require the sum of all solve work, while synchronous wall time is bounded below by the slowest MIP in each iteration.
assumptions_latex: Exactly \(S\) scenario MIPs are solved in each of \(K\) synchronous iterations.
\(T_{ks}\) includes all work needed to meet the specified MIP tolerance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_{\mathrm{wall}}\ge\sum_{k=1}^{K}\max_s T_{ks}\).

notation.meaning: Solve time for scenario s in iteration k.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: direct work accounting and synchronous critical-path bound
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

children.title: Cut-Pool Degeneracy Failure Regimes
children.top_down_role: Large collections of redundant, weak, or unstable cuts.

children.title: Cut-Pool Proliferation
children.top_down_role: Excessive growth in stored or active cutting planes.

knowledge_statements.title: Cut-Pool Proliferation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Master-size growth when decomposition retains all generated cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let a decomposition master initially contain \(R_0\) rows and retain \(r_{ks}\ge0\) cuts generated by scenario \(s\) at iteration \(k\). After \(K\) iterations its row count is
\[
R_K=R_0+\sum_{k=1}^{K}\sum_{s=1}^{S}r_{ks}.
\]
If every scenario contributes at least one retained cut per iteration, then \(R_K\ge R_0+KS\). In an explicit dense representation with \(n\) master variables, cut-coefficient storage is \(\Omega(nKS)\), and merely scanning all retained cut rows costs \(\Omega(KS)\) operations. Thus an unfiltered cut pool grows at least linearly in both iteration and scenario counts.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Retaining at least one cut per scenario per iteration creates at least KS new master rows and correspondingly growing storage and processing costs.
assumptions_latex: All generated cuts counted by \(r_{ks}\) remain active in storage.
For the dense-storage bound, every retained cut stores \(n\) coefficients.
At least one cut is retained per scenario and iteration.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_K\ge R_0+KS\), with dense coefficient storage \(\Omega(nKS)\).

notation.meaning: Master row count after K iterations.
Cuts retained from scenario s at iteration k.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: exact retained-row accounting under the stated cut-management policy

children.title: Degenerate Master Geometry
children.top_down_role: Master formulations with many equivalent faces, bases, or weakly distinguished incumbents.

knowledge_statements.title: Degenerate Master Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A geometric degeneracy condition for cut-based master linear programs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider a full-dimensional master polyhedron \(P=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax\ge b\}\) and a vertex \(\bar x\in P\). Let
\[
I(\bar x)=\{i:a_i^{\mathsf T}\bar x=b_i\}
\]
be its active-row set. Because \(\bar x\) is a vertex, \(\operatorname{rank}(A_{I(\bar x)})=n\). The vertex is geometrically degenerate whenever
\[
|I(\bar x)|>n.
\]
In particular, adding a redundant cut that is active at \(\bar x\) can increase \(|I(\bar x)|\) without changing \(P\), excluding \(\bar x\), or changing the normal cone of \(P\) at \(\bar x\). Such active-cut accumulation produces redundant active descriptions and supplies no geometric separation at that vertex.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A full-dimensional master vertex is geometrically degenerate when more than n constraints are active. Redundant cuts active at that vertex can increase the active-row count without changing the region or its local normal cone.
assumptions_latex: \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is a full-dimensional polyhedron.
\(\bar x\) is a vertex of \(P\).
Any added cut discussed in the final claim is redundant for \(P\) and active at \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(|I(\bar x)|>n\), then \(\bar x\) is geometrically degenerate; redundant cuts active at \(\bar x\) can increase this excess without changing \(P\).

notation.meaning: Indices of constraints active at the vertex.
Matrix formed from the active constraint normals.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard polyhedral degeneracy criterion specialized to a cut master

children.title: Redundant Cut Accumulation
children.top_down_role: Collections dominated by duplicate, inactive, weak, or nearly parallel cuts.

knowledge_statements.title: Redundant Cut Accumulation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A no-progress condition for cuts already implied by the master.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let the current master region be \(P_k=\{x:A_kx\ge b_k\}\). A proposed cut \(a^{\mathsf T}x\ge\beta\) is redundant at iteration \(k\) when
\[
\inf_{x\in P_k}a^{\mathsf T}x\ge\beta.
\]
For any collection \(C_k\) of such cuts,
\[
P_k\cap\bigcap_{(a,\beta)\in C_k}\{x:a^{\mathsf T}x\ge\beta\}=P_k.
\]
Consequently, retaining \(r\) redundant cuts leaves the master feasible region and optimal bound unchanged while adding \(r\) stored rows. Repeated accumulation can therefore increase memory and linear-algebra work without producing any relaxation improvement.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cut implied by the current master changes neither its feasible region nor its bound; storing many such cuts adds rows without progress.
assumptions_latex: \(P_k\) is nonempty.
Each cut in \(C_k\) satisfies the displayed implication test.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Adding \(C_k\) leaves \(P_k\) unchanged and cannot improve the master optimum.

notation.meaning: Master feasible region at iteration k.
Collection of cuts redundant for the current master.
Normal and right-hand side of a proposed cut.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: redundancy follows directly from polyhedral implication

children.title: Numerical Instability Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Precision or conditioning failures associated with large unstable cut collections.

knowledge_statements.title: Numerical Instability Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A conditioning boundary for floating-point master-basis computations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(B\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) be a nonsingular basis matrix selected from a cut-based master, let \(u\) be the arithmetic unit roundoff, and let \(\kappa_2(B)=\|B\|_2\|B^{-1}\|_2\). Standard first-order forward-error control for solving \(Bx=d\) requires the dimensionless product \(\kappa_2(B)u\) to be substantially below one. When
\[
\kappa_2(B)u\ge1,
\]
that perturbation bound has no finite denominator, so computed primal values, reduced costs, and cut-violation tests cannot be certified from this bound. Poorly scaled or nearly dependent accumulated cuts can drive the master across this numerical reliability boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When basis condition number times unit roundoff reaches one, standard floating-point error bounds no longer certify master solutions or cut violations.
assumptions_latex: \(B\) is a nonsingular master basis matrix.
Floating-point arithmetic has unit roundoff \(u>0\).
Error assessment uses normwise first-order perturbation bounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\kappa_2(B)u\ge1\) invalidates finite certification by the standard first-order forward-error bound.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard normwise conditioning threshold applied to a cut-master basis
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The qualitative conditioning failure is plausible, but the exact threshold and finite-denominator claim depend on the particular floating-point forward-error theorem, including its dimension- and algorithm-dependent constants. An authoritative numerical linear algebra source with a theorem or page locator is required before fixing this mathematical boundary.

children.title: Parallel Load Imbalance
children.top_down_role: Uneven scenario difficulty and synchronization delays.

knowledge_statements.title: Parallel Load Imbalance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic lower bound for synchronized parallel scenario evaluation with indivisible tasks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let scenario task \(s\in\{1,\ldots,S\}\) require time \(\tau_s\ge 0\), and assign every task without duplication to one of \(P\ge 1\) identical workers. If \(T_P\) is the makespan before the next synchronization, then
\[T_P\ge \max\left\{\max_s\tau_s,\frac{1}{P}\sum_{s=1}^S\tau_s\right\}.\]
Consequently, relative to serial time \(T_1=\sum_s\tau_s\), the parallel efficiency satisfies
\[\frac{T_1}{P T_P}\le \min\left\{1,\frac{\sum_s\tau_s}{P\max_s\tau_s}\right\}.\]
Thus a single disproportionately difficult scenario bounds efficiency regardless of the assignment rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Synchronization time is at least the longest scenario time and average worker load; one dominant scenario can therefore destroy parallel efficiency.
assumptions_latex: \(P\) identical workers execute indivisible scenario tasks.
Task times \(\tau_s\) exclude communication and are nonnegative.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[T_P\ge \max\left\{\max_s\tau_s,P^{-1}\sum_s\tau_s\right\},\qquad \frac{T_1}{P T_P}\le \frac{\sum_s\tau_s}{P\max_s\tau_s}.\]

notation.meaning: Execution time of scenario task s.
Parallel makespan through the synchronization point.

review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The scheduling lower bound and efficiency consequence are mathematically correct and fit the failure-boundary topic, but no inspectable citation supports the specialized parallel-decomposition framing.

children.title: Model-Sampling Failure Regimes
children.top_down_role: Failures caused by unsuitable scenario models, unstable discrete choices, or inadequate recourse.

children.title: Rare-Event Recourse Failures
children.top_down_role: Low-frequency scenarios producing severe feasibility or cost consequences.

knowledge_statements.title: Rare-Event Recourse Failures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sampling boundary when recourse infeasibility or severe loss is confined to a rare event.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(E\) be an uncertainty event with probability \(\varepsilon\in(0,1)\), and let \(N\) scenarios be sampled independently. The probability that the sample contains no realization in \(E\) is
\[\mathbb P\{E\text{ is omitted}\}=(1-\varepsilon)^N.\]
If \(E\) is the only event on which a candidate decision \(x\) has infeasible recourse, then omission prevents the sampled model from detecting that infeasibility. If instead \(Q(x,\xi)\ge M\) on \(E\), then
\[\mathbb E[Q(x,\xi)\mathbf 1_E]\ge \varepsilon M.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A rare event is missed with probability (1−ε)^N, potentially hiding event-specific infeasibility or at least εM of expected recourse cost.
assumptions_latex: Scenarios are independent draws from the true distribution.
\(E\) has probability \(\varepsilon\in(0,1)\).
For the cost conclusion, \(Q(x,\xi)\ge M\) for every \(\xi\in E\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\mathbb P\{\text{sample misses }E\}=(1-\varepsilon)^N,\qquad \mathbb E[Q(x,\xi)\mathbf 1_E]\ge \varepsilon M.\]

notation.meaning: Recourse cost for decision x and realization ξ.

children.title: Scenario-Omission Bias
children.top_down_role: Discrete plans distorted by missing uncertainty regimes.

knowledge_statements.title: Scenario-Omission Bias
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Binary protection example showing arbitrarily large regret after omission of a rare scenario.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider \(x\in\{0,1\}\), where protection \(x=1\) costs \(c>0\). A rare scenario occurs with probability \(\varepsilon\in(0,1)\) and incurs loss \(M>0\) only when \(x=0\). The true objective is
\[F(x)=cx+\varepsilon M(1-x).\]
If the rare scenario is omitted, the reduced objective is \(F_{\mathrm{om}}(x)=cx\), whose unique minimizer is \(x_{\mathrm{om}}=0\). Whenever \(\varepsilon M>c\), the true unique minimizer is \(x^\star=1\), and the omitted-scenario decision has true regret
\[F(x_{\mathrm{om}})-F(x^\star)=\varepsilon M-c,\]
which is unbounded as \(M\) grows with \(c\) and \(\varepsilon\) fixed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Omitting a rare loss scenario selects no protection even though protection is truly optimal; the resulting regret can grow without bound.
assumptions_latex: The rare scenario is absent from the reduced model.
\(\varepsilon M>c\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[x_{\mathrm{om}}=0,\qquad x^\star=1,\qquad F(x_{\mathrm{om}})-F(x^\star)=\varepsilon M-c.\]

children.title: Recourse Model Misspecification
children.top_down_role: Misleading plans caused by unrealistic corrective-action structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Recourse Model Misspecification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optimistic bias caused by modeling corrective actions that are unavailable in the true system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a first-stage decision \(x\) and realization \(\xi\), let
\[Q(x,\xi)=\inf_{y\in Y(x,\xi)}q(y,\xi),\qquad \widehat Q(x,\xi)=\inf_{y\in\widehat Y(x,\xi)}q(y,\xi),\]
where the infimum over an empty set is \(+\infty\). If \(Y(x,\xi)\subseteq\widehat Y(x,\xi)\), then
\[\widehat Q(x,\xi)\le Q(x,\xi).\]
Thus an expanded but unrealistic modeled recourse set is optimistic and may yield finite modeled recourse when the true recourse set is empty. Reverse inclusion instead yields conservative recourse values.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Allowing unrealizable corrective actions understates recourse cost and can make a truly infeasible plan appear feasible.
assumptions_latex: True and modeled recourse use the same extended-real cost function \(q\).
\(Y(x,\xi)\subseteq\widehat Y(x,\xi)\).
The infimum of an empty feasible set is \(+\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\widehat Q(x,\xi)\le Q(x,\xi),\qquad Y(x,\xi)=\varnothing\not\Rightarrow\widehat Y(x,\xi)=\varnothing.\]

notation.meaning: True and modeled optimal recourse values.

children.title: Discrete Policy Instability
children.top_down_role: Abrupt changes in selected policies under small data perturbations.

knowledge_statements.title: Discrete Policy Instability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Decision discontinuity at a tie between discrete policies.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X=\{0,1\}\) and define \(f_\theta(0)=0\) and \(f_\theta(1)=\theta\). For every \(\theta<0\), the unique optimizer is \(x^\star(\theta)=1\), whereas for every \(\theta>0\), it is \(x^\star(\theta)=0\). Thus arbitrarily small perturbations across \(\theta=0\) change the selected discrete policy by one unit, even though the optimal value
\[v(\theta)=\min\{0,\theta\}\]
is continuous.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a discrete-policy tie, an arbitrarily small data change can switch the optimizer even while the optimal value remains continuous.
assumptions_latex: The feasible policy set is \(X=\{0,1\}\).
The objective values are \(f_\theta(0)=0\) and \(f_\theta(1)=\theta\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[x^\star(\theta)=\begin{cases}1,&\theta<0,\\0,&\theta>0,\end{cases}\qquad v(\theta)=\min\{0,\theta\}.\]

notation.meaning: Unique optimizer away from the tie.

children.title: Multistage Decomposition Pathologies
children.top_down_role: Failure boundaries specific to nonconvex stagewise value approximation.

children.title: Discrete State-Space Explosion
children.top_down_role: Growth caused by integer linking states and their reformulations.

knowledge_statements.title: Discrete State-Space Explosion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exponential representation bound for binary linking states in multistage recourse.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose a stage carries an unrestricted binary linking state \(z\in\{0,1\}^m\) into its successor problem. Then the state domain has cardinality \(2^m\). Any exact tabular value-function representation storing one independently specifiable value for every state requires \(2^m\) entries. Likewise, any state-expanded formulation that explicitly contains a distinct successor block for every possible state contains at least \(2^m\) such blocks before uncertainty branching is counted. Therefore adding one unrestricted binary linking component doubles the explicit state-indexed representation size.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An unrestricted state of m binary linking variables has 2^m configurations, forcing exponential size in exact tabular or explicitly state-expanded representations.
assumptions_latex: The linking state contains \(m\) unrestricted binary components.
Values at distinct states may be independently specified.
The representation enumerates all states explicitly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[|\{0,1\}^m|=2^m,\qquad \text{explicit state-indexed storage}=\Omega(2^m).\]

children.title: Weak Stagewise Value Approximations
children.top_down_role: Slow progress from cuts informative only near sampled states.

knowledge_statements.title: Weak Stagewise Value Approximations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Information lower bound for value approximation when some discrete states remain unsampled.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\) be a finite stage-state set, let \(S\subsetneq X\) be the sampled states, and choose \(u\in X\setminus S\). Consider admissible value functions \(V_0\) and \(V_1\) with \(V_0(x)=0\) for every \(x\in X\), \(V_1(u)=\Delta>0\), and \(V_1(x)=0\) for \(x\ne u\). Any deterministic approximation rule using only observations on \(S\) produces the same estimate \(\widehat V(u)\) for both functions. Consequently,
\[\max_{i\in\{0,1\}}|\widehat V(u)-V_i(u)|\ge\frac{\Delta}{2}.\]
Thus estimates carrying no information from sampled states to \(u\) cannot guarantee a smaller uniform error over this admissible class.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If an unsampled state can have an independent value, sampled-state observations cannot distinguish two admissible functions and must incur at least half their separation at that state.
assumptions_latex: \(S\subsetneq X\) and \(u\in X\setminus S\).
The deterministic approximation rule observes function values only on \(S\).
The admissible class contains \(V_0\) and \(V_1\) as specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\inf_{a\in\mathbb R}\max_{i\in\{0,1\}}|a-V_i(u)|=\frac{\Delta}{2}.\]

notation.meaning: Value separation at the unsampled state.
Estimated value at the unsampled state.

children.title: Nonfinite Cut Families for General-Integer States
children.top_down_role: Loss of finite-family termination arguments outside finite state representations.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonfinite Cut Families for General-Integer States
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete general-integer value function requiring infinitely many affine supporting cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the unbounded general-integer state \(z\in\mathbb Z\), define \(Q(z)=z^2\). For every \(k\in\mathbb Z\), the affine function \(\ell_k(z)=2kz-k^2\) satisfies \(\ell_k(z)\le Q(z)\), with equality at \(z=k\), and
\[Q(z)=\sup_{k\in\mathbb Z}\ell_k(z)\quad\text{for every }z\in\mathbb Z.\]
No finite subfamily gives this representation on all of \(\mathbb Z\): the maximum of finitely many affine functions grows at most linearly as \(|z|\to\infty\), whereas \(Q(z)\) grows quadratically. Hence integrality alone does not provide a finite global family of these affine cuts on an unbounded state domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The integer-state function z² is the supremum of infinitely many affine tangent cuts, but no finite subset represents it globally.
assumptions_latex: The state domain is the unbounded set \(\mathbb Z\).
Cuts are affine functions required to underestimate \(Q\) globally.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[Q(z)=\sup_{k\in\mathbb Z}(2kz-k^2),\qquad Q\ne\max_{k\in K}(2kz-k^2)\ \text{on }\mathbb Z\ \text{for every finite }K\subset\mathbb Z.\]

notation.meaning: Affine supporting cut indexed by integer k.

children.title: Stochastic MIP Application Templates
children.top_down_role: Recurring architectures coupling uncertain operations with discrete planning, commitment, location, production, routing, or scheduling decisions.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: Chapter 8, Thermal and Hydro Electricity Production

children.title: Stochastic Unit Commitment
children.top_down_role: Power-system architecture coupling discrete generator commitment with uncertain operational recourse.

children.title: Unit-Commitment Horizon Architectures
children.top_down_role: Staging choices for commitment and corrective operation.

children.title: Day-Ahead Two-Stage Unit Commitment
children.top_down_role: Day-ahead commitments followed by scenario-dependent operation.

knowledge_statements.title: Day-Ahead Two-Stage Unit Commitment
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical two-stage template with here-and-now commitments and scenario-dependent dispatch.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given finite generator, period, and scenario sets \(G\), \(T\), and \(S\), with scenario probabilities \(p_s\), a two-stage unit-commitment template is
\[\min_{u,v}\left\{\sum_{g\in G,t\in T}\bigl(C_g^{\mathrm{nl}}u_{gt}+C_g^{\mathrm{su}}v_{gt}\bigr)+\sum_{s\in S}p_sQ_s(u)\right\},\]
where \(u_{gt},v_{gt}\in\{0,1\}\), \(u_{gt}-u_{g,t-1}\le v_{gt}\), and
\[Q_s(u)=\min_{p_{\cdot\cdot s},\ell_{\cdot s}\ge0}\left\{\sum_{g\in G,t\in T}C_g(p_{gts})+V\sum_{t\in T}\ell_{ts}:\ \sum_{g\in G}p_{gts}+\ell_{ts}=D_{ts},\ \underline P_gu_{gt}\le p_{gts}\le\overline P_gu_{gt}\right\}.\]
Commitment and startup decisions are common to all scenarios, whereas dispatch and load shedding are scenario dependent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Day-ahead binary commitments are chosen before uncertainty, followed by scenario-specific dispatch and load-shedding recourse.
assumptions_latex: \(G\), \(T\), and \(S\) are finite sets.
\(p_s\ge0\) for every \(s\in S\) and \(\sum_{s\in S}p_s=1\).
Commitment and startup variables are chosen before the scenario is revealed.
Dispatch costs, demands, capacity limits, and initial commitment values are defined.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\min_{u,v}\left\{C^{\mathrm{DA}}(u,v)+\sum_{s\in S}p_sQ_s(u)\right\},\quad (u,v)\text{ scenario independent},\quad (p_{\cdot\cdot s},\ell_{\cdot s})\text{ scenario dependent}.\]

children.title: Multistage Unit Commitment
children.top_down_role: Sequential commitment and operation under progressively revealed uncertainty.

knowledge_statements.title: Multistage Unit Commitment
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scenario-tree formulation for sequential commitment and dispatch with nonanticipative decisions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathcal T\) be a finite scenario tree with root \(r\), path probabilities \(\pi_n\), and parent \(a(n)\) for every nonroot node \(n\ne r\). Associate with each node binary commitment and startup decisions \(u_{gn},v_{gn}\), dispatch \(p_{gn}\), and load shedding \(\ell_n\). A multistage template minimizes
\[\sum_{n\in\mathcal T}\pi_n\left[\sum_g\bigl(C_g^{\mathrm{nl}}u_{gn}+C_g^{\mathrm{su}}v_{gn}+C_g(p_{gn})\bigr)+V\ell_n\right]\]
subject to nodewise balance and capacity constraints and, for each \(n\ne r\),
\[u_{gn}-u_{g,a(n)}\le v_{gn}.\]
Root transition constraints use a specified initial commitment state. Node-indexed decisions depend only on the history reaching their node; equivalently, scenario-indexed copies sharing the same observed history must be equal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Commitment and dispatch decisions are revised along a scenario tree while decisions sharing the same observed history remain identical.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal T\) is a finite rooted scenario tree.
\(\pi_n\) is the probability of reaching node \(n\).
The initial commitment state at the root is specified.
Decisions at a node use only information revealed along its root-to-node path.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\min\sum_{n\in\mathcal T}\pi_nc_n(u_n,v_n,p_n,\ell_n)\quad\text{subject to nodewise unit constraints and nonanticipativity}.\]

notation.meaning: Parent of a nonroot node n.
Node-indexed commitment, startup, dispatch, and load-shedding decisions.

children.title: Rolling-Horizon Stochastic Unit Commitment
children.top_down_role: Repeated commitment optimization with updated forecasts and system states.

knowledge_statements.title: Rolling-Horizon Stochastic Unit Commitment
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Receding-horizon procedure that repeatedly resolves stochastic unit commitment after observing new information.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Input an initial physical state \(s_0\), decision epochs \(k=0,\ldots,K-1\), a look-ahead length \(H\), and a conditional scenario generator. At epoch \(k\), observe \(s_k\); update the conditional distribution \(\mathcal P_k\) of demand and renewable generation; construct scenarios over periods \(k,\ldots,k+H\); solve the resulting stochastic unit-commitment model with initial conditions fixed by \(s_k\); implement only its first-period commitment and dispatch action \(a_k\); observe \(\xi_{k+1}\); and update
\[s_{k+1}=F(s_k,a_k,\xi_{k+1}).\]
After epoch \(K-1\), output the implemented trajectory \((a_0,\ldots,a_{K-1})\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly update forecasts, solve a finite stochastic commitment horizon, implement its first action, and advance the physical state.
assumptions_latex: The observed state \(s_k\) records all commitment-history data needed by future constraints.
A conditional scenario model \(\mathcal P_k\) is available at every epoch.
Each finite-horizon subproblem is solved to the prescribed tolerance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[a_k=\operatorname{FirstAction}\bigl(\operatorname{SolveSUC}(s_k,\mathcal P_k,H)\bigr),\qquad s_{k+1}=F(s_k,a_k,\xi_{k+1}).\]

notation.meaning: First-period action implemented at epoch k.
Conditional uncertainty model available at epoch k.

children.title: Unit-Commitment Uncertainty-Recourse Architecture
children.top_down_role: Operational recourse structures associated with major power-system uncertainties.

children.title: Demand-Renewable Uncertainty Taxonomy
children.top_down_role: Commitment architectures driven by demand and variable-generation uncertainty.

children.title: Load Uncertainty
children.top_down_role: Demand forecast variation affecting commitment feasibility, cost, or capacity adequacy.

knowledge_statements.title: Load Uncertainty
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-horizon stochastic demand process used in unit-commitment balance and recourse constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Load uncertainty over periods \(t=1,\ldots,T\) is represented by a nonnegative stochastic process \((D_t)_{t=1}^T\) on a probability space \((\Omega,\mathcal F,\mathbb P)\), adapted to an information filtration \((\mathcal F_t)_{t=0}^T\). Relative to a planning-time forecast, write
\[D_t=\widehat D_{t\mid0}+\varepsilon_t,\]
where \(\varepsilon_t\) is the forecast error. In stochastic unit commitment, each decision must be measurable with respect to the information available when that decision is made, while dispatch or load-shedding recourse enforces balance against the load revealed by that time. A finite scenario representation consists of trajectories \(D_{ts}\) with probabilities \(p_s\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Load uncertainty is an adapted nonnegative demand process represented through forecast errors or weighted demand trajectories and balanced through recourse after relevant information is revealed.
assumptions_latex: \(T<\infty\) and \(D_t\ge0\) almost surely.
\((\mathcal F_t)_{t=0}^T\) represents information revealed through time \(t\).
For a finite scenario representation, \(p_s\ge0\) and \(\sum_s p_s=1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[D_t=\widehat D_{t\mid0}+\varepsilon_t,\qquad D_t\text{ is }\mathcal F_t\text{-measurable},\qquad \sum_s p_s=1.\]

notation.meaning: Realized system load in period t.
Load in period t along scenario s.

children.title: Renewable-Generation Uncertainty
children.top_down_role: Variable-generation forecast variation affecting commitment or balancing requirements.

knowledge_statements.title: Renewable-Generation Uncertainty
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scenario-based renewable availability for two-stage stochastic unit commitment.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For periods \(t\in T\), renewable units \(r\in R\), and scenarios \(\omega\in\Omega\), let \(\widehat W_{rt}\ge 0\) be forecast production and \(\varepsilon^W_{rt\omega}\) its forecast error. Renewable-generation uncertainty is the random availability \[W_{rt\omega}=\min\{\overline W_{rt},\max\{0,\widehat W_{rt}+\varepsilon^W_{rt\omega}\}\}.\] A feasible recourse dispatch satisfies \(0\le w_{rt\omega}\le W_{rt\omega}\); renewable curtailment is \(c_{rt\omega}=W_{rt\omega}-w_{rt\omega}\ge0\). The scenario probabilities satisfy \(p_\omega>0\) and \(\sum_{\omega\in\Omega}p_\omega=1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Renewable uncertainty is scenario-dependent available generation obtained from a bounded forecast error; realized dispatch cannot exceed availability, and unused availability is curtailment.
assumptions_latex: \(T\), \(R\), and finite \(\Omega\) are nonempty.
Forecasts and nameplate limits are finite and nonnegative.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(0\le w_{rt\omega}\le W_{rt\omega}\le\overline W_{rt}\) and \(c_{rt\omega}\ge0\).

notation.meaning: renewable power available in scenario omega

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cited general stochastic-systems section does not support the specific clipped renewable-availability and curtailment model. Also, the plain statement calls the forecast error bounded, whereas the formula bounds availability by clipping an otherwise unrestricted error.

children.title: Joint Forecast-Error Structure
children.top_down_role: Dependence patterns linking demand errors with renewable-generation errors.

knowledge_statements.title: Joint Forecast-Error Structure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Joint load-renewable error law across units, locations, and times.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\varepsilon=(\varepsilon^D,\varepsilon^W)\) collect all load and renewable forecast errors over the scheduling horizon. Its joint forecast-error structure is a probability law \(P_\varepsilon\) on \(\mathbb R^m\), not merely its marginal laws. When second moments exist, cross-dependence includes \[\Sigma_{DW}=\mathbb E[(\varepsilon^D-\mu_D)(\varepsilon^W-\mu_W)^{\mathsf T}],\] together with temporal and spatial covariance blocks. A finite scenario model \(\{(\varepsilon_\omega,p_\omega)\}_{\omega\in\Omega}\) represents this structure when \(p_\omega>0\), \(\sum_\omega p_\omega=1\), and all uncertain quantities in a scenario share the same index \(\omega\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The joint structure is the full multivariate law of load and renewable errors, including cross-variable, temporal, and spatial dependence represented by coherent scenarios.
assumptions_latex: \(\varepsilon\) is a finite-dimensional random vector.
Second moments exist when covariance matrices are used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P_\varepsilon\) determines both marginal uncertainty and dependence among forecast errors.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cited section does not specifically support multivariate load-renewable forecast-error modeling. A scenario collection represents the stated joint law only when its discrete distribution equals that law; shared scenario indices and normalized probabilities alone do not establish this.

children.title: Commitment Sensitivity Regimes
children.top_down_role: Conditions under which forecast variation materially changes discrete commitment choices.

knowledge_statements.title: Commitment Sensitivity Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Parametric regimes in which uncertainty changes the optimal commitment schedule.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\theta\in\Theta\) parameterize a forecast-error law and let \(U\) be the finite set of feasible binary commitment schedules. Define \[F(u;\theta)=C^{\mathrm{DA}}(u)+\mathbb E_{\theta}[Q(u,\xi)],\qquad U^*(\theta)=\mathop{\mathrm{argmin}}_{u\in U}F(u;\theta).\] A commitment-stability regime is a connected set \(K\subseteq\Theta\) on which \(U^*(\theta)\) is constant. A commitment-switching boundary consists of parameters \(\theta\) for which distinct schedules \(u,v\in U\) satisfy \(F(u;\theta)=F(v;\theta)=\min_{z\in U}F(z;\theta)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sensitivity regime is a connected parameter region with the same optimal commitments; boundaries occur where two or more schedules tie for optimality.
assumptions_latex: \(U\) is finite and nonempty.
\(F(u;\theta)\) is finite for every compared schedule and parameter.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Inside a stability regime the optimal-schedule set is unchanged; switching can occur at an optimal-value tie.

notation.meaning: optimal recourse cost for commitment u and realization xi

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The generic sensitivity chapter does not substantiate this parametric unit-commitment construction. Calling the optimal-tie locus a switching boundary additionally requires regularity assumptions: ties need not be topological boundaries, and switching under discontinuous objectives need not have the stated characterization.

children.title: Dispatch-Reserve Recourse Coupling
children.top_down_role: Corrective operating decisions involving dispatch, reserves, and flexibility.

children.title: Dispatch Recourse
children.top_down_role: Corrective generation output decisions following uncertainty realization.

knowledge_statements.title: Dispatch Recourse
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scenario-dependent generation adjustment after commitment and uncertainty realization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a commitment schedule \(u_{gt}\in\{0,1\}\). Dispatch recourse in scenario \(\omega\) is a vector \(p_\omega=(p_{gt\omega})\) satisfying, for each period \(t\), \[\sum_g p_{gt\omega}+\sum_r w_{rt\omega}=D_{t\omega},\qquad \underline P_g u_{gt}\le p_{gt\omega}\le\overline P_g u_{gt},\] together with scenario-wise ramp inequalities \(-R_g^-\le p_{gt\omega}-p_{g,t-1,\omega}\le R_g^+\), modified where startup or shutdown allowances apply. Its recourse value is the minimum scenario operating cost over this feasible set, with \(+\infty\) assigned when the set is empty.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dispatch recourse reoptimizes scenario generation under fixed commitments while enforcing balance, capacity, and intertemporal ramp limits.
assumptions_latex: Commitment \(u\) is chosen before scenario revelation.
Demand and renewable availability are known within each recourse scenario.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Feasible \(p_\omega\) balances realized net demand without changing \(u\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A general recourse section does not support the specific unit-commitment balance, capacity, ramping, startup, and shutdown formulation. Generator and renewable index sets and several parameters are not introduced, while the ramp modification is left informal.

children.title: Reserve Recourse
children.top_down_role: Deployment or reallocation of committed reserve capability.

knowledge_statements.title: Reserve Recourse
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scenario deployment of procured upward and downward operating reserve.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given first-stage reserve awards \(r^+_{gt},r^-_{gt}\ge0\), reserve recourse selects deployments \(a^+_{gt\omega},a^-_{gt\omega}\) after scenario \(\omega\) is observed. They satisfy \[0\le a^+_{gt\omega}\le r^+_{gt},\qquad 0\le a^-_{gt\omega}\le r^-_{gt},\qquad p_{gt\omega}=p^0_{gt}+a^+_{gt\omega}-a^-_{gt\omega},\] as well as committed-unit capacity, ramping, and system balance constraints. Reserve recourse is feasible only if the procured awards and other flexible resources admit such deployments for every scenario required by the model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reserve recourse deploys no more than the procured upward or downward reserve and couples that deployment to realized dispatch and balance.
assumptions_latex: Reserve awards are fixed before uncertainty is observed.
Deployment occurs within the modeled response interval.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(a^+_{gt\omega}\le r^+_{gt}\), \(a^-_{gt\omega}\le r^-_{gt}\), and deployment changes realized dispatch.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cited generic recourse section does not support this reserve-procurement and deployment formulation.
