The domains of generator, period, and scenario indices and the precise capacity, ramp, response-time, and balance conditions require an operating-reserve or stochastic-unit-commitment source.

children.title: Flexibility Substitution
children.top_down_role: Tradeoffs among redispatch, reserves, storage, curtailment, or responsive demand.

knowledge_statements.title: Flexibility Substitution
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Aggregate substitution among dispatch, reserve, storage, and responsive demand.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a fixed period and scenario, let flexible resource \(k\) provide a signed adjustment \(z_k\in[\underline z_k,\overline z_k]\). If resources interact only through the aggregate balancing requirement \(\sum_k z_k=\Delta\), then the attainable aggregate adjustment set is the Minkowski sum \[\mathcal Z=\sum_k[\underline z_k,\overline z_k]=\left[\sum_k\underline z_k,\sum_k\overline z_k\right].\] Hence resources are feasibility substitutes for imbalance \(\Delta\) precisely when \(\Delta\in\mathcal Z\). Technology-specific ramping, energy, network, or reserve-deliverability constraints generally destroy this exact aggregate substitution representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Independent flexible resources substitute through their summed adjustment interval; intertemporal, network, or deliverability constraints limit that substitution.
assumptions_latex: Each local adjustment set is a nonempty interval.
No constraints couple resources except aggregate balance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Delta\) is coverable if and only if \(\Delta\in[\sum_k\underline z_k,\sum_k\overline z_k]\).

notation.meaning: adjustment supplied by flexible resource k

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The interval Minkowski-sum statement is mathematically plausible under a finite resource set, but that set is not introduced or assumed finite. The cited generic recourse section does not support the claimed dispatch-reserve-storage-demand substitution interpretation or its stated failure modes.

children.title: Recourse-Coupling Regimes
children.top_down_role: Operational conditions where dispatch choices constrain reserve availability or conversely.

knowledge_statements.title: Recourse-Coupling Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separable versus coupled dispatch-reserve recourse feasible sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For fixed first-stage decision \(x\) and scenario \(\omega\), let \(Y_D(x,\omega)\) and \(Y_R(x,\omega)\) denote dispatch and reserve-recourse sets. The regime is recourse-separable when \[Y(x,\omega)=Y_D(x,\omega)\times Y_R(x,\omega)\quad\text{and}\quad q(y_D,y_R)=q_D(y_D)+q_R(y_R).\] It is recourse-coupled when either equality fails. Shared capacity, ramping, energy, network-flow, or balance constraints produce coupling because feasibility of one recourse component then depends on the value chosen for another.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dispatch and reserve recourse are separable only when their feasible set is Cartesian and their cost additive; shared physical constraints create coupling.
assumptions_latex: The first-stage decision and scenario are fixed.
All recourse sets are defined in compatible finite-dimensional spaces.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Under separability, recourse minimization decomposes; otherwise dispatch and reserve must be optimized jointly.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The separability definition fits the container, but the cited generic recourse section does not substantiate the dispatch-reserve coupling taxonomy. The decomposition conclusion also needs nonemptiness and attainment, or should be stated in terms of infima.

children.title: Outage-Contingency Recourse Taxonomy
children.top_down_role: Corrective operation under equipment outages and contingency scenarios.

children.title: Equipment-Outage Recourse
children.top_down_role: Corrective operation following generator, transmission, or supporting-equipment failures.

knowledge_statements.title: Equipment-Outage Recourse
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Corrective redispatch after scenario-dependent generator or line unavailability.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(a_{e\omega}\in\{0,1\}\) indicate whether equipment \(e\) is available in scenario \(\omega\). Equipment-outage recourse selects post-outage operating variables while preserving first-stage commitments. For a generator \(g\), \[\underline P_g u_{gt}a_{g\omega}\le p_{gt\omega}\le\overline P_g u_{gt}a_{g\omega};\] for an unavailable transmission element \(\ell\), \(a_{\ell\omega}=0\) imposes \(f_{\ell t\omega}=0\). Remaining variables must satisfy balance, network, ramping, and corrective-action limits. Thus failed equipment contributes no capacity during the associated scenario.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Equipment-outage recourse redispatches the surviving system while forcing failed generators or lines to contribute zero capacity or flow.
assumptions_latex: Availability indicators are revealed before corrective recourse.
First-stage commitment decisions remain fixed during recourse.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(a_{e\omega}=0\), the failed equipment supplies no scenario capacity or flow.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The general recourse citation does not support generator- and transmission-outage modeling. Setting an unavailable line's flow to zero is insufficient unless the associated network equation is also disabled or reformulated; an authoritative security-constrained power-system source is required.

children.title: Security-Contingency Recourse
children.top_down_role: Corrective operation across designated power-system security events.

knowledge_statements.title: Security-Contingency Recourse
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Post-contingency corrective actions satisfying network-security constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each contingency \(c\in\mathcal C\) and uncertainty scenario \(\omega\), security-contingency recourse is a corrective state \((p^{c\omega},f^{c\omega},\vartheta^{c\omega})\) satisfying nodal balance and the contingency network equations. Under a DC model, each in-service line \(\ell=(i,j)\) obeys \[f^{c\omega}_{\ell t}=a^c_\ell B_\ell(\vartheta^{c\omega}_{it}-\vartheta^{c\omega}_{jt}),\qquad |f^{c\omega}_{\ell t}|\le a^c_\ell\overline F^c_\ell.\] Corrective generation changes also satisfy contingency response, capacity, and ramp limits. Security recourse is feasible when these conditions hold for every modeled pair \((c,\omega)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Security-contingency recourse corrects dispatch after each modeled contingency while satisfying nodal balance, post-contingency network limits, and response constraints.
assumptions_latex: A DC network approximation is used.
The contingency set \(\mathcal C\) is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every required \((c,\omega)\) admits a network-feasible corrective operating state.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No citation is supplied for the DC post-contingency network equations, corrective-response constraints, or universal scenario-contingency feasibility requirement. The definition is domain-specific and cannot rely on standard-field rationale alone.

children.title: Common-Cause Event Regimes
children.top_down_role: Correlated or cascading failures that invalidate isolated-event treatment.

knowledge_statements.title: Common-Cause Event Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dependent multi-equipment outages generated by a shared latent event.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A_e\in\{0,1\}\) denote equipment availability and let \(Z\) be a latent event variable, such as a storm, wildfire, or substation failure. A common-cause regime is present when at least two distinct elements \(e\ne e'\) satisfy \[\mathbb P(A_e=0,A_{e'}=0)\ne\mathbb P(A_e=0)\mathbb P(A_{e'}=0),\] with their dependence represented through \(P(A\mid Z)P_Z\). A scenario generator that independently samples all \(A_e\) is therefore invalid for this regime unless its resulting joint law reproduces the required simultaneous-outage probabilities.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A common-cause regime has dependent simultaneous outages driven by a shared latent event, so independent equipment sampling generally misrepresents risk.
assumptions_latex: At least two equipment elements are modeled.
The joint availability distribution is well defined.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Common-cause outages require a joint, generally nonproduct distribution of equipment availability.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Ordinary pairwise dependence does not by itself identify a common-cause mechanism, and the expression P(A|Z)P_Z omits marginalization over Z. The generic stochastic-systems citation cannot determine the correct common-cause formalization.

children.title: Corrective Feasibility Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Contingency conditions where available operational recourse cannot restore feasibility.

knowledge_statements.title: Corrective Feasibility Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between contingencies admitting corrective recourse and those requiring violation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For fixed first-stage decision \(x\) and realization \(\xi\), introduce nonnegative slacks \(s\) into all corrective balance, capacity, ramp, and network constraints, and define \[\phi(x,\xi)=\min\{\mathbf 1^{\mathsf T}s:(y,s)\text{ satisfies the slack-relaxed corrective constraints},\ s\ge0\}.\] Corrective recourse is feasible exactly when \(\phi(x,\xi)=0\). The corrective feasibility boundary in the realization space is the boundary of \(\{\xi:\phi(x,\xi)=0\}\); realizations with \(\phi(x,\xi)>0\) lie beyond the corrective capability of \(x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimum total violation is zero exactly for correctable realizations; its zero-level feasible set separates correctable events from unavoidable violations.
assumptions_latex: The slack-relaxed corrective problem is feasible and attains its minimum.
All slacks have strictly positive weights.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\phi(x,\xi)=0\) if and only if unrelaxed corrective recourse exists.

notation.meaning: fixed first-stage commitment and procurement decision

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The generic recourse citation does not support this feasibility-boundary construction. The relaxation must specify how equalities and both inequality directions receive slacks and ensure zero slack is exactly the original system; defining a boundary also requires a stated realization space and topology.

children.title: Unit-Commitment Coupling Regimes
children.top_down_role: Unit-commitment variants coupled to network security or flexible resources.

children.title: Security-Constrained Stochastic Unit Commitment
children.top_down_role: Commitment integrated with transmission and contingency-security recourse.

knowledge_statements.title: Security-Constrained Stochastic Unit Commitment
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-stage finite-scenario formulation with network and contingency recourse.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For finite uncertainty scenarios \(\Omega\) and contingencies \(\mathcal C\), a security-constrained stochastic unit-commitment model has the form \[\min_{x\in X_{\mathrm{UC}}}\left\{c^{\mathsf T}x+\sum_{\omega\in\Omega}p_\omega Q(x,\omega)\right\},\qquad Q(x,\omega)=\min_y\{q_\omega^{\mathsf T}y:y\in Y(x,\omega)\}.\] Here \(x\) contains pre-revelation commitment, startup, and shutdown decisions. The recourse set \(Y(x,\omega)\) enforces scenario dispatch, reserves, nodal balance, transmission limits, and corrective feasibility for every required \(c\in\mathcal C\), while preserving the nonanticipative first-stage commitment.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Security-constrained stochastic unit commitment minimizes commitment plus expected recourse cost while requiring network-feasible dispatch and corrective contingency actions in every modeled scenario.
assumptions_latex: \(\Omega\) and \(\mathcal C\) are finite.
\(p_\omega>0\) and \(\sum_{\omega\in\Omega}p_\omega=1\).
First-stage commitments are nonanticipative.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An optimal \(x\) minimizes expected operating cost subject to unit-commitment and scenario-contingency security feasibility.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cited sources support generic two-stage recourse but not the specialized security-constrained stochastic unit-commitment formulation, including reserve, network, contingency, and corrective-feasibility requirements. A directly relevant authoritative source is required.

children.title: Storage-Coupled Stochastic Unit Commitment
children.top_down_role: Commitment coupled to intertemporal storage decisions.

knowledge_statements.title: Storage-Coupled Stochastic Unit Commitment
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-scenario unit commitment with scenario-dependent dispatch and storage operation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For scenarios \(s\in S\) with probabilities \(p_s\), a storage-coupled stochastic unit-commitment model has the form \[\min_{u,y,z}\; C^{\mathrm{com}}(u)+\sum_{s\in S}p_s C_s^{\mathrm{op}}(y_s,z_s).\] Here \(u\) satisfies binary commitment, startup, shutdown, and minimum-time constraints. For every scenario, \(y_s\) satisfies generation limits, ramping, and power balance, while storage variables obey \[e_{t,s}=e_{t-1,s}+\eta_c c_{t,s}-d_{t,s}/\eta_d,\qquad 0\le e_{t,s}\le \bar e.\] Decisions sharing the same observed history are constrained to be equal; first-stage commitments are therefore common across scenarios.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The model jointly chooses nonanticipative generator commitments and scenario-dependent dispatch, charging, discharging, and stored energy while enforcing operating and intertemporal storage constraints.
assumptions_latex: \(S\) is finite and \(p_s>0\) with \(\sum_{s\in S}p_s=1\).
\(0<\eta_c,\eta_d\le 1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed formulation is a stochastic mixed-integer program coupling binary commitment with scenario-dependent storage dynamics.

notation.meaning: charge, discharge, and stored energy in period t and scenario s

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation fits the leaf and is mathematically coherent, but the cited generic integer-first-stage section does not establish the unit-commitment and storage-specific formulation.

children.title: Demand-Side Flexibility Unit-Commitment Family
children.top_down_role: Commitment coupled to discrete or continuous demand-side flexibility.

children.title: Demand-Response Unit Commitment
children.top_down_role: Commitment models incorporating explicit demand-response participation.

knowledge_statements.title: Demand-Response Unit Commitment
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-stage commitment with scenario-dependent demand-response activation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D_{t,s}\) be baseline demand and let \(r_{t,s}^{-},r_{t,s}^{+}\ge0\) denote downward response and rebound. Demand-response unit commitment minimizes \[C^{\mathrm{com}}(u)+\sum_{s\in S}p_s\bigl(C_s^{\mathrm{gen}}(g_s)+C_s^{\mathrm{DR}}(r_s)\bigr)\] subject to commitment logic and, for each \(t,s\), \[\sum_i g_{i,t,s}=D_{t,s}-r_{t,s}^{-}+r_{t,s}^{+},\qquad 0\le r_{t,s}^{-}\le \bar r_t^{-},\qquad 0\le r_{t,s}^{+}\le \bar r_t^{+}.\] Any required rebound or energy-neutrality rule, such as \(\sum_t r_{t,s}^{-}=\sum_t r_{t,s}^{+}\), is imposed scenario-wise, with nonanticipativity on decisions made before uncertainty is observed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Generator commitments are coordinated with bounded, compensated demand reductions and rebounds under each scenario, with response decisions respecting information availability.
assumptions_latex: \(S\) is finite with probabilities \(p_s\).
Demand response is represented as a compensated load displacement over the modeled horizon.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The formulation is a stochastic mixed-integer unit-commitment model whose recourse includes demand-response activation.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation fits demand-response unit commitment, but the cited source does not specifically support the reduction, rebound, and energy-neutrality model.

children.title: Flexible-Load Unit Commitment
children.top_down_role: Commitment models incorporating shiftable, deferrable, or interruptible consumption.

knowledge_statements.title: Flexible-Load Unit Commitment
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Commitment model with scenario-wise rescheduling of energy-constrained loads.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For flexible loads \(j\in J\), let \(\ell_{j,t,s}\) be their scenario-dependent consumption. Flexible-load unit commitment augments the stochastic commitment objective by load-service costs and imposes \[\underline\ell_{j,t}\le \ell_{j,t,s}\le \bar\ell_{j,t},\qquad \sum_{t\in W_j}\ell_{j,t,s}=E_j\] for every \(j,s\), where \(W_j\) is the service window and \(E_j\) the required energy. System balance is \(\sum_i g_{i,t,s}=D_{t,s}^{\mathrm{fix}}+\sum_j\ell_{j,t,s}\). Commitments and all flexible-load decisions made before scenario histories diverge satisfy the corresponding nonanticipativity equalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The formulation schedules fixed-energy flexible loads within service windows while jointly selecting generator commitments and scenario-dependent dispatch.
assumptions_latex: \(S\) and the scheduling horizon are finite.
Each service requirement satisfies \(E_j\in[\sum_{t\in W_j}\underline\ell_{j,t},\sum_{t\in W_j}\bar\ell_{j,t}]\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Feasible recourse preserves every flexible load's required service while allowing its timing to adapt to revealed uncertainty.

notation.meaning: scheduled consumption of flexible load j
allowable service periods for load j

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The fixed-energy service-window representation is coherent and fits the leaf, but its application-specific formulation is unsupported by the cited generic stochastic-programming section.

children.title: Discrete Demand-Side Flexibility
children.top_down_role: Demand-side options represented through activation, acceptance, block, or interruption choices.

knowledge_statements.title: Discrete Demand-Side Flexibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-mode formulation of scenario-dependent demand-side actions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose flexible resource \(j\) has a finite set \(K_j\) of admissible consumption profiles \(a_{jkt}\). Its discrete flexibility condition is represented by binary variables \(z_{jk,s}\) satisfying \[z_{jk,s}\in\{0,1\},\qquad \sum_{k\in K_j}z_{jk,s}=1,\qquad \ell_{j,t,s}=\sum_{k\in K_j}a_{jkt}z_{jk,s}.\] If the mode must be selected before scenarios \(s\) and \(s'\) become distinguishable, nonanticipativity requires \(z_{jk,s}=z_{jk,s'}\). Coupling these conditions with unit-commitment logic and scenario power balances yields a stochastic mixed-integer formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each flexible load selects exactly one admissible discrete profile, with equal selections across scenarios that share the same information history.
assumptions_latex: \(K_j\) is finite and nonempty for every resource \(j\).
Each profile \(a_{jkt}\) is feasible for the resource in isolation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed binary constraints are necessary and sufficient for \(\ell_{j,\cdot,s}\) to equal one profile from the finite family.

notation.meaning: consumption in period t under mode k

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite-profile condition and its content kind fit the leaf, but the cited general discrete-optimization section does not specifically support this demand-side formulation or its nonanticipativity treatment.

children.title: Continuous Demand-Side Flexibility
children.top_down_role: Demand-side options represented through continuously adjustable consumption levels.

knowledge_statements.title: Continuous Demand-Side Flexibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Polyhedral continuous recourse for adjustable electricity consumption.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A continuously flexible load \(j\) in scenario \(s\) is represented by a vector \(\ell_{j,s}\in\mathbb R^{T}\) constrained to a nonempty polyhedron \[\mathcal L_j=\{\ell\in\mathbb R^{T}:A_j\ell\le b_j,\;E_j^{-}\le \mathbf 1^{\mathsf T}\ell\le E_j^{+}\}.\] Thus \(\ell_{j,s}\in\mathcal L_j\), and system balance includes its component \(\ell_{j,t,s}\). For scenarios with identical information through the decision time, the corresponding consumption components are equal. When commitment variables remain binary but \(\ell_{j,s}\) is continuous, demand-side flexibility enters the stochastic unit-commitment model as continuous recourse.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adjustable demand ranges over a polyhedral set encoding power, ramping, timing, and total-energy restrictions, subject to nonanticipativity.
assumptions_latex: \(T<\infty\) and \(\mathcal L_j\ne\varnothing\).
The matrices \(A_j\) and vectors \(b_j\) are deterministic model data.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Membership in \(\mathcal L_j\), together with nonanticipativity, completely specifies the continuous demand-side recourse domain.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The polyhedral continuous-recourse condition fits the leaf, but the cited introductory section does not support the asserted electricity-demand interpretation, including ramping and timing restrictions.

children.title: Unit-Commitment Solution Architectures
children.top_down_role: Application-specific use of monolithic and decomposed SMIP formulations.

children.title: Extensive-Form Unit Commitment
children.top_down_role: Scenario-expanded unit-commitment formulations solved as monolithic MIPs.

knowledge_statements.title: Extensive-Form Unit Commitment
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Monolithic finite-scenario deterministic equivalent of stochastic unit commitment.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\) be a finite scenario set. If \(u_s\) denotes a scenario copy of commitment decisions and \(y_s\) its operating decisions, the extensive form is \[\min_{(u_s,y_s)_{s\in S}}\sum_{s\in S}p_s\bigl(c_s^{\mathsf T}u_s+q_s^{\mathsf T}y_s\bigr)\] subject to \((u_s,y_s)\in X_s\) for every \(s\), \(u_s\) binary where required, and \(H_su_s=H_{s'}u_{s'}\) whenever the selected components are decided under the same scenario history. Solving this single mixed-integer program simultaneously enforces every scenario constraint and all nonanticipativity equalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The extensive form expands every scenario into one mixed-integer model and links scenario copies through explicit nonanticipativity equalities.
assumptions_latex: \(S\) is finite with \(p_s>0\) and \(\sum_s p_s=1\).
Each scenario feasible set \(X_s\) has a mixed-integer linear description.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The monolithic formulation is the deterministic equivalent of the finite-scenario stochastic unit-commitment model.

notation.meaning: unit-commitment and operating constraints under scenario s
selector for decisions subject to nonanticipativity

children.title: Scenario-Decomposed Unit Commitment
children.top_down_role: Scenario coordination through nonanticipativity decomposition.

knowledge_statements.title: Scenario-Decomposed Unit Commitment
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Progressive-hedging-style coordination of scenario unit-commitment subproblems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize multipliers \(w_s^0=0\), choose \(\rho>0\), and solve each scenario subproblem for \(x_s^0\). At iteration \(k\), compute the probability-weighted consensus \(\bar x^k=\sum_{s\in S}p_sx_s^k\), then independently solve \[x_s^{k+1}\in\arg\min_{x\in X_s}\left\{f_s(x)+(w_s^k)^{\mathsf T}x+\frac{\rho}{2}\lVert x-\bar x^k\rVert_2^2\right\}\] and update \(w_s^{k+1}=w_s^k+\rho(x_s^{k+1}-\bar x^{k+1})\). Stop when the prescribed primal nonanticipativity residual and objective-change tolerances hold; return a nonanticipative feasible incumbent obtained directly or by mixed-integer recovery.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Scenario subproblems are solved separately and coordinated by consensus penalties and multiplier updates until nonanticipativity tolerances are met.
assumptions_latex: \(S\) is finite and every scenario subproblem \(X_s\) is nonempty.
\(\rho>0\), and each subproblem is solved to the accuracy required by the stopping rule.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The algorithm decomposes the scenario-expanded model, although integer variables preclude a general global-convergence guarantee without additional assumptions.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the solution-architecture leaf, but no source is supplied for the progressive-hedging iteration, stopping criteria, or the unspecified mixed-integer recovery step.

children.title: Stage-Decomposed Unit Commitment
children.top_down_role: Stagewise value approximation for sequential commitment decisions.

knowledge_statements.title: Stage-Decomposed Unit Commitment
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Backward value approximation and forward commitment decisions on a scenario tree.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For stages \(t=T,\ldots,1\), define the cost-to-go recursion \[V_t(x_{t-1},\xi_t)=\min_{u_t,y_t}\left\{c_t(u_t,y_t,\xi_t)+\mathbb{E}\!\left[V_{t+1}(x_t,\xi_{t+1})\mid\mathcal F_t\right]:(u_t,y_t,x_t)\in X_t(x_{t-1},\xi_t)\right\},\] with \(V_{T+1}=0\) and binary commitment components in \(u_t\). A stage-decomposition method replaces future \(V_{t+1}\) by maintained approximations, performs forward simulations to choose feasible adapted decisions, and uses backward subproblem information to update those approximations. It stops under a stated iteration or bound-gap rule and returns the best feasible policy encountered.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sequential commitment is computed by forward policy simulation and backward refinement of approximate future-cost functions.
assumptions_latex: The horizon and scenario tree are finite.
At stage \(t\), decisions are measurable with respect to \(\mathcal F_t\).
Every visited stage subproblem admits a feasible mixed-integer solution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The procedure decomposes multistage unit commitment by time through approximations of conditional cost-to-go functions.

notation.meaning: state passed from stage t to stage t+1

children.title: Stochastic Infrastructure Design Family
children.top_down_role: Discrete infrastructure decisions followed by uncertain flow, allocation, or service recourse.

children.title: Stochastic Facility Location
children.top_down_role: Facility-opening decisions with uncertain allocation or disruption recourse.

knowledge_statements.title: Stochastic Facility Location
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-stage facility opening with allocation recourse under finite scenarios.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x_i\in\{0,1\}\) indicate whether facility \(i\) is opened before demand is known. A capacitated stochastic facility-location model is \[\min_x\left\{\sum_i f_ix_i+\sum_{s\in S}p_s Q_s(x):x\in X\cap\{0,1\}^{I}\right\},\] where \[Q_s(x)=\min_{y_s,r_s}\left\{\sum_{i,j}c_{ij,s}y_{ij,s}+\sum_j\pi_{j,s}r_{j,s}:\sum_i y_{ij,s}+r_{j,s}=d_{j,s},\;\sum_jy_{ij,s}\le K_{i,s}x_i,\;y_s,r_s\ge0\right\}.\] Scenario-dependent capacities \(K_{i,s}\) may represent disruptions, and unmet-demand variables \(r_{j,s}\) provide penalized recourse.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Facilities are opened before uncertainty, then customers are allocated under scenario demand and capacity, with optional penalized unmet demand.
assumptions_latex: \(S\), the facility set, and the customer set are finite.
\(p_s>0\), \(f_i\ge0\), and recourse penalties \(\pi_{j,s}\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The model is a two-stage stochastic mixed-integer program with binary facility openings and continuous allocation recourse.

notation.meaning: scenario allocation from facility i to customer j
optimal operating cost in scenario s

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The two-stage facility-location representation is coherent and fits the leaf, but neither cited general stochastic-programming section specifically supports the facility-allocation and disruption formulation.

children.title: Stochastic Capacity Expansion
children.top_down_role: Discrete capacity investments coupled to uncertain future operations.

knowledge_statements.title: Stochastic Capacity Expansion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Discrete capacity investment followed by scenario-dependent operation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x_i\in\mathbb Z_+\) count capacity modules installed before uncertainty is observed, each supplying \(k_i\) units. A two-stage capacity-expansion model is \[\min_{x\in X\cap\mathbb Z_+^I}\left\{c^{\mathsf T}x+\sum_{s\in S}p_sQ_s(x)\right\},\] where \[Q_s(x)=\min_{y_s,r_s}\left\{q_s^{\mathsf T}y_s+\pi_s^{\mathsf T}r_s:W_sy_s+r_s\ge d_s,\;0\le y_{i,s}\le \bar K_i+k_ix_i,\;r_s\ge0\right\}.\] The investment vector is common to all scenarios, whereas operation and shortage recourse adapt after the scenario is revealed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Discrete capacity modules are selected before uncertainty and coupled to scenario-dependent operation and penalized shortage recourse.
assumptions_latex: \(S\) and \(I\) are finite, with \(p_s>0\) and \(\sum_sp_s=1\).
Costs and capacities are finite, and \(r_s\) ensures complete recourse.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The formulation is a stochastic mixed-integer capacity-expansion model with integer investment and continuous operating recourse.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The capacity-expansion representation is mathematically coherent, but the generic cited sections do not specifically support the modular investment and operating-recourse formulation.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Multistage stochastic capacity-expansion model
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded representation of adaptive power-generation capacity planning under uncertain demand and costs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For stages \(t=1,\ldots,H\), technologies \(i=1,\ldots,n\), and load modes \(j=1,\ldots,m\), the capacity-expansion problem is represented by
\[
\min_{\mathbf x,\mathbf w,\mathbf y\ge 0}\;\mathbb E_{\boldsymbol\xi}\!\left[\sum_{t=1}^{H}\left(\sum_{i=1}^{n}\mathbf r_i^t\mathbf w_i^t+\sum_{i=1}^{n}\sum_{j=1}^{m}\mathbf q_i^t\tau_j^t\mathbf y_{ij}^t\right)\right]
\]
subject, for every applicable \(i,j,t\), to
\[
\mathbf w_i^t=\mathbf w_i^{t-1}+\mathbf x_i^t-\mathbf x_i^{t-L_i},\qquad
\sum_{i=1}^{n}\mathbf y_{ij}^t=\mathbf d_j^t,
\]
\[
\sum_{j=1}^{m}\mathbf y_{ij}^t\le a_i\bigl(g_i^t+\mathbf w_i^{t-\Delta_i}\bigr),
\]
where \(\mathbf x_i^s=0\) for \(s\le0\). Each stage-\(t\) decision is measurable with respect to information available through stage \(t\) and cannot depend on future realizations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The model minimizes expected capacity and operating costs while accounting for capacity additions and retirements, construction delays, demand satisfaction, and technology availability. Decisions adapt to information observed by their stage but cannot anticipate future uncertainty.
assumptions_latex: t=1,\ldots,H,\quad i=1,\ldots,n,\quad j=1,\ldots,m
\mathbf x,\mathbf w,\mathbf y\ge0
\mathbf x_i^s=0\quad\text{for }s\le0
(\mathbf x^t,\mathbf w^t,\mathbf y^t)\text{ is measurable with respect to stage-}t\text{ information}
\text{The stochastic constraints hold for the realized data.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{This is a nonanticipative multistage stochastic capacity-expansion formulation.}

source_evidence.locator: Introduction and Examples / 1.3. Capacity Expansion / Definition 1.3-extra-1

source_refs.locator: Introduction and Examples / 1.3. Capacity Expansion / Definition 1.3-extra-1

knowledge_statements.title: Multistage stochastic capacity-expansion model

source_witnesses.locator: Introduction and Examples / 1.3. Capacity Expansion / Definition 1.3-extra-1

children.title: Stochastic Supply-Chain Network Design
children.top_down_role: Network configuration with uncertain sourcing, production, and distribution recourse.

knowledge_statements.title: Stochastic Supply-Chain Network Design
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-stage network configuration with sourcing, production, and shipment recourse.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x_a\in\{0,1\}\) select candidate facilities or arcs \(a\in A\). A stochastic supply-chain design model is \[\min_{x\in X\cap\{0,1\}^{A}}\left\{f^{\mathsf T}x+\sum_{s\in S}p_sQ_s(x)\right\},\] where \(Q_s(x)\) minimizes scenario sourcing, production, inventory, transportation, and shortage costs subject to node balances and constraints \[0\le y_{a,s}\le U_{a,s}x_a\qquad(a\in A).\] The design is fixed before uncertainty, while flows and other operating variables adapt by scenario. In a multistage extension, decisions at scenario-tree nodes additionally satisfy history-based nonanticipativity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Binary network choices precede uncertainty; scenario recourse routes supply, production, inventory, and distribution through the installed capacities.
assumptions_latex: \(S\) and the candidate network are finite.
Each recourse model has linear balance and capacity constraints and admits a feasible penalized-shortage solution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The model couples discrete supply-chain topology decisions to scenario-dependent multicommodity operating recourse.

notation.meaning: binary installation decision for facility or arc a
optimal supply-chain operating cost in scenario s

children.title: Stochastic Network Interdiction
children.top_down_role: Discrete interdiction decisions interacting with uncertain network response.

knowledge_statements.title: Stochastic Network Interdiction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Attacker-first interdiction with scenario-dependent optimal network response.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x_a\in\{0,1\}\) indicate interdiction of arc \(a\), and let \(B\) be the attack budget. An attacker-first stochastic interdiction model can be written \[\max_{x\in\{0,1\}^{A}}\left\{\sum_{s\in S}p_sQ_s(x):\sum_{a\in A}b_ax_a\le B\right\},\] where \[Q_s(x)=\min_{y_s}\left\{c_s^{\mathsf T}y_s:N_sy_s=d_s,\;0\le y_{a,s}\le u_{a,s}(1-x_a)\right\}.\] The common binary vector \(x\) is chosen before scenario revelation; the defender's feasible flow \(y_s\) adapts afterward. Alternative response objectives replace \(Q_s\) without changing the information structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A budgeted attacker disables arcs before uncertainty, and each scenario then produces an optimal feasible network response on the surviving capacities.
assumptions_latex: \(S\) and \(A\) are finite, and \(b_a>0\).
Each defender problem is feasible, or infeasibility is assigned an explicitly modeled penalty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The formulation is a stochastic bilevel mixed-integer model with here-and-now interdiction and scenario-dependent network response.

notation.meaning: binary interdiction decision for arc a
optimal defender value in scenario s

children.title: Stochastic Production-Inventory System Family
children.top_down_role: Discrete setup, ordering, or production decisions with uncertain demand and inventory recourse.

children.title: Stochastic Lot Sizing
children.top_down_role: Setup and production decisions linked by uncertain demand and inventory states.

knowledge_statements.title: Stochastic Lot Sizing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-scenario multistage formulation with setup, production, inventory, backlog, and nonanticipativity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For periods \(t\in T\) and scenarios \(\omega\in\Omega\), a stochastic lot-sizing model is
\[
\min \sum_{\omega\in\Omega}p_\omega\sum_{t\in T}(f_ty_{t\omega}+c_tx_{t\omega}+h_tI_{t\omega}+b_tB_{t\omega})
\]
subject to \(I_{t-1,\omega}-B_{t-1,\omega}+x_{t\omega}=d_{t\omega}+I_{t\omega}-B_{t\omega}\), \(0\le x_{t\omega}\le M_ty_{t\omega}\), \(y_{t\omega}\in\{0,1\}\), and \(I_{t\omega},B_{t\omega}\ge0\). Decisions at scenario-tree nodes having identical information through period \(t\) are equal. Thus setups and production are adapted to observed demand, while inventory balance holds scenario-wise.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimize expected setup, production, holding, and backlog costs while enforcing scenario-wise inventory balance, setup-linked production, and nonanticipative decisions.
assumptions_latex: \(T\) and \(\Omega\) are finite, with \(p_\omega>0\) and \(\sum_{\omega}p_\omega=1\).
\(M_t\) is a valid production upper bound for period \(t\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min \mathbb E[\text{setup cost}+\text{production cost}+\text{inventory cost}+\text{backlog cost}]\) subject to adapted lot-sizing decisions.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation fits the leaf, but the cited generic two-stage stochastic-programming section does not specifically support this multistage lot-sizing formulation, its scenario-wise inventory equations, or its nonanticipativity structure. An application-specific source with a precise model locator is required.

children.title: Stochastic Fixed-Charge Production Planning
children.top_down_role: Production activation and continuous output under uncertainty.

knowledge_statements.title: Stochastic Fixed-Charge Production Planning
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-stage finite-scenario production model with first-stage activation and scenario-dependent output.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(i\in I\) index production resources and \(\omega\in\Omega\) scenarios. A two-stage fixed-charge production model is
\[
\min_{y\in\{0,1\}^{I}}\left\{\sum_{i\in I}f_i y_i+\sum_{\omega\in\Omega}p_\omega Q(y,\omega)\right\},
\]
where
\[
Q(y,\omega)=\min_{x_\omega,s_\omega\ge0}\left\{\sum_i c_{i\omega}x_{i\omega}+q_\omega^{\mathsf T}s_\omega: A_\omega x_\omega+s_\omega\ge d_\omega,\ 0\le x_{i\omega}\le U_i y_i\right\}.
\]
The binary vector \(y\) is chosen before the scenario is known; production and shortage or auxiliary recourse variables may respond afterward.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose capacity activations before uncertainty, then minimize expected scenario-dependent production and recourse cost subject to activation-linked output limits.
assumptions_latex: \(\Omega\) is finite and \(p_\omega\ge0\) with \(\sum_\omega p_\omega=1\).
\(U_i<\infty\) is a valid activated-output bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min_{y}\{f^{\mathsf T}y+\mathbb E[Q(y,\omega)]\}\) represents activation followed by production recourse.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The content kind and two-stage activation/production interpretation fit the leaf. The citation supports a generic two-stage template, however, not this fixed-charge production model or its particular recourse constraints; an application-specific source is required.

children.title: Stochastic Batch Sizing
children.top_down_role: Multistage batch and setup decisions under uncertain requirements.

knowledge_statements.title: Stochastic Batch Sizing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multistage batch formulation with integer batch counts, setup indicators, inventory balance, and nonanticipativity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For each period \(t\) and scenario \(\omega\), let production equal an integer number of fixed-size batches: \(x_{t\omega}=q_tk_{t\omega}\), where \(k_{t\omega}\in\mathbb Z_+\). A stochastic batch-sizing model minimizes
\[
\sum_{\omega\in\Omega}p_\omega\sum_{t\in T}(f_ty_{t\omega}+g_tk_{t\omega}+h_tI_{t\omega}+b_tB_{t\omega})
\]
subject to \(I_{t-1,\omega}-B_{t-1,\omega}+q_tk_{t\omega}=d_{t\omega}+I_{t\omega}-B_{t\omega}\), \(0\le k_{t\omega}\le K_ty_{t\omega}\), and nonanticipativity for scenarios sharing the same information history. Here \(y_{t\omega}\in\{0,1\}\) and inventories and backlogs are nonnegative.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Select adapted setups and integer batch counts that balance uncertain demand while minimizing expected setup, batch, inventory, and backlog costs.
assumptions_latex: \(q_t>0\) is the fixed batch quantity and \(K_t\in\mathbb Z_+\) is a valid batch-count bound.
\(T\) and \(\Omega\) are finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_{t\omega}\in q_t\mathbb Z_+\) and all scenario decisions satisfy inventory balance and nonanticipativity.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation belongs in this leaf, but the displayed objective lacks an explicit minimization operator and the cited stochastic-dynamic-programming section does not establish this batch-sizing formulation. A model-specific source is needed before deciding the exact corrected formulation.

children.title: Stochastic Multi-Echelon Inventory Design
children.top_down_role: Discrete stocking or network choices coupled to uncertain multi-level flows.

knowledge_statements.title: Stochastic Multi-Echelon Inventory Design
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-stage network design with discrete stocking choices and scenario-dependent multi-echelon flows.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(N\) be inventory locations, \(A\) shipment arcs, and \(\Omega\) demand scenarios. A two-stage design template is
\[
\min_{y\in Y}\left\{\sum_{i\in N}F_i y_i+\sum_{\omega\in\Omega}p_\omega Q(y,\omega)\right\},
\]
where \(Y\subseteq\mathbb Z_+^{N}\) encodes stocking or capacity choices and \(Q(y,\omega)\) minimizes holding, shipment, and shortage costs over nonnegative scenario flows and inventories. Its constraints impose flow conservation at every location and echelon, satisfy realized customer demand with deliveries and shortage, and enforce inventory or throughput capacities \(I_{i\omega}\le C_i y_i\). Design choices are scenario-independent; operational flows are scenario-dependent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose discrete stocking capacities before demand is known, then route and hold inventory across echelons in each scenario at minimum expected cost.
assumptions_latex: \(N\), \(A\), and \(\Omega\) are finite.
\(C_i\ge0\) is a valid capacity per installed stocking unit.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min_{y\in Y}\{F^{\mathsf T}y+\mathbb E[Q(y,\omega)]\}\) couples discrete network design with feasible scenario flows.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation role fits, but the recourse variables, echelon structure, flow-conservation equations, and demand constraints are only described informally. The generic two-stage citation does not support these application-specific details, so a multi-echelon inventory-design source is required.

children.title: Stochastic Mobility-Service System Family
children.top_down_role: Routing, fleet, assignment, and service decisions with uncertain demand or availability.

children.title: Stochastic Vehicle Routing
children.top_down_role: Discrete routes with recourse for uncertain customers, demands, or travel conditions.

knowledge_statements.title: Stochastic Vehicle Routing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-stage routing template with planned arcs and scenario-dependent service or recovery recourse.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
On a directed graph \(G=(V,A)\), let \(x_{ak}\in\{0,1\}\) indicate whether vehicle \(k\) plans to traverse arc \(a\). A two-stage stochastic routing model is
\[
\min_{x\in X}\left\{\sum_{a,k}c_{ak}x_{ak}+\sum_{\omega\in\Omega}p_\omega Q(x,\omega)\right\},
\]
where \(X\) imposes depot, flow-conservation, and planned-route constraints. For realized customers, demands, or travel conditions in scenario \(\omega\), \(Q(x,\omega)\) is the minimum cost of feasible recourse routes, missed-service variables, reloads, or rerouting actions, subject to vehicle capacities and scenario service requirements. The planned route is common to all scenarios.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Select planned vehicle routes before uncertainty, then use scenario-dependent rerouting or service recourse while respecting flow, service, and vehicle-capacity constraints.
assumptions_latex: \(G\), the vehicle set, and \(\Omega\) are finite.
\(p_\omega\ge0\) and \(\sum_\omega p_\omega=1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min_{x\in X}\{c^{\mathsf T}x+\mathbb E[Q(x,\omega)]\}\) represents routing with stochastic recourse.

notation.meaning: planned use of arc by vehicle

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The content kind fits the routing leaf, but the recourse definition combines several distinct variants—uncertain customers, demands, travel conditions, reloads, missed service, and rerouting—without one explicit feasible model. The generic two-stage source cannot determine which formulation and hypotheses are intended.

children.title: Stochastic Fleet Assignment
children.top_down_role: Fleet deployment with uncertain operations and recovery actions.

knowledge_statements.title: Stochastic Fleet Assignment
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-stage assignment of fleet types to services with scenario-dependent recovery actions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(L\) index scheduled legs and \(K\) fleet types. With \(x_{lk}\in\{0,1\}\) denoting the planned assignment of type \(k\) to leg \(l\), a stochastic fleet-assignment template is
\[
\min_{x\in X}\left\{\sum_{l,k}c_{lk}x_{lk}+\sum_{\omega\in\Omega}p_\omega Q(x,\omega)\right\}.
\]
The set \(X\) enforces one assignment per operated leg, fleet availability, and connection balance. Given scenario \(\omega\), \(Q(x,\omega)\) minimizes recovery, reassignment, cancellation, delay, and unmet-capacity costs subject to realized vehicle availability and operating conditions. Planned assignments are scenario-independent, whereas recovery decisions depend on observed disruption information.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Assign fleet types to scheduled legs before disruptions, then recover through scenario-dependent swaps, cancellations, or delays at minimum expected total cost.
assumptions_latex: \(L\), \(K\), and \(\Omega\) are finite.
\(X\) contains only assignments satisfying nominal fleet conservation and availability.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min_{x\in X}\{c^{\mathsf T}x+\mathbb E[Q(x,\omega)]\}\) couples fleet deployment with disruption recovery.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation fits stochastic fleet assignment, but the recovery problem and disruption information structure are not mathematically specified. The cited generic two-stage section does not support the fleet-balance, recovery, cancellation, and delay claims; an application-specific source is required.

children.title: Stochastic Service Network Design
children.top_down_role: Scheduled service choices coupled to uncertain shipment or passenger flows.

knowledge_statements.title: Stochastic Service Network Design
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-stage scheduled-service design with scenario-dependent commodity or passenger flows.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(A\) be candidate service arcs and \(K\) commodities. With \(y_a\in\mathbb Z_+\) denoting the number of scheduled services on arc \(a\), a stochastic service-network design model is
\[
\min_{y\in Y}\left\{\sum_{a\in A}F_a y_a+\sum_{\omega\in\Omega}p_\omega Q(y,\omega)\right\}.
\]
For scenario \(\omega\), \(Q(y,\omega)\) minimizes routing, delay, and unmet-demand costs over flows \(z_{ak\omega}\ge0\), subject to commodity flow conservation and \(\sum_k z_{ak\omega}\le u_a y_a\). The design \(y\) is fixed before demands are observed; flows and unmet-demand recourse adapt to the scenario.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Schedule service capacity before demand is observed, then route scenario-dependent shipments or passengers subject to conservation and installed arc capacities.
assumptions_latex: \(A\), \(K\), and \(\Omega\) are finite.
\(u_a\ge0\) is the capacity supplied by one service on arc \(a\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min_{y\in Y}\{F^{\mathsf T}y+\mathbb E[Q(y,\omega)]\}\) represents scheduled-service design with flow recourse.

notation.meaning: number of scheduled services on arc

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation and terminal container are compatible. Nevertheless, the recourse objective, unmet-demand variables, demand equations, and feasible design set are not fully specified, and the generic two-stage citation does not substantiate this service-network formulation.

children.title: Stochastic Server Location
children.top_down_role: Discrete service-location decisions with uncertain demand and integer recourse.

knowledge_statements.title: Stochastic Server Location
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-stage capacitated server-location model with integer deployment and demand-dependent assignment recourse.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(I\) be candidate server sites and \(J\) demand zones. With \(y_i\in\mathbb Z_+\) servers installed at site \(i\), a stochastic server-location model is
\[
\min_{y\in Y}\left\{\sum_{i\in I}F_i y_i+\sum_{\omega\in\Omega}p_\omega Q(y,\omega)\right\},
\]
where \(Q(y,\omega)\) minimizes assignment, waiting, overflow, or unmet-demand costs over integer assignments \(z_{ij\omega}\ge0\). Recourse satisfies \(\sum_i z_{ij\omega}+s_{j\omega}=d_{j\omega}\) and \(\sum_j z_{ij\omega}\le C_i y_i\), with \(s_{j\omega}\ge0\). Locations are chosen before demand; assignments and shortages respond afterward.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Install integer server capacity before demand is known, then assign realized demand to servers or shortage recourse under installed capacities.
assumptions_latex: \(I\), \(J\), and \(\Omega\) are finite.
\(C_i\in\mathbb Z_+\) is the service capacity of one server at site \(i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min_{y\in Y}\{F^{\mathsf T}y+\mathbb E[Q(y,\omega)]\}\) couples server location with integer assignment recourse.

notation.meaning: scenario demand assigned from zone to site

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation fits the leaf, but integer recourse is asserted while the displayed domain only states nonnegativity for the assignment variables. The generic two-stage source does not resolve the intended integer server-location model, assignment units, or capacity interpretation.

children.title: Stochastic Scheduling-Staffing System Family
children.top_down_role: Sequencing, assignment, and staffing decisions with combinatorial recourse.

children.title: Stochastic Project Scheduling
children.top_down_role: Activity and resource plans under uncertain durations or disruptions.

knowledge_statements.title: Stochastic Project Scheduling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scenario-based resource-constrained scheduling with nonanticipative activity decisions and uncertain durations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(J\) be activities with precedence arcs \(P\), and let \(S_{j\omega}\) be the start time of activity \(j\) under scenario \(\omega\). A stochastic project-scheduling model minimizes \(\sum_{\omega\in\Omega}p_\omega C_\omega\) plus optional resource or disruption costs, subject to
\[
S_{j\omega}\ge S_{i\omega}+D_{i\omega}\quad((i,j)\in P),\qquad C_\omega\ge S_{j\omega}+D_{j\omega}\quad(j\in J),
\]
resource-capacity constraints, and integrality conditions required by the scheduling representation. Start or allocation decisions made before two scenarios become distinguishable must be equal. Consequently, the schedule is adapted only to durations or disruptions already observed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimize expected project completion and resource costs while enforcing scenario-wise precedence, capacity, integrality, and nonanticipativity constraints.
assumptions_latex: \(J\), \(P\), and \(\Omega\) are finite.
\(D_{j\omega}\ge0\) is revealed according to the specified scenario-tree filtration.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S_{j\omega}\) forms a nonanticipative, resource-feasible schedule in every scenario.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation fits stochastic project scheduling, but resource constraints and the decision/revelation timing needed to define nonanticipative start decisions are omitted. The cited general stochastic-dynamic-programming section does not support this particular scheduling formulation.

children.title: Stochastic Workforce Scheduling
children.top_down_role: Staffing and shift decisions with demand-dependent assignment recourse.

knowledge_statements.title: Stochastic Workforce Scheduling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-stage shift selection with scenario-dependent worker assignment, shortage, and overtime recourse.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(S\) be candidate shifts, \(J\) service periods, and \(a_{sj}\in\{0,1\}\) indicate whether shift \(s\) covers period \(j\). A stochastic workforce-scheduling model is
\[
\min_{x\in X}\left\{\sum_{s\in S}c_sx_s+\sum_{\omega\in\Omega}p_\omega Q(x,\omega)\right\},
\]
where \(x_s\in\mathbb Z_+\) is scheduled staffing and \(X\) encodes labor rules. For each scenario, \(Q(x,\omega)\) minimizes assignment, overtime, and shortage costs subject to \(\sum_s a_{sj}z_{sj\omega}+o_{j\omega}+u_{j\omega}\ge d_{j\omega}\) and \(0\le z_{sj\omega}\le x_s\). Staffing is fixed before demand; assignments and recourse adapt afterward.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose shift staffing before demand, then assign available workers and use overtime or shortage recourse in each demand scenario.
assumptions_latex: \(S\), \(J\), and \(\Omega\) are finite.
\(X\subseteq\mathbb Z_+^{S}\) represents the applicable labor and shift rules.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min_{x\in X}\{c^{\mathsf T}x+\mathbb E[Q(x,\omega)]\}\) represents staffing with demand-dependent assignment recourse.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation fits workforce scheduling, but the meanings and domains of overtime and shortage variables, worker reuse across periods, and the complete recourse objective are unspecified. The generic two-stage citation does not validate these workforce-specific constraints.

children.title: Stochastic Healthcare Scheduling
children.top_down_role: Surgical, appointment, or treatment scheduling under uncertain durations and arrivals.

knowledge_statements.title: Stochastic Healthcare Scheduling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-stage appointment or treatment scheduling with duration, arrival, overtime, and waiting uncertainty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(P\) index patients or procedures and \(R\) clinical resources. A stochastic healthcare-scheduling model chooses a feasible baseline schedule \(x\in X\) before uncertain arrivals and durations are observed:
\[
\min_{x\in X}\left\{c^{\mathsf T}x+\sum_{\omega\in\Omega}p_\omega Q(x,\omega)\right\}.
\]
For each scenario \(\omega\), \(Q(x,\omega)\) minimizes waiting, overtime, cancellation, diversion, and rescheduling costs over operational variables satisfying realized temporal precedence, patient-resource assignment, and resource-capacity constraints. Baseline appointment times, reserved blocks, or sequencing decisions are scenario-independent; operational adjustments may depend only on information observed by their decision time.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose a baseline healthcare schedule, then minimize expected waiting, overtime, cancellation, and recovery costs through information-adapted operational recourse.
assumptions_latex: \(P\), \(R\), and \(\Omega\) are finite.
\(X\) enforces all deterministic eligibility, sequencing, and reservation restrictions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min_{x\in X}\{c^{\mathsf T}x+\mathbb E[Q(x,\omega)]\}\) represents baseline scheduling with clinical recourse.

notation.meaning: baseline appointment, block, or sequence decisions

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation fits the healthcare-scheduling leaf, but it blends appointment, block, treatment, sequencing, arrival, and duration variants while leaving the recourse constraints abstract. The generic two-stage citation cannot support a definite mathematical formulation.

children.title: Staffing-Schedule Coupling
children.top_down_role: Coupled staffing-level and operational assignment decisions under uncertainty.

children.title: Staffing-Level Decisions
children.top_down_role: Workforce capacity, skill-mix, shift-count, or staffing-pool choices under uncertainty.

knowledge_statements.title: Staffing-Level Decisions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-stage staffing component of a coupled stochastic staffing-and-scheduling model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given resource types \(r\in R\) and planning units \(t\in T\), staffing-level decisions are integer variables \(x_{rt}\in\mathbb Z_+\) chosen before operational uncertainty is observed. They satisfy a deterministic feasible set \(X\), which may include hiring, availability, budget, skill-mix, and interperiod balance constraints. In a two-stage model their cost and downstream effect have the form
\[
\min_{x\in X}\left\{\sum_{r,t}c_{rt}x_{rt}+\sum_{\omega\in\Omega}p_\omega Q(x,\omega)\right\},
\]
where \(Q(x,\omega)\) schedules or assigns the installed staff under scenario \(\omega\), and no recourse assignment may use more staff than the corresponding level \(x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Staffing-level decisions are pre-uncertainty integer choices of available personnel by type and period that bound scenario-dependent schedules and assignments.
assumptions_latex: \(R\), \(T\), and \(\Omega\) are finite.
\(X\subseteq\mathbb Z_+^{R\times T}\) is the deterministic staffing-feasibility set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\in X\) is scenario-independent and supplies upper bounds or capacities to every recourse schedule.

notation.meaning: staff level of type r in planning unit t

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Definition is an appropriate role for this terminal decision-component leaf, and the pre-uncertainty interpretation is plausible. However, the generic two-stage source does not specifically establish the staffing-level definition or the asserted coupling between each staffing level and all recourse assignments; a staffing-and-scheduling source is required.

children.title: Operational Scheduling Decisions
children.top_down_role: Assignment, sequencing, roster, or shift-placement choices within available staffing capacity.

knowledge_statements.title: Operational Scheduling Decisions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-scenario, staffing-constrained operational schedules chosen as recourse after uncertainty is observed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I\), \(T\), \(K\), and \(\Omega\) be finite sets of activities, periods, staff types, and scenarios. For each \(i\in I\) and \(\omega\in\Omega\), let \(T_i^\omega\subseteq T\) be a nonempty set of allowable periods. Given requirements \(a_{ki}\ge 0\) and first-stage staffing capacities \(u_{kt}\in\mathbb Z_+\), an operational scheduling decision in scenario \(\omega\) is a vector \(x^\omega\in\{0,1\}^{I\times T}\). It is feasible when \[x_{it}^\omega=0\quad(i\in I,\ t\notin T_i^\omega),\qquad \sum_{t\in T_i^\omega}x_{it}^\omega=1\quad(i\in I),\] and \[\sum_{i\in I}a_{ki}x_{it}^\omega\le u_{kt}\quad(k\in K,\ t\in T).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In each scenario, an operational schedule assigns every activity to exactly one allowable period and keeps the simultaneous use of each staff type within the staffing capacity fixed before uncertainty is observed.
assumptions_latex: The sets \(I\), \(T\), \(K\), and \(\Omega\) are finite.
Every allowable-period set \(T_i^\omega\) is nonempty.
The capacities \(u_{kt}\in\mathbb Z_+\) are fixed before the scenario is observed, and staff consumption is additive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For each \(\omega\in\Omega\), the vector \(x^\omega\) is a feasible operational scheduling decision exactly when it satisfies the displayed allowable-period, assignment, and staffing-capacity constraints.

notation.meaning: binary assignment of activity i to period t in scenario omega
first-stage capacity of staff type k in period t
units of staff type k consumed by activity i
allowable periods for activity i in scenario omega

children.title: Staffing–Schedule Coupling
children.top_down_role: Structural links between workforce-capacity choices and operational schedule feasibility.

knowledge_statements.title: Staffing–Schedule Coupling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-scenario capacity linkage between here-and-now staffing and wait-and-see scheduling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I\), \(T\), \(K\), and \(\Omega\) be finite sets of activities, periods, staff types, and scenarios. Let \(u_{kt}\in\mathbb Z_+\) be the scenario-independent first-stage staffing of type \(k\in K\) in period \(t\in T\), and let \(x_{it}^\omega\in\{0,1\}\) indicate whether activity \(i\in I\) is assigned to period \(t\) in scenario \(\omega\in\Omega\). If activity \(i\) consumes \(a_{ki}\ge 0\) units of staff type \(k\), staffing and scheduling satisfy the coupling conditions \[\sum_{i\in I}a_{ki}x_{it}^\omega\le u_{kt}\qquad(k\in K,\ t\in T,\ \omega\in\Omega).\] Because \(u\) is common to all scenarios, every scenario-dependent schedule must be supported by the same here-and-now staffing plan. Replacing \(u\) with independently chosen variables \(u^\omega\) would instead model scenario-dependent staffing and would violate the stated first-stage information restriction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every scenario-dependent schedule must stay within the capacities supplied by the same staffing plan chosen before the scenario is known; independently choosing staffing by scenario would change staffing into a wait-and-see decision.
assumptions_latex: The sets \(I\), \(T\), \(K\), and \(\Omega\) are finite.
The staffing variables \(u_{kt}\) are scenario-independent, nonnegative, integer-valued first-stage decisions.
The scheduling variables may depend on the realized scenario, and staff consumption is additive across simultaneously scheduled activities.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The inequalities \(\sum_{i\in I}a_{ki}x_{it}^\omega\le u_{kt}\) are the staffing–schedule coupling conditions linking first-stage capacity to scenario-dependent operational recourse.

notation.meaning: number of staff of type k assigned to period t before uncertainty is observed
scenario-dependent assignment of activity i to period t
units of staff type k consumed by activity i

children.title: Recourse Coordination Regimes
children.top_down_role: Conditions governing reassignment, overtime, reserve staffing, or schedule repair after uncertainty realization.

knowledge_statements.title: Recourse Coordination Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-scenario representation of static, information-adapted, fully revealed, and anticipative-relaxation operational decisions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Omega\) be a finite scenario set with probabilities \(p_\omega>0\) satisfying \(\sum_{\omega\in\Omega}p_\omega=1\). Let \(u\) be a first-stage staffing decision, and suppose that \(Y(u,\omega)\subseteq\mathcal Y\) is the feasible recourse set in scenario \(\omega\), where the common space \(\mathcal Y\) makes cross-scenario equality meaningful. Let \(\mathcal P\) be the partition of \(\Omega\) induced by the information available when the operational decision is made. The coordinated recourse value is \[Q_{\mathcal P}(u)=\min_{(y^\omega)_{\omega\in\Omega}}\left\{\sum_{\omega\in\Omega}p_\omega q_\omega(y^\omega): y^\omega\in Y(u,\omega),\ y^\omega=y^{\omega'}\text{ whenever }\omega,\omega'\text{ lie in the same cell of }\mathcal P\right\}.\] The one-cell partition \(\mathcal P=\{\Omega\}\) gives a fully static operational decision, while the singleton partition gives fully revealed scenario-wise recourse and permits decomposition into independent scenario minima. Dropping equalities required by the actual information partition produces an anticipative relaxation because decisions may then depend on information unavailable at the decision time.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A recourse regime is determined by the scenario distinctions available when operational decisions are made: decisions must agree within each indistinguishable scenario group, with one group giving a static decision and singleton groups giving fully revealed scenario-wise recourse.
assumptions_latex: The set \(\Omega\) is finite, with \(p_\omega>0\) and \(\sum_{\omega[0muild\Omega}p_\omega=1\).
The staffing vector \(u\) is chosen before the scenario is observed.
Each feasible recourse set \(Y(u,\omega)\) is contained in a common decision space \(\mathcal Y\), and each cost function \(q_\omega:\mathcal Y\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) is specified.
The partition \(\mathcal P\) represents exactly the scenario information available at the operational decision time.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The coordination regime is determined by the information partition \(\mathcal P\) and its associated nonanticipativity equalities on the family \((y^\omega)_{\omega\in\Omega}\).

notation.meaning: operational recourse decision associated with scenario omega
feasible recourse set after staffing u in scenario omega
partition of scenarios induced by information available at the operational decision time
